question: How do Southwest Airlines' (LUV) recent strategic shifts—including seating policy overhauls and network optimization—address the structural underperformance and operational fragility highlighted by Elliott Investment Management's activist campaign and the 2022-2023 technical failures?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-04-23

**Research question**
How do Southwest Airlines' (LUV) recent strategic shifts—including seating policy overhauls and network optimization—address the structural underperformance and operational fragility highlighted by Elliott Investment Management's activist campaign and the 2022-2023 technical failures?

## Answer

As of 2025-04-23, Southwest has a credible plan to improve margins, but it has not shown that it can close the gap alleged by Elliott Investment Management or recover more reliably from a major disruption. Elliott took a $1.9 billion position in June 2024. The clearest evidence for its critique is Southwest’s reported $465 million annual profit on record revenue of $27.5 billion: the issue is how much revenue Southwest keeps, not simply how much it sells. Those results neither quantify a margin gap against peers nor measure the benefit of the new policies. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1281385492) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250414114607/https://www.dallasnews.com/business/airlines/2025/02/07/two-more-southwest-airlines-board-members-step-down-completing-elliott-makeover/#:~:text=Last%20month%2C%20Southwest%20Airlines%20veteran%20executives%20Tammy%20Romo%2C%20chief,McAllen%2C%20Texas.%20He%20is%20a%20University%20of%20Washington%20graduate.)

## Evidence

Assigned seating addresses the revenue problem directly: Southwest can charge passengers who value a particular seat or extra legroom without raising the fare for everyone. Melius Research saw a $1.5 billion to 1.8 billion opportunity in seat assignments and premium options. That is an analyst estimate, not a Southwest profit target or realized earnings. Open seating was still in place, with the transition scheduled for 2026. The relevant gain is what customers pay for the new options less the revenue displaced and the cost of delivering them. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250414114607/https://www.dallasnews.com/business/airlines/2024/09/10/southwest-airlines-caves-activist-investor-pressure-shakes-up-board/#:~:text=The%20changes%20came%20as%20Southwest%20leaders%2C%20including%20Kelly%2C%20met,the%20latest%20airlines%20news%2C%20delivered%20straight%20to%20your%20inbox.) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250317113716/https://www.visaverge.com/news/southwest-airlines-criticized-for-dropping-free-checked-bags-policy/#:~:text=Perhaps%20the%20most%20controversial%20among%20these%20changes%E2%80%94beyond%20the%20baggage,to%20Southwest%20is%20being%20tested%20in%20an%20unprecedented%20way.) [5](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1286766291) [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20250414114607/https://www.dallasnews.com/business/airlines/2024/09/10/southwest-airlines-caves-activist-investor-pressure-shakes-up-board/#:~:text=Elliott%20had%20previously%20disclosed%20it%20achieved%2010%25%20common%20shares,be%20lost%20as%20they%20make%20changes%20to%20%2B50-year-old%20policies%3F%E2%80%9D)

Checked-bag fees separate the price of travel from the price of a service that once distinguished Southwest. The March announcement superseded the earlier plan to retain free bags: fees for most passengers were to start May 28, 2025, with exemptions including A-List Preferred and Business Select. The reported airline estimates of $210 million in 2025 and $300 million in 2026 are additional revenue, not net profit. A customer who pays the fee adds revenue; one who switches airlines can take the entire fare away. More carry-ons could also slow boarding. [7](https://web.archive.org/web/20250405110702/https://www.cbsnews.com/texas/news/southwest-airlines-free-checked-bags-changes-seat-assignments/#:~:text=Editor%27s%20Note%3A%20Southwest%20Airlines%20announced%20on%20March%2011%2C%202025%2C,seek%20to%20reverse%20shrinking%20profits%20and%20slumping%20stock%20price.) [8](https://web.archive.org/web/20250317113716/https://www.visaverge.com/news/southwest-airlines-criticized-for-dropping-free-checked-bags-policy/#:~:text=%E2%80%A2%20Southwest%20Airlines%20will%20end%20its%20%E2%80%9Cbags%20fly%20free%E2%80%9D,new%20revenue%20model%2C%20reactions%20have%20been%20swift%20and%20critical.) [9](https://web.archive.org/web/20250317113716/https://www.visaverge.com/news/southwest-airlines-criticized-for-dropping-free-checked-bags-policy/#:~:text=For%20passengers%2C%20the%20disappearance%20of%20free%20checked%20bags%20is,travelers%2C%20who%20will%20have%20fewer%20truly%20low-cost%20options%20available.)

Red-eye flights offer a distinct route to better margins: an aircraft that would otherwise sit overnight can earn another fare without Southwest adding a plane. But extra flying is profitable only if receipts cover the added crew, fuel and other operating costs. It can also consume time that would otherwise help an aircraft get back on schedule. The available network evidence identifies the red-eye initiative, not route-level profits, utilization gains or recovery buffers; it does not establish that the revised schedule is either more profitable or more resilient. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250414114607/https://www.dallasnews.com/business/airlines/2024/09/10/southwest-airlines-caves-activist-investor-pressure-shakes-up-board/#:~:text=The%20changes%20came%20as%20Southwest%20leaders%2C%20including%20Kelly%2C%20met,the%20latest%20airlines%20news%2C%20delivered%20straight%20to%20your%20inbox.)

The operational failure was not simply exposure to bad weather; it was the inability to put crews and aircraft back on schedule after conditions improved. On December 25 and 26, 2022, Southwest canceled over 5,500 flights versus Delta’s 311. The sharper comparison is Denver: as weather warmed and other airlines largely resumed service, Southwest still canceled about 75% of its schedule there. Crew-scheduling phone waits exceeded five hours. The available evidence does not document a separate 2023 incident in comparable detail or show recovery times in a comparable later shock through 2025-04-23. Better recovery is therefore unproven, not disproven. [10](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1278479828)

## What would change the view

My base case is a partial margin improvement from paid choices, with no assumed improvement in disruption recovery. The strongest alternative is that customers valued Southwest’s simple bundled fare more than they value seat choice: fee receipts could rise while total profit stagnates. Stable repeat bookings, higher revenue per available seat mile and a narrowing peer operating-margin gap after rollout would favor the base case; falling retention and flat margins despite fee growth would favor the alternative. For resilience, the decisive test is separate: after comparable weather clears, do crew-assignment delays subside and cancellation rates return to normal as quickly as at similarly affected peers? [9](https://web.archive.org/web/20250317113716/https://www.visaverge.com/news/southwest-airlines-criticized-for-dropping-free-checked-bags-policy/#:~:text=For%20passengers%2C%20the%20disappearance%20of%20free%20checked%20bags%20is,travelers%2C%20who%20will%20have%20fewer%20truly%20low-cost%20options%20available.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250414114607/https://www.dallasnews.com/business/airlines/2024/09/10/southwest-airlines-caves-activist-investor-pressure-shakes-up-board/#:~:text=The%20changes%20came%20as%20Southwest%20leaders%2C%20including%20Kelly%2C%20met,the%20latest%20airlines%20news%2C%20delivered%20straight%20to%20your%20inbox.) [10](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1278479828)

question: How do Teck Resources' recent earnings beats, the $2.4 billion Highland Valley copper mine extension, and the Quebrada Blanca ramp-up reconcile with the simultaneous price target reductions by JP Morgan and RBC, and what does this suggest about the company's valuation as it transitions into a copper-focused producer?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-07-29

**Research question**
How do Teck Resources' recent earnings beats, the $2.4 billion Highland Valley copper mine extension, and the Quebrada Blanca ramp-up reconcile with the simultaneous price target reductions by JP Morgan and RBC, and what does this suggest about the company's valuation as it transitions into a copper-focused producer?

## Answer

As of 2025-07-29, Teck’s future copper production warrants an execution-risk discount relative to a valuation that assumes the mines deliver on schedule, not a premium simply for exiting coal. The transition is material: the coal divestiture valued those operations at US$9 billion and left Teck focused on copper and zinc. If confirmed, the earnings beats and the JP Morgan and RBC target cuts would not conflict: earnings can exceed expectations for a past quarter while the expected value of future mine cash flows falls. That is a valuation judgment, not a finding that Teck’s shares already trade at a discount. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1291896569)

## Evidence

The earnings beats and simultaneous target cuts remain unverified question premises. The available history reports revenue from an earlier period, not recent reported earnings against pre-release consensus on the same accounting basis. It supplies neither bank’s dated note, prior and revised targets, currency or rationale. A lower target alone would not establish a lower valuation multiple: a bank could apply the same multiple to a smaller earnings forecast. There is no basis here for attributing either bank’s decision to mine performance. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1291896569)

The Highland Valley extension and its stated cost are unverified question premises. Teck’s Highland Valley mine produced 119,000 tonnes of copper in 2016, but that history establishes neither the extension budget nor its currency or spending schedule. The extension’s value depends on how much profitable production it would preserve relative to operating the mine without it. Construction could therefore reduce near-term free cash flow even if the added years of production justify the investment. An earnings beat would not settle the funding question: the relevant test is whether operating cash flow covers both sustaining capital and extension spending. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1291896569)

## Outlook

Quebrada Blanca presents a different valuation test: how quickly it can turn capacity into profitable copper sales. The evidence confirms Teck runs the Chilean mine, not the pace or cost of the reported ramp-up. The base case gives partial credit for future production: slower throughput would defer receipts and spread fixed costs over fewer saleable tonnes while Highland Valley spending could draw on the same cash. Without production, unit-cost and capital-spending data, neither the cash shortfall nor the appropriate discount can be quantified. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1291896569)

## What would change the view

The strongest case for a premium is that Quebrada Blanca reaches sustained, profitable output soon enough to help fund Highland Valley, giving shareholders a longer copper production life without a prolonged drain on cash. The observable signal would be successive operating reports showing Quebrada Blanca meeting throughput, recovery and unit-cost guidance, Highland Valley meeting disclosed budget milestones, and positive free cash flow after extension spending at comparable copper prices. That would justify reducing the execution discount; a premium over other copper producers would still require a peer valuation comparison. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1291896569)

## Sources

1. [Teck Resources](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1291896569), available by 2025-05-24.

question: Given Statistics Canada's reports of a 0.2% GDP contraction in February 2025 and a subsequent 6.6% plunge in building permits, how has the outlook for Canadian domestic demand shifted? Analysis should contrast Q4 2024 growth against softening retail sales and the 7.0% May unemployment rate.
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-06-17

**Research question**
Given Statistics Canada's reports of a 0.2% GDP contraction in February 2025 and a subsequent 6.6% plunge in building permits, how has the outlook for Canadian domestic demand shifted? Analysis should contrast Q4 2024 growth against softening retail sales and the 7.0% May unemployment rate.

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-06-17, I would flag downside risk to Canadian domestic demand but not downgrade the growth forecast from its Q4 2024 pace on this evidence alone. Statistics Canada’s tracker notice identifies relevant series but gives neither the quarterly growth benchmark nor the monthly readings. Holding the forecast is a decision not to act on unverified figures, not a finding that households and businesses sustained their earlier spending pace. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250510235106/https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/250410/dq250410e-eng.htm#:~:text=The%20Canadian%20Economic%20Tracker%20presents%20selected%20monthly%20indicators%20from,release%2C%20%22Canadian%20Economic%20Tracker%3A%20A%20new%20data%20visualization%20tool.%22) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250510235106/https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/250410/dq250410e-eng.htm#:~:text=Skip%20to%20%22About%20this%20site%22%20Monthly%20Analysis%20on%20the,that%20accompanies%20the%20Canadian%20Economic%20Tracker%20is%20now%20available.)

## Evidence

The contrast between Q4 2024 growth and subsequent household weakness is plausible but unverified. The notice lists retail sales without a reference month, direction or distinction between dollar sales and volume. It also does not verify the unemployment rate attributed to May. Even a confirmed May rate would need a prior reading to establish deterioration; a rate level by itself does not show that households cut spending. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250510235106/https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/250410/dq250410e-eng.htm#:~:text=The%20Canadian%20Economic%20Tracker%20presents%20selected%20monthly%20indicators%20from,release%2C%20%22Canadian%20Economic%20Tracker%3A%20A%20new%20data%20visualization%20tool.%22)

## What would change the view

Test the unchanged forecast against quarterly real final domestic demand, comparing its growth with Q4 2024 on the same basis. The strongest case for a downgrade would be slower real consumption and investment, corroborated by sustained retail-volume weakness and rising unemployment in dated releases. If spending instead holds up, an isolated output dip and volatile permits would be a better explanation than a common demand slowdown. The tracker notice directs readers to the underlying analysis but does not resolve that test. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250510235106/https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/250410/dq250410e-eng.htm#:~:text=To%20access%20the%20analysis%2C%20click%20on%20the%20%22Monthly%20analysis%22,upper%20right-hand%20corner%20of%20the%20Canadian%20Economic%20Tracker%20page.) [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250510235106/https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/250410/dq250410e-eng.htm#:~:text=The%20Canadian%20Economic%20Tracker%20presents%20selected%20monthly%20indicators%20from,release%2C%20%22Canadian%20Economic%20Tracker%3A%20A%20new%20data%20visualization%20tool.%22)

## Sources

[The Daily — Monthly Analysis on the Canadian Economic Tracker, April 2025](https://web.archive.org/web/20250510235106/https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/250410/dq250410e-eng.htm#:~:text=The%20Canadian%20Economic%20Tracker%20presents%20selected%20monthly%20indicators%20from,release%2C%20%22Canadian%20Economic%20Tracker%3A%20A%20new%20data%20visualization%20tool.%22), available by 2025-05-10.

question: How will tightening U.S. trade policies regarding the de minimis loophole and new tariff adjustments impact PDD Holdings’ international growth trajectory via Temu, and what are the resulting risks to the group’s consolidated margin profile under the leadership of Chairman and Co-CEO Lei Chen?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-05-27

**Research question**
How will tightening U.S. trade policies regarding the de minimis loophole and new tariff adjustments impact PDD Holdings’ international growth trajectory via Temu, and what are the resulting risks to the group’s consolidated margin profile under the leadership of Chairman and Co-CEO Lei Chen?

## Answer

As of 2025-05-27, lower near-term forecasts for both Temu-led international revenue growth and PDD Holdings’ consolidated operating margin under Chairman and Co-CEO Lei Chen. The U.S. ended duty-free entry for low-value shipments from China and Hong Kong; later relief cut the postal tariff rate but did not restore the exemption. Expect slower international growth, not necessarily a contraction. The margin cut has a separate basis: Chen says merchant and consumer support was already weighing on profitability before the May policy changes. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250524171650/https://www.channelnewsasia.com/world/trump-ends-china-low-value-shipments-duty-free-access-de-minimis-5105226#:~:text=Packages%20are%20seen%20stacked%20on%20the%20doorstep%20of%20a,airports%20and%20caused%20millions%20of%20packages%20to%20pile%20up.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250526150301/https://www.inc.com/reuters/in-another-trump-retreat-u-s-slashes-de-minimis-tariff/91188437#:~:text=The%20tariff%20relief%2C%20which%20affects%20big%20Chinese%20e-commerce%20players,those%20tariff%20fees%20from%20sellers%20in%20China%20in%20advance.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250527104913/https://finance.yahoo.com/news/pdd-holdings-announces-first-quarter-103000839.html#:~:text=Net%20income%20attributable%20to%20ordinary%20shareholders%20in%20the%20quarter,reduce%20costs%20for%20a%20broader%20base%20of%20SME%20merchants.%E2%80%9D) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250527104913/https://finance.yahoo.com/news/pdd-holdings-announces-first-quarter-103000839.html#:~:text=Oops%2C%20something%20went%20wrong%20DUBLIN%20and%20SHANGHAI%2C%20May%2027%2C,quarter%20ended%20March%2031%2C%202025.%20First%20Quarter%202025%20Highlights)

## Evidence

The May 2 change removed an exemption; the May 14 change altered the cost of shipping without it. For items valued at up to $800 sent from China via postal services, the rate fell from 120% to 54%, with a flat $100 per package as an alternative, not a surcharge. That is meaningful relief relative to the initial tariff, but still a cost relative to duty-free entry. Neither postal rate should be applied to all Temu sales or to bulk imports for U.S. warehouses. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250524171650/https://www.channelnewsasia.com/world/trump-ends-china-low-value-shipments-duty-free-access-de-minimis-5105226#:~:text=Packages%20are%20seen%20stacked%20on%20the%20doorstep%20of%20a,airports%20and%20caused%20millions%20of%20packages%20to%20pile%20up.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250526150301/https://www.inc.com/reuters/in-another-trump-retreat-u-s-slashes-de-minimis-tariff/91188437#:~:text=The%20tariff%20relief%2C%20which%20affects%20big%20Chinese%20e-commerce%20players,those%20tariff%20fees%20from%20sellers%20in%20China%20in%20advance.)

PDD’s disclosures support a lower group margin forecast, but not a numerical split between Temu and domestic merchant support. In the quarter ended March 31, 2025, attributable net income fell 47% year over year. That is not an operating-margin measure, and the quarter predates the loss of the exemption. Management expects sustained ecosystem investment, but the available results give neither Temu operating profit nor a domestic support expense breakdown. Treat any future Temu subsidy as a risk, not a measured loss to add on top of reported group spending. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250527104913/https://finance.yahoo.com/news/pdd-holdings-announces-first-quarter-103000839.html#:~:text=Oops%2C%20something%20went%20wrong%20DUBLIN%20and%20SHANGHAI%2C%20May%2027%2C,quarter%20ended%20March%2031%2C%202025.%20First%20Quarter%202025%20Highlights) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250527104913/https://finance.yahoo.com/news/pdd-holdings-announces-first-quarter-103000839.html#:~:text=Net%20income%20attributable%20to%20ordinary%20shareholders%20in%20the%20quarter,reduce%20costs%20for%20a%20broader%20base%20of%20SME%20merchants.%E2%80%9D) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250527104913/https://finance.yahoo.com/news/pdd-holdings-announces-first-quarter-103000839.html#:~:text=%E2%80%9CAs%20communicated%20previously%2C%20a%20slowdown%20in%20growth%20rate%20is,this%20press%20release.%20First%20Quarter%202025%20Unaudited%20Financial%20Results)

## Outlook

The base case is a slower U.S. sales ramp while sellers rebuild the assortment. Temu said U.S. orders would be fulfilled domestically. A seller that once shipped after receiving an order must now have stock in the country before making that sale. Sellers may stock fewer unproven items or raise prices to cover landed costs, weakening Temu’s appeal; if Temu subsidizes prices to preserve demand, the pressure shifts from growth toward margin. This is a U.S. channel shock, not evidence of weaker demand in every international market. [6](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1289186606) [7](https://web.archive.org/web/20250526150301/https://www.inc.com/reuters/in-another-trump-retreat-u-s-slashes-de-minimis-tariff/91188437#:~:text=The%20tariff%20pause%20will%20give%20online%20retailers%20like%20Shein,US%2C%20it%E2%80%99s%20too%20risky%2C%E2%80%9D%20said%20Hu%20of%20Brands%20Factory.) [8](https://web.archive.org/web/20250527145946/https://www.supplychaindive.com/news/temu-walks-back-price-increases/747126/#:~:text=A%20Shein%20spokesperson%20didn%E2%80%99t%20immediately%20respond%20to%20a%20request,co-founder%20of%20AI%20firm%20Pimberly%2C%20said%20in%20emailed%20comments.)

## What would change the view

The strongest alternative is that local fulfillment makes the U.S. disruption brief: Temu was already adding warehouses, and shorter delivery times and a broader range of bulky goods could offset the loss of cheap direct parcels. Restore the growth forecast if U.S. order growth recovers as locally stocked selection expands, or if sales elsewhere demonstrably offset U.S. weakness. Restore the margin forecast separately: look for that recovery without heavier incentives and for sustained improvement in consolidated operating margin. A group rebound alone would not identify Temu’s contribution. [6](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1289186606) [7](https://web.archive.org/web/20250526150301/https://www.inc.com/reuters/in-another-trump-retreat-u-s-slashes-de-minimis-tariff/91188437#:~:text=The%20tariff%20pause%20will%20give%20online%20retailers%20like%20Shein,US%2C%20it%E2%80%99s%20too%20risky%2C%E2%80%9D%20said%20Hu%20of%20Brands%20Factory.) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250527104913/https://finance.yahoo.com/news/pdd-holdings-announces-first-quarter-103000839.html#:~:text=%E2%80%9CAs%20communicated%20previously%2C%20a%20slowdown%20in%20growth%20rate%20is,this%20press%20release.%20First%20Quarter%202025%20Unaudited%20Financial%20Results)

## Sources

1. [China low-value package tariff exemption ends but questions remain over US collections - CNA](https://web.archive.org/web/20250524171650/https://www.channelnewsasia.com/world/trump-ends-china-low-value-shipments-duty-free-access-de-minimis-5105226#:~:text=Packages%20are%20seen%20stacked%20on%20the%20doorstep%20of%20a,airports%20and%20caused%20millions%20of%20packages%20to%20pile%20up.), available by 2025-05-24.
2. question: How do Colin Langan's June 2025 rating adjustments and price target revisions for Autoliv, BorgWarner, and Dana reflect a diverging sector outlook between diversified auto suppliers and pure-play electric vehicle manufacturers like Tesla and Rivian?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-06-29

**Research question**
How do Colin Langan's June 2025 rating adjustments and price target revisions for Autoliv, BorgWarner, and Dana reflect a diverging sector outlook between diversified auto suppliers and pure-play electric vehicle manufacturers like Tesla and Rivian?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-06-29, the evidence does not establish that Wells Fargo’s Colin Langan favored Autoliv, BorgWarner and Dana over Tesla and Rivian in June 2025. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250413011922/https://www.kbb.com/car-news/ev-sales-jumped-10-in-the-first-quarter/#:~:text=Americans%20bought%2010.6%25%20more%20electric%20vehicles%20%28EVs%29%20in%20the,electric%2C%20up%20half%20a%20percent%20from%20last%20year%E2%80%99s%20total.) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1295235410)

## Evidence

The strongest market evidence points to a divergence *within* the US EV market, not between suppliers and EV makers. Kelley Blue Book reports that first-quarter EV purchases rose 10.6% year over year, while sales of Tesla’s Model Y fell 34% on the same basis. That contrast is consistent with a Tesla-specific competitive or product issue rather than a market-wide demand decline. It does not establish Langan’s rationale, show comparable weakness at Rivian or identify a catalyst for Autoliv, BorgWarner or Dana. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250413011922/https://www.kbb.com/car-news/ev-sales-jumped-10-in-the-first-quarter/#:~:text=Americans%20bought%2010.6%25%20more%20electric%20vehicles%20%28EVs%29%20in%20the,electric%2C%20up%20half%20a%20percent%20from%20last%20year%E2%80%99s%20total.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250413011922/https://www.kbb.com/car-news/ev-sales-jumped-10-in-the-first-quarter/#:~:text=Stellantis%20launched%20the%20first%20EVs%20under%20the%20Jeep%20and,the%20first%20quarter%20were%20down%2026%25%20from%20that%20peak.)

## What would change the view

The working base case is to assess each company on its own rather than infer a sector call from the sales split. The strongest alternative is that Langan favored diversified suppliers for a shared reason even as EV sales grew. To distinguish those views, compare his dated June notes with the preceding rating and target for each stock. Consistently stronger supplier ratings would establish a preference; a common earnings or valuation assumption explicitly driving the revisions would support a sector explanation. Distinct catalysts would instead support company-specific calls, even if the targets moved together. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250413011922/https://www.kbb.com/car-news/ev-sales-jumped-10-in-the-first-quarter/#:~:text=New%20EVs%20Pick%20Up%20Sales%20Pace%20The%20sales%20pace,Cadillac%20Lyriq%2C%20and%20even%20the%20off-road-oriented%20GMC%20Hummer%20EV.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250413011922/https://www.kbb.com/car-news/ev-sales-jumped-10-in-the-first-quarter/#:~:text=Stellantis%20launched%20the%20first%20EVs%20under%20the%20Jeep%20and,the%20first%20quarter%20were%20down%2026%25%20from%20that%20peak.)

## Sources

[EV Sales Jumped 10% in the First Quarter - Kelley Blue Book](https://web.archive.org/web/20250413011922/https://www.kbb.com/car-news/ev-sales-jumped-10-in-the-first-quarter/#:~:text=Americans%20bought%2010.6%25%20more%20electric%20vehicles%20%28EVs%29%20in%20the,electric%2C%20up%20half%20a%20percent%20from%20last%20year%E2%80%99s%20total.), available by 2025-04-13.

question: How should portfolio managers evaluate the divergence between high-profile institutional exits and the aggressive accumulation by Krane Funds and JPMorgan, given TME's consistent revenue growth and the cluster of analyst upgrades and price target hikes observed in early 2025?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-05-21

**Research question**
How should portfolio managers evaluate the divergence between high-profile institutional exits and the aggressive accumulation by Krane Funds and JPMorgan, given TME's consistent revenue growth and the cluster of analyst upgrades and price target hikes observed in early 2025?

## Answer

Hold TME as of 2025-05-21. The reported high-profile exits, aggressive accumulation by Krane Funds and JPMorgan, and cluster of analyst upgrades and target hikes in early 2025 are unverified question premises. The scale of the operating improvement is clearer: first-quarter revenue rose 8.7% year over year to RMB7.36 billion. That argues against trimming solely because others reportedly sold. Without the May market price or comparable forward earnings estimates, it does not establish a margin of safety for adding. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250514122530/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/tencent-music-entertainment-group-announces-first-quarter-2025-unaudited-financial-results-302453595.html#:~:text=Total%20revenues%20were%20RMB7.36%20billion%20%28US%241.01%20billion%29%2C%20representing%20an,RMB11.4%20from%20RMB10.6%20in%20the%20same%20period%20of%202024.)

## Evidence

Give neither side of the reported ownership divergence weight yet. A larger position by market value can reflect appreciation with no purchase; even a larger share count can reflect fund inflows or index rebalancing rather than a discretionary bet. Compare the same managers’ split-adjusted TME share counts across matching quarter-ends, then check changes against fund flows and benchmark weights. Apply the same test to the reported sellers. The JPMorgan material describes the bank, not its TME holdings; the record establishes neither trade size nor motive. [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1290805468)

## Outlook

The base case is that subscription growth continues to outweigh weakness in social entertainment, not that revenue growth is assured. Paying users rose 8.3% year over year and monthly revenue per paying user rose to RMB11.4 from RMB10.6. Those gains helped lift subscription revenue to RMB4.22 billion, while social entertainment and other revenue fell 11.9% to RMB1.55 billion. The next report can test whether paid users and spending per user keep rising together and whether the resulting music revenue gain still exceeds the social revenue loss. The reported quarter supports that mechanism, not a claim of consistent growth across multiple quarters. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250514122530/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/tencent-music-entertainment-group-announces-first-quarter-2025-unaudited-financial-results-302453595.html#:~:text=Total%20revenues%20were%20RMB7.36%20billion%20%28US%241.01%20billion%29%2C%20representing%20an,RMB11.4%20from%20RMB10.6%20in%20the%20same%20period%20of%202024.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250514122530/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/tencent-music-entertainment-group-announces-first-quarter-2025-unaudited-financial-results-302453595.html#:~:text=Total%20revenues%20increased%20by%20RMB588%20million%2C%20or%208.7%25%2C%20to,live-streaming%20interactive%20functions%20and%20more%20stringent%20compliance%20procedures%20implemented.)

## What would change the view

The strongest case for trimming is that the price already assumes further premium-tier adoption, leaving earnings and the valuation multiple exposed if promotions resume and social entertainment keeps shrinking. Flat or falling spending per paying user alongside continued social declines would strengthen that case. For each reported target hike, compare the analyst’s old and new earnings estimates for the same fiscal period: a higher target on unchanged earnings is a bet on a richer multiple, not better profits. Increase only if earnings revisions support the higher targets and a valuation using weaker monetization and a lower multiple implies tolerable downside from the cutoff price. The available evidence supplies neither the forecast revisions nor the prices needed for that test. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250514122530/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/tencent-music-entertainment-group-announces-first-quarter-2025-unaudited-financial-results-302453595.html#:~:text=Total%20revenues%20increased%20by%20RMB588%20million%2C%20or%208.7%25%2C%20to,live-streaming%20interactive%20functions%20and%20more%20stringent%20compliance%20procedures%20implemented.)

## Sources

1. [Tencent Music Entertainment Group Announces First Quarter 2025 Unaudited Financial Results](https://web.archive.org/web/20250514122530/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/tencent-music-entertainment-group-announces-first-quarter-2025-unaudited-financial-results-302453595.html#:~:text=Total%20revenues%20were%20RMB7.36%20billion%20%28US%241.01%20billion%29%2C%20representing%20an,RMB11.4%20from%20RMB10.6%20in%20the%20same%20period%20of%202024.), available by 2025-05-14.
2. [JPMorgan Chase](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1290805468), available by 2025-05-17.
3. [Tencent Music Entertainment Group Announces First Quarter 2025 Unaudited Financial Results](https://web.archive.org/web/20250514122530/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/tencent-music-entertainment-group-announces-first-quarter-2025-unaudited-financial-results-302453595.html#:~:text=Total%20revenues%20increased%20by%20RMB588%20million%2C%20or%208.7%25%2C%20to,live-streaming%20interactive%20functions%20and%20more%20stringent%20compliance%20procedures%20implemented.), available by 2025-05-14.

question: How do Copart's $3.34 billion cash position and historical reinvestment efficiency reconcile with significant Q4 2024 institutional divestments by AllianceBernstein and Capital Research, and the recent insider selling activity by directors James E. Meeks and Steven D. Cohan?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-06-17

**Research question**
How do Copart's $3.34 billion cash position and historical reinvestment efficiency reconcile with significant Q4 2024 institutional divestments by AllianceBernstein and Capital Research, and the recent insider selling activity by directors James E. Meeks and Steven D. Cohan?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Evidence

Copart’s expansion history explains why retaining cash could make sense, but does not establish reinvestment efficiency. The NER acquisition doubled the facility count; national coverage then helped Copart pursue insurer contracts. That gives a new yard a potential benefit beyond its own sales if it helps win volume across the network. Neither the acquisition history nor the cash premise tells us how much additional operating profit Copart earned per dollar invested, or whether comparable opportunities remain. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1288176292)

AllianceBernstein’s firmwide assets under management in April are not a measure of its Copart holdings in the preceding December. Compare consecutive quarter-end holdings disclosures on the same reporting basis for each manager to establish any net reduction; those snapshots would not reveal trade dates or motives. For Meeks and Cohan, check transaction filings for sale dates, amounts, remaining stakes and trading-plan disclosures. Even verified sales transfer holders’ shares, not Copart’s operating cash: portfolio rebalancing or personal diversification could coexist with attractive reinvestment returns. [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1288484772)

## What would change the view

The hold case predicts that added capacity will attract insurer volume and lift operating profit as yards mature. The strongest alternative is that the best sites are already in place: cash may accumulate for lack of attractive projects while newer yards earn less. Verify the dated cash balance against Copart’s filings, then compare the sustained increase in after-tax operating profit with the capital committed to successive expansions, allowing similar time for each to mature. Persistently lower returns on mature projects would support a trim even without holder sales; confirmed sales alone would not. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1288176292)

## Sources

1. [Copart](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1288176292), available by 2025-04-30.
2. [AllianceBernstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1288484772), available by 2025-05-02.

question: Given the divergence between significant Q4 2024 institutional inflows from firms like Balyasny and D1 Capital and aggressive insider liquidation by CEO Douglas Yearley and CFO Martin Connor, how should investors assess Toll Brothers' valuation and margin sustainability as it pivots toward lower-priced inventory?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-05-27

**Research question**
Given the divergence between significant Q4 2024 institutional inflows from firms like Balyasny and D1 Capital and aggressive insider liquidation by CEO Douglas Yearley and CFO Martin Connor, how should investors assess Toll Brothers' valuation and margin sustainability as it pivots toward lower-priced inventory?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

Wait rather than buy Toll Brothers at the 2025-05-27 price. The reported significant Q4 2024 purchases by Balyasny and D1 Capital and aggressive insider selling by Douglas Yearley and Martin Connor are unverified question premises. The available evidence identifies Yearley as CEO but gives neither the shares bought by either manager nor the fraction of either insider’s stake sold. Give the reports no weight in the valuation. The cited home prices are not a stock quote; without a verified cutoff share price and a conservative estimate of cash earnings per share, a margin of safety is unproven, not necessarily absent. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1264406239) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1292602434)

## Evidence

Test the apparent divergence against the filings before interpreting it. Compare Toll share counts in consecutive quarter-end holdings filings for each manager: a larger reported stake would establish a net increase in shares held, not the cash spent, entry price or investment thesis. The later report naming Maplebear as D1 Capital’s largest U.S.-listed long position neither confirms nor contradicts an earlier Toll purchase. For Yearley and Connor, check transaction codes, trading-plan footnotes and holdings before and after each transaction. A discretionary sale of a substantial share of an insider’s stake is more informative than shares withheld for taxes, but even a verified sale would not establish that housing margins are deteriorating. None of the relevant filings is supplied. [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1292602434) [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1264406239)

## What would change the view

The strongest buy case is that cheaper homes tie up less capital for less time: even with fewer gross-profit dollars per delivery, Toll could earn more on its average inventory investment. Look for higher deliveries per community, stable or rising total homebuilding gross profit and improving operating cash flow without deeper incentives, rather than faster orders alone. To move from wait to buy, verify the cutoff price and compare it with a conservative per-share value based on cash earnings after inventory reinvestment, allowing for net debt and a slower-turn downside. The historical price data supply none of those valuation inputs. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1264406239)

## Sources

1. [Toll Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1264406239), available by 2024-12-21.
2. [D1 Capital Partners](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1292602434), available by 2025-05-27.

question: How is the integration of Marathon Oil and the resulting production surge influencing ConocoPhillips' valuation outlook, given the divergence between quantitative value models and the recent wave of sell-side rating downgrades and price target reductions observed in May 2025?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-06-05

**Research question**
How is the integration of Marathon Oil and the resulting production surge influencing ConocoPhillips' valuation outlook, given the divergence between quantitative value models and the recent wave of sell-side rating downgrades and price target reductions observed in May 2025?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Evidence

The acquisition changes what a production comparison measures: post-close ConocoPhillips includes Marathon barrels that pre-close ConocoPhillips did not. Consolidated output could therefore rise even if neither operator improved well performance. Marathon had already spun off its downstream operations, so the relevant cash-flow test is what the acquired production earns at realized oil and gas prices after operating costs and the capital needed to sustain output. The available evidence supplies neither acquired volumes nor that cash-flow contribution. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1287386462)

Which May cuts also involved rating downgrades? None can be verified from the available evidence; that is not a finding that none occurred. The dated transaction report establishes the closing, not an analyst action. Verification requires each firm’s dated old and new target and recommendation: a lower target with an unchanged recommendation is not a downgrade. Without those notes, the value models’ inputs or a cutoff share price, neither the size of a valuation gap nor its cause can be established. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1287386462)

## Outlook

My base case gives Marathon credit for acquired output but no valuation premium until cash generation per diluted share improves. A value model using normalized commodity prices and a sell-side target using a weaker near-term price forecast could both be internally consistent; those are possible explanations, not documented assumptions. To distinguish a price disagreement from an integration disagreement, compare the valuations at the same commodity prices and horizon, then examine what each assumes about costs, capital spending and share count. [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1292266911) [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1287386462)

## What would change the view

The strongest bullish alternative is that combining the upstream assets lowers recurring costs enough to lift sustainable free cash flow per diluted share beyond what the market price implies. I would look for a reconciliation from standalone ConocoPhillips to combined cash flow per share at common realized prices, separating acquired cash flow, realized savings, integration spending, sustaining capital and financing effects. A durable gain that supports a value above the cutoff price would justify the discount thesis; more barrels without that gain would favor caution, though not validate a particular target. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1287386462)

## Sources

1. [Marathon Oil](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1287386462), available by 2025-04-25.
2. [ConocoPhillips](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1292266911), available by 2025-05-26.

question: How do PTTEP’s recent strategic actions—including the divestment of North American assets, the acquisition of Jadestone’s Sinphuhorm stake, and intensified drilling campaigns in Sarawak—impact the feasibility of its 900,000 boe/d production target for 2030 amid ongoing recovery challenges at the Erawan gas field?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-07-21

**Research question**
How do PTTEP’s recent strategic actions—including the divestment of North American assets, the acquisition of Jadestone’s Sinphuhorm stake, and intensified drilling campaigns in Sarawak—impact the feasibility of its 900,000 boe/d production target for 2030 amid ongoing recovery challenges at the Erawan gas field?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Evidence

The North American divestment and the purchase of Jadestone’s Sinphuhorm stake, as described in the question, have opposite effects on attributable volumes only to the extent that the interests carry output. The relevant comparison is the volume PTTEP would have retained from the sold interests in the target year against the volume due to PTTEP from the acquired stake that year—not the gross output of Sinphuhorm. The historical portfolio count establishes neither the transactions’ effective dates nor their net rates. There is no basis to say the purchase replaces the loss; a baseline taken after closing must not count either transaction again. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1301342510)

Erawan recovery would help PTTEP grow from a depressed baseline, but restoring lost flow is not new field capacity. Credit only the sustained increase above the chosen baseline, and none of the recovery already reflected in it. The portfolio profile counts Thai projects but gives no Erawan rate or recovery schedule. It therefore cannot show how much of the gap restoration would close or whether the restored rate could be maintained. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1301342510)

Treat the Sarawak drilling campaign described in the question as exploration upside, not committed supply. Bintulu’s offshore gas history and LNG infrastructure make commercialization plausible in principle; neither demonstrates a commercial PTTEP discovery, a sanctioned development or access to processing capacity. Include a project in the committed case only when its approval, timetable and PTTEP share support an attributable rate deliverable by the target year. [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1300423154)

## What would change the view

The investment base case leaves the target unproven. The strongest alternative is that sustained Erawan recovery, Sinphuhorm and timely Sarawak developments together more than offset divested volumes and decline elsewhere. The decisive signal would be a dated PTTEP reconciliation from reported production or sales to a target on the same basis: net volumes sold and acquired, observed Erawan delivery, and sanctioned project start dates with attributable rates after ramp-up. If those rates cover the gap after decline without relying on unsanctioned wells, the target becomes credible. Project counts and regional infrastructure cannot pass that test. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1301342510) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1300423154)

## Sources

1. [PTT Exploration and Production](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1301342510), available by 2025-07-19.
2. [Bintulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1300423154), available by 2025-07-14.

question: How is the operational divergence between H World Group's Legacy-Huazhu and Legacy-DH segments impacting its long-term margin profile, considering the Q1 2025 earnings miss and the aggressive transition to a 91% manachised business model under CEO Jin Hui's expansion strategy?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-05-27

**Research question**
How is the operational divergence between H World Group's Legacy-Huazhu and Legacy-DH segments impacting its long-term margin profile, considering the Q1 2025 earnings miss and the aggressive transition to a 91% manachised business model under CEO Jin Hui's expansion strategy?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-05-27, I would not forecast a sustained increase in H World’s consolidated operating margin above its 2024 level solely on the strength of the expansion attributed to CEO Jin Hui. Legacy-Huazhu can earn fees from additional rooms without directly operating the hotels. But weaker Legacy-Huazhu revenue per available room and a burdensome Legacy-DH cost base are unverified question premises. If both persist, lower fees on existing rooms and costs at DH could offset the profit from new rooms. The available evidence establishes the fee model and the acquisition of Deutsche Hospitality, but gives neither the group’s baseline operating margin nor the segment results needed to quantify the offset. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250425054324/https://ir.hworld.com/news-releases/news-release-details/huazhu-group-limited-announces-acquisition-blossom-hill-hotels#:~:text=Huazhu%20Group%20Limited%20is%20a%20leading%20hotel%20operator%20and,For%20more%20information%2C%20please%20visit%20the%20Company%E2%80%99s%20website%3A%20http%3A%2F%2Fir.huazhu.com.) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1265176034) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250512054054/https://www.cushmanwakefield.com/en/germany/news/2025/04/hotelinvestmentmarket-germany#:~:text=The%20hotel%20segment%20accounted%20for%206%25%20of%20the%20total,for%20its%20award-winning%20culture.%20For%20additional%20information%2C%20visit%20www.cushmanwakefield.com.)

## Evidence

The Q1 2025 miss was in adjusted EPS and, according to Zacks’s headline, revenue. Adjusted EPS was $0.34 against consensus of $0.42, an actual-minus-consensus difference of -0.08 per share, despite improving from $0.29 a year earlier. The excerpt gives no size for the revenue miss and no operating-profit estimate. It therefore establishes neither an operating-profit miss nor a decline in operating margin. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250520155503/https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2474420/h-world-group-htht-misses-q1-earnings-and-revenue-estimates#:~:text=If%20you%20wish%20to%20go%20to%20ZacksTrade%2C%20click%20OK.,year%20ago.%20These%20figures%20are%20adjusted%20for%20non-recurring%20items.)

## What would change the view

The strongest case for a higher margin is that new fee-paying rooms add more profit per unit of reported revenue than directly operated hotels, even without a RevPAR recovery. The risk is that lower room takings reduce revenue-linked fees across the existing Huazhu network while DH’s costs do not fall with revenue. To distinguish those outcomes, track Huazhu fee revenue per operating fee-paying room alongside comparable-hotel RevPAR, then compare each segment’s operating profit with its revenue. I would raise the base case if fee growth consistently lifted Huazhu’s margin enough to carry the consolidated margin above its baseline after DH costs. More openings alone would not meet that test. question: How does the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board's (CPPIB) systematic reduction of its stake in Viking Holdings (VIK) throughout 2025 impact the company's equity capital structure and market liquidity, especially given CEO Torstein Hagen’s continued majority voting control and the stock's recent price rally?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-08-20

**Research question**
How does the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board's (CPPIB) systematic reduction of its stake in Viking Holdings (VIK) throughout 2025 impact the company's equity capital structure and market liquidity, especially given CEO Torstein Hagen’s continued majority voting control and the stock's recent price rally?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-08-20, the documented sell-down changed who owned Viking, not how many shares Viking had outstanding or who controlled the vote. CPPIB and TPG were the sellers in a public offering of 30,531,917 existing ordinary shares at $44.20 per share that closed on May 29. That share count is the sellers’ combined total, not CPPIB’s sale alone. The proceeds went to the sellers; Viking raised no equity capital and existing holders suffered no dilution from the deal. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250722150855/https://www.ropesgray.com/en/news-and-events/news/2025/06/viking-holdings-closes-on-secondary-public-offering#:~:text=Ropes%20%26%20Gray%20represented%20selling%20shareholders%20TPG%20Capital%20and,selling%20shareholders%20in%20Viking%E2%80%99s%20IPO%20and%202024%20secondary%20offering.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250723223341/https://ir.viking.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/191/viking-announces-pricing-of-its-secondary-offering#:~:text=Viking%20Announces%20Pricing%20of%20its%20Secondary%20Offering%20LOS%20ANGELES--%28BUSINESS,BofA%20Securities%20are%20acting%20as%20underwriters%20for%20the%20offering.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250723223224/https://ir.viking.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/190/viking-announces-launch-of-secondary-offering-of-ordinary-shares#:~:text=Viking%20Announces%20Launch%20of%20Secondary%20Offering%20of%20Ordinary%20Shares,Securities%20are%20acting%20as%20underwriters%20for%20the%20proposed%20offering.)

## Evidence

The sale left the controlling block untouched. As of May 1, 2025, Viking Capital Limited held approximately 87% of the votes through its ordinary and special shares. Neither the block nor the total votes changed when CPPIB and TPG transferred ordinary shares to buyers. The filing therefore supports continuity of control, including over director elections. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250703175029/https://ir.viking.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001193125-25-129504/d884654d424b7.htm#:~:text=Our%20Principal%20Shareholder%20As%20of%20May%201%2C%202025%2C%20Viking,within%20the%20meaning%20of%20the%20rules%20of%20the%20NYSE.) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250703175029/https://ir.viking.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001193125-25-129504/d884654d424b7.htm#:~:text=Our%20Financial%20Shareholders%20In%20this%20prospectus%20supplement%20and%20the,voting%20power%20of%20our%20issued%20and%20outstanding%20share%20capital.)

Moving a large sponsor block into public hands likely increased the supply available for trading, but better trading liquidity is not an observed result. The completed placement demonstrates demand for the block at the offer price; it does not show how widely the buyers dispersed the shares or how cheaply investors could trade afterward. A sustained narrowing of bid–ask spreads and greater quoted depth relative to the pre-offering market would support a liquidity improvement more convincingly than a burst of volume around the sale. Those trading data are unavailable here. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250722150855/https://www.ropesgray.com/en/news-and-events/news/2025/06/viking-holdings-closes-on-secondary-public-offering#:~:text=Ropes%20%26%20Gray%20represented%20selling%20shareholders%20TPG%20Capital%20and,selling%20shareholders%20in%20Viking%E2%80%99s%20IPO%20and%202024%20secondary%20offering.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250723223341/https://ir.viking.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/191/viking-announces-pricing-of-its-secondary-offering#:~:text=Viking%20Announces%20Pricing%20of%20its%20Secondary%20Offering%20LOS%20ANGELES--%28BUSINESS,BofA%20Securities%20are%20acting%20as%20underwriters%20for%20the%20offering.)

## Outlook

The base case is a meaningful potential seller, not an imminent sale or a threat to control. Assuming all proposed shares sold, the May prospectus put TPG’s remaining holding at zero and CPPIB’s at 31,344,744 ordinary shares—9.939 of the 315,371,680 ordinary shares outstanding on March 31, 2025, but only approximately 2.0% of voting power across both classes. That residual was comparable in size to the entire May placement. It matters to the price buyers might demand for another block, even though it matters little to governance. The prospectus estimate is not a verified cutoff-date balance or a commitment to sell. [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250703175029/https://ir.viking.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001193125-25-129504/d884654d424b7.htm#:~:text=Our%20Financial%20Shareholders%20In%20this%20prospectus%20supplement%20and%20the,voting%20power%20of%20our%20issued%20and%20outstanding%20share%20capital.) [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20250703175029/https://ir.viking.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001193125-25-129504/d884654d424b7.htm#:~:text=Unless%20otherwise%20stated%2C%20the%20number%20of%20shares%20to%20be,condition%20was%20not%20satisfied%20as%20of%20March%2031%2C%202025%3B) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250723223341/https://ir.viking.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/191/viking-announces-pricing-of-its-secondary-offering#:~:text=Viking%20Announces%20Pricing%20of%20its%20Secondary%20Offering%20LOS%20ANGELES--%28BUSINESS,BofA%20Securities%20are%20acting%20as%20underwriters%20for%20the%20offering.)

## Checked calculations

- C1. CPPIB residual if all May offering shares sold, as a share of ordinary shares on the March 31 prospectus base (percent of ordinary shares) — 31,344,744 ÷ 315,371,680 × 100 ≈ 9.938985 [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250703175029/https://ir.viking.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001193125-25-129504/d884654d424b7.htm#:~:text=Our%20Financial%20Shareholders%20In%20this%20prospectus%20supplement%20and%20the,voting%20power%20of%20our%20issued%20and%20outstanding%20share%20capital.) [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20250703175029/https://ir.viking.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001193125-25-129504/d884654d424b7.htm#:~:text=Unless%20otherwise%20stated%2C%20the%20number%20of%20shares%20to%20be,condition%20was%20not%20satisfied%20as%20of%20March%2031%2C%202025%3B)

question: How does the execution of Phong Le's '21-21 plan' and the introduction of Bitcoin-centric KPIs impact MicroStrategy's (MSTR) valuation premium relative to its underlying asset holdings, especially given recent insider activity and the market's evolving view of MSTR as a Bitcoin proxy?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-06-17

**Research question**
How does the execution of Phong Le's '21-21 plan' and the introduction of Bitcoin-centric KPIs impact MicroStrategy's (MSTR) valuation premium relative to its underlying asset holdings, especially given recent insider activity and the market's evolving view of MSTR as a Bitcoin proxy?

## Answer

As of 2025-06-17, the stronger explanation for MSTR’s premium is demand for leveraged Bitcoin exposure and the value of being able to sell common shares above NAV—not demonstrated, repeatable growth in bitcoin per diluted share. Under CEO Phong Le and executive chairman Michael Saylor, who leads Bitcoin acquisition strategy, Strategy had sold the full $21B common-stock allotment of its 21/21 plan by May 2025. That establishes that investors would fund purchases at scale. It does not establish what each diluted share gained or how large a premium those gains warrant. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1295020656) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250603045904/https://www.vaneck.com/us/en/blogs/digital-assets/matthew-sigel-deconstructing-strategy-mstr-premium-leverage-and-capital-structure/#:~:text=In%20October%202024%2C%20Strategy%20announced%20the%20ambitious%2021%2F21%20capital,debt%20offerings.%2042%2F42%20Capital%20Raising%20Plan%20-%2032%25%20Complete) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250603045904/https://www.vaneck.com/us/en/blogs/digital-assets/matthew-sigel-deconstructing-strategy-mstr-premium-leverage-and-capital-structure/#:~:text=From%20a%20strategic%20standpoint%2C%20Strategy%20offers%20several%20key%20lessons,without%20relying%20solely%20on%20traditional%20debt%20or%20equity%20issuance.)

## Evidence

The Bitcoin-centric KPI asks the right dilution question: did the coins attributable to each diluted share increase? From August 2024 to May 2025, holdings rose from 226,000 BTC to 555,450 BTC, a period that begins before the plan’s October 2024 announcement. Those are treasury balances, not per-share results. The evidence lacks matched diluted-share counts at the endpoints and a same-date common-equity valuation and net asset reconciliation at the cutoff. Neither realized per-share growth nor the precise premium can be calculated from it. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250603045904/https://www.vaneck.com/us/en/blogs/digital-assets/matthew-sigel-deconstructing-strategy-mstr-premium-leverage-and-capital-structure/#:~:text=From%20a%20strategic%20standpoint%2C%20Strategy%20offers%20several%20key%20lessons,without%20relying%20solely%20on%20traditional%20debt%20or%20equity%20issuance.) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250603045904/https://www.vaneck.com/us/en/blogs/digital-assets/matthew-sigel-deconstructing-strategy-mstr-premium-leverage-and-capital-structure/#:~:text=While%20Strategy%E2%80%99s%20core%20business%20generates%20some%20operational%20income%2C%20its,offerings%2C%20a%20bear%20market%20could%20prove%20challenging%20for%20Strategy.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250603045904/https://www.vaneck.com/us/en/blogs/digital-assets/matthew-sigel-deconstructing-strategy-mstr-premium-leverage-and-capital-structure/#:~:text=In%20October%202024%2C%20Strategy%20announced%20the%20ambitious%2021%2F21%20capital,debt%20offerings.%2042%2F42%20Capital%20Raising%20Plan%20-%2032%25%20Complete)

MSTR’s appeal has shifted from access to the form of exposure. An earlier account called it a quasi-Bitcoin ETF when no US spot ETF was available; US spot funds began trading in January 2024. Investors no longer need MSTR simply to hold exchange-traded Bitcoin exposure. MSTR instead offers common equity behind debt and preferred claims, plus an active options market. VanEck’s reported options activity supports demand to trade that volatility, though open interest is not a measure of bullish conviction. [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250524141838/https://markets.businessinsider.com/news/stocks/microstrategy-bitcoin-margin-call-21000-crypto-loan-mstr-stock-price-2022-5#:~:text=In%20March%2C%20MicroStrategy%20took%20out%20a%20%24205%20million%20bitcoin-collateralized,no%20true%20bitcoin%20ETF%20yet%20approved%20in%20the%20US.) [6](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1295331723) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250603045904/https://www.vaneck.com/us/en/blogs/digital-assets/matthew-sigel-deconstructing-strategy-mstr-premium-leverage-and-capital-structure/#:~:text=From%20a%20strategic%20standpoint%2C%20Strategy%20offers%20several%20key%20lessons,without%20relying%20solely%20on%20traditional%20debt%20or%20equity%20issuance.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250603045904/https://www.vaneck.com/us/en/blogs/digital-assets/matthew-sigel-deconstructing-strategy-mstr-premium-leverage-and-capital-structure/#:~:text=In%20October%202024%2C%20Strategy%20announced%20the%20ambitious%2021%2F21%20capital,debt%20offerings.%2042%2F42%20Capital%20Raising%20Plan%20-%2032%25%20Complete)

Recent insider activity is an unverified question premise, not a valuation signal on this record. The documented June sales raised capital for Strategy; they were not reported as personal disposals by Le or Saylor. Without dated insider filings showing the seller, size relative to holdings and whether trades were prearranged, there is no basis to infer a change in management’s conviction. [7](https://web.archive.org/web/20250617103511/https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2025/06/16/strategy-adds-over-10k-btc-to-its-bitcoin-treasury-funded-by-strd-offering#:~:text=To%20finance%20the%20purchase%2C%20Strategy%20recently%20completed%20its%2010%25,1.60%25in%20pre-market%20hours%2C%20while%20bitcoin%20is%20holding%20near%20%24107%2C000.)

A premium can help Strategy increase common NAV per share; the ability to use it is not proof that past gains justify it. When Strategy sells common shares for net proceeds above pre-issue common NAV per share and buys bitcoin, common NAV per share rises, all else equal. Gross BTC per diluted share rises only if each new share buys more bitcoin than a diluted share previously represented. The expansion to $84B on May 1, 2025 increased financing capacity, not realized gains. The STRD preferred offering illustrates the distinction: it netted approximately $979.7 million. Investing those proceeds in bitcoin can raise gross BTC per diluted share without issuing common stock, but the preferred holders have a claim ahead of common holders. The gross KPI does not deduct that claim. [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250603045904/https://www.vaneck.com/us/en/blogs/digital-assets/matthew-sigel-deconstructing-strategy-mstr-premium-leverage-and-capital-structure/#:~:text=In%20October%202024%2C%20Strategy%20announced%20the%20ambitious%2021%2F21%20capital,debt%20offerings.%2042%2F42%20Capital%20Raising%20Plan%20-%2032%25%20Complete) [7](https://web.archive.org/web/20250617103511/https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2025/06/16/strategy-adds-over-10k-btc-to-its-bitcoin-treasury-funded-by-strd-offering#:~:text=To%20finance%20the%20purchase%2C%20Strategy%20recently%20completed%20its%2010%25,1.60%25in%20pre-market%20hours%2C%20while%20bitcoin%20is%20holding%20near%20%24107%2C000.)

## Outlook

Base case: the premium narrows if demand for leveraged exposure fades, because a lower issue price also reduces what Strategy can earn for existing holders on the next common sale. Watch net common issuance prices relative to contemporaneous common NAV and the pace of purchases as that spread narrows. Financing slowed sharply in the earlier crypto downturn, while preferred dividends now add a funding need; paying STRK dividends in common shares would itself dilute BTC per share. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250603045904/https://www.vaneck.com/us/en/blogs/digital-assets/matthew-sigel-deconstructing-strategy-mstr-premium-leverage-and-capital-structure/#:~:text=While%20Strategy%E2%80%99s%20core%20business%20generates%20some%20operational%20income%2C%20its,offerings%2C%20a%20bear%20market%20could%20prove%20challenging%20for%20Strategy.)

## What would change the view

The strongest alternative is that Strategy has a durable financing advantage: investors value the options embedded in its securities enough to fund purchases on favorable terms even at a modest common-stock premium. The persuasive signal would be sustained growth in both BTC per diluted share and common NAV per share measured in BTC through a period of narrow issuance premiums. Reconcile conversions, senior claims, interest and dividends in that comparison. If gains survive those adjustments and are large enough to cover the premium an investor pays, the case for a sustained premium would rest on results rather than on the next buyer’s willingness to pay one. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250603045904/https://www.vaneck.com/us/en/blogs/digital-assets/matthew-sigel-deconstructing-strategy-mstr-premium-leverage-and-capital-structure/#:~:text=From%20a%20strategic%20standpoint%2C%20Strategy%20offers%20several%20key%20lessons,without%20relying%20solely%20on%20traditional%20debt%20or%20equity%20issuance.) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250603045904/https://www.vaneck.com/us/en/blogs/digital-assets/matthew-sigel-deconstructing-strategy-mstr-premium-leverage-and-capital-structure/#:~:text=While%20Strategy%E2%80%99s%20core%20business%20generates%20some%20operational%20income%2C%20its,offerings%2C%20a%20bear%20market%20could%20prove%20challenging%20for%20Strategy.)

## Sources

1. [MicroStrategy](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1295020656), available by 2025-06-11.
2. [Deconstructing Strategy (MSTR): Premium, Leverage, and Capital Structure | VanEck](https://web.archive.org/web/20250603045904/https://www.vaneck.com/us/en/blogs/digital-assets/matthew-sigel-deconstructing-strategy-mstr-premium-leverage-and-capital-structure/#:~:text=In%20October%202024%2C%20Strategy%20announced%20the%20ambitious%2021%2F21%20capital,debt%20offerings.%2042%2F42%20Capital%20Raising%20Plan%20-%2032%25%20Complete), available by 2025-06-03.
3. [Deconstructing Strategy (MSTR): Premium, Leverage, and Capital Structure | VanEck](https://web.archive.org/web/20250603045904/https://www.vaneck.com/us/en/blogs/digital-assets/matthew-sigel-deconstructing-strategy-mstr-premium-leverage-and-capital-structure/#:~:text=From%20a%20strategic%20standpoint%2C%20Strategy%20offers%20several%20key%20lessons,without%20relying%20solely%20on%20traditional%20debt%20or%20equity%20issuance.), available by 2025-06-03.
4. question: Given the significant institutional accumulation of StoneCo Ltd. (STNE) and its 66% year-to-date outperformance through May 2025, how do diverging analyst price targets and exceptionally low PEG ratios (0.36–0.41) signal its relative competitive positioning and valuation sustainability against Brazilian fintech peers like PagSeguro and DLocal?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-05-21

**Research question**
Given the significant institutional accumulation of StoneCo Ltd. (STNE) and its 66% year-to-date outperformance through May 2025, how do diverging analyst price targets and exceptionally low PEG ratios (0.36–0.41) signal its relative competitive positioning and valuation sustainability against Brazilian fintech peers like PagSeguro and DLocal?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-05-21, StoneCo has demonstrated growth, but not a durable valuation discount to PagSeguro or dLocal. In the latest quarter, adjusted net income rose 23.1% year over year, while adjusted basic EPS rose 35.6%, helped by repurchases. The distinction matters: a low PEG is less persuasive if it relies on per-share earnings continuing to grow faster than the business. My base case is that StoneCo’s growth is real but its apparent cheapness is forecast-dependent, not evidence of a competitive advantage over either peer. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250513013629/https://www.panabee.com/news/stoneco-q1-earnings-2025#:~:text=StoneCo%20reported%20a%20robust%20start%20to%202025%2C%20with%20overall,revenue%20growth%20was%201.7%25%20Q%2FQ%2C%20also%20aided%20by%20repricing.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250512123151/https://api.mziq.com/mzfilemanager/v2/d/46ed7b29-1318-408a-a036-ba544e2ecccb/a4f36e19-fb7a-9848-1d83-442ef5534748?origin=1#:~:text=tax%20rate%20during%20the%20period.%20o%20Adjusted%20Basic%20EPS,3%2C676.2%2017.1%25%20Key%20Accounts%2053.3%2052.3%202.0%25%2051.9%202.6%25)

## Evidence

The strongest operating evidence for the bull case is that StoneCo is winning more small merchants and drawing them into banking. Small-merchant payment volume rose 17.2% year over year, and active banking clients grew 36.2%. StoneCo says that when customers switch from debit to Pix QR, it earns a comparable net merchant fee while increasing use of the banking account. That is a plausible advantage of selling payments and banking together, though without peer retention or merchant profitability data it does not establish superiority. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250512123151/https://api.mziq.com/mzfilemanager/v2/d/46ed7b29-1318-408a-a036-ba544e2ecccb/a4f36e19-fb7a-9848-1d83-442ef5534748?origin=1#:~:text=MSMB%20%28Micro%20and%20SMB%20clients%29%20o%20MSMB%20TPV%20was,of%20our%20retail%20deposits%20was%20as%20follows%3A%20%E2%96%AA%20Deposits)

## Outlook

I would not extrapolate the latest EPS growth rate. It exceeded adjusted net income growth by 12.5 percentage points, helped by R$2.4 billion of repurchases over the prior year. Meanwhile, adjusted pretax margin improved year over year but fell -2.8 percentage points on a signed quarter-over-quarter basis: funding costs rose before merchant repricing fully caught up. If that lag persists or repurchases slow, EPS growth could disappoint even as revenue rises. At an unchanged P/E, a lower growth forecast alone raises the PEG. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250513013629/https://www.panabee.com/news/stoneco-q1-earnings-2025#:~:text=StoneCo%20reported%20a%20robust%20start%20to%202025%2C%20with%20overall,revenue%20growth%20was%201.7%25%20Q%2FQ%2C%20also%20aided%20by%20repricing.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250512123151/https://api.mziq.com/mzfilemanager/v2/d/46ed7b29-1318-408a-a036-ba544e2ecccb/a4f36e19-fb7a-9848-1d83-442ef5534748?origin=1#:~:text=tax%20rate%20during%20the%20period.%20o%20Adjusted%20Basic%20EPS,3%2C676.2%2017.1%25%20Key%20Accounts%2053.3%2052.3%202.0%25%2051.9%202.6%25) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250512123151/https://api.mziq.com/mzfilemanager/v2/d/46ed7b29-1318-408a-a036-ba544e2ecccb/a4f36e19-fb7a-9848-1d83-442ef5534748?origin=1#:~:text=StoneCo%20Reports%20First%20Quarter%202025%20Results%20George%20Town%2C%20Grand,and%20partially%20offset%20by%20seasonally%20lower%20administrative%20expenses.%20o)

## What would change the view

The strongest alternative is that the margin squeeze is temporary: repricing catches up, time deposits lower funding costs, and overdue loans stabilize as the credit portfolio matures. The share of loans more than 90 days past due rose 0.96 percentage points sequentially, so stabilization is a test, not an assumption. A pretax margin recovery alongside stable arrears and sustained net income growth without heavy buybacks would make the growth forecast more credible. A durable relative discount would still require a lower PEG than both peers on matched estimates; a rising share price alone would not change that judgment. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250512123151/https://api.mziq.com/mzfilemanager/v2/d/46ed7b29-1318-408a-a036-ba544e2ecccb/a4f36e19-fb7a-9848-1d83-442ef5534748?origin=1#:~:text=StoneCo%20Reports%20First%20Quarter%202025%20Results%20George%20Town%2C%20Grand,and%20partially%20offset%20by%20seasonally%20lower%20administrative%20expenses.%20o) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250512123151/https://api.mziq.com/mzfilemanager/v2/d/46ed7b29-1318-408a-a036-ba544e2ecccb/a4f36e19-fb7a-9848-1d83-442ef5534748?origin=1#:~:text=MSMB%20%28Micro%20and%20SMB%20clients%29%20o%20MSMB%20TPV%20was,of%20our%20retail%20deposits%20was%20as%20follows%3A%20%E2%96%AA%20Deposits) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250512123151/https://api.mziq.com/mzfilemanager/v2/d/46ed7b29-1318-408a-a036-ba544e2ecccb/a4f36e19-fb7a-9848-1d83-442ef5534748?origin=1#:~:text=Table%204%3A%20Credit%201%20o%20In%201Q25%2C%20our%20total,%282.2%29%20%288.3%29%20%2873.6%25%29%20%280.4%29%20393.3%25%20Coverage%20ratio%20256.3%25%20331.2%25)

## Checked calculations

- C1. 1Q25 YoY adjusted EPS growth minus adjusted net income growth; buybacks helped widen this gap (percentage points) — 35.6 − 23.1 = 12.5 [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250513013629/https://www.panabee.com/news/stoneco-q1-earnings-2025#:~:text=StoneCo%20reported%20a%20robust%20start%20to%202025%2C%20with%20overall,revenue%20growth%20was%201.7%25%20Q%2FQ%2C%20also%20aided%20by%20repricing.)
- C2. 1Q25 versus 4Q24 change in adjusted pretax margin; funding costs rose ahead of repricing (percentage points) — 18.8 − 21.6 = -2.8 [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250512123151/https://api.mziq.com/mzfilemanager/v2/d/46ed7b29-1318-408a-a036-ba544e2ecccb/a4f36e19-fb7a-9848-1d83-442ef5534748?origin=1#:~:text=StoneCo%20Reports%20First%20Quarter%202025%20Results%20George%20Town%2C%20Grand,and%20partially%20offset%20by%20seasonally%20lower%20administrative%20expenses.%20o)
- C3. 1Q25 versus 4Q24 change in the share of the credit portfolio over 90 days past due (percentage points) — 4.57 − 3.61 = 0.96 [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250512123151/https://api.mziq.com/mzfilemanager/v2/d/46ed7b29-1318-408a-a036-ba544e2ecccb/a4f36e19-fb7a-9848-1d83-442ef5534748?origin=1#:~:text=Table%204%3A%20Credit%201%20o%20In%201Q25%2C%20our%20total,%282.2%29%20%288.3%29%20%2873.6%25%29%20%280.4%29%20393.3%25%20Coverage%20ratio%20256.3%25%20331.2%25)
