question: Given the significant divestment by Wellington Management alongside accumulation by Price T Rowe, how do Exelon’s shifting ownership, recent price target upgrades by major banks, and outperformance relative to the XLU index indicate a potential fundamental re-rating or a momentum-driven peak for the company?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-05-21

**Research question**
Given the significant divestment by Wellington Management alongside accumulation by Price T Rowe, how do Exelon’s shifting ownership, recent price target upgrades by major banks, and outperformance relative to the XLU index indicate a potential fundamental re-rating or a momentum-driven peak for the company?

## Answer

As of 2025-05-21, I would not pay a valuation premium for Exelon on the evidence provided. Wellington Management’s reported sale, Price T Rowe’s reported accumulation, major banks’ target increases and Exelon’s outperformance of XLU are all unverified question premises. Neither the size of the trades nor the return spread is established. Exelon’s separation from its generation business makes regulated earnings the right place to look for support; it does not establish a durable re-rating or a momentum peak. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1288944724) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250430113218/https://brandsownedby.com/list-of-companies-owned-by-t-rowe-price/#:~:text=Wellington%20Management%20Group%20LLP%20%E2%80%93%202.85%25%20Ownership%20Wellington%20Management%2C,firm%E2%80%99s%20future%20growth.%20Insiders%20and%20Executives%20%E2%80%93%2010.48%25%20Ownership)

## Evidence

The ownership evidence concerns the wrong securities. Wellington’s 2.85% stake is in T. Rowe Price, not Exelon, and the cited T. Rowe Price portfolio excerpt identifies Microsoft and Apple, not an Exelon purchase. To verify the shifts, compare each manager’s Exelon share count across the same consecutive quarter ends and measure the change against its starting position. Even confirmed opposite trades would show a change in exposure, not either manager’s motive or its position at the cutoff: the filings are lagged snapshots. [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250430113218/https://brandsownedby.com/list-of-companies-owned-by-t-rowe-price/#:~:text=Wellington%20Management%20Group%20LLP%20%E2%80%93%202.85%25%20Ownership%20Wellington%20Management%2C,firm%E2%80%99s%20future%20growth.%20Insiders%20and%20Executives%20%E2%80%93%2010.48%25%20Ownership) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250430113218/https://brandsownedby.com/list-of-companies-owned-by-t-rowe-price/#:~:text=1.%20Microsoft%20Corporation%20%28MSFT%29%20Microsoft%20Corporation%20is%20a%20leading,about%2011.76%25%20of%20its%20portfolio%2C%20totaling%2024%2C361%2C223%20shares.%20%E2%80%8B) [4](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1223018657)

The supplied financial-news excerpts do not verify a bank target change: they contain a reporting credit and unrelated headlines, not a dated Exelon analyst note. Before counting an upgrade as independent support, identify the bank, its prior and revised targets, and what changed in its forecast. A higher target based on higher regulated earnings estimates would support the fundamental case; the same increase based solely on a richer multiple would restate the valuation judgment rather than validate it. [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250424233754/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-constellation-exelon-idUSTRE73Q8BS20110428/#:~:text=Reporting%20by%20Krishna%20N%20Das%20in%20Bangalore%3B%20Editing%20by,kills%2012%20in%20Kyiv11%3A07%20PM%20UTC%20%C2%B7%20Updated%20ago) [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20250424233754/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-constellation-exelon-idUSTRE73Q8BS20110428/#:~:text=Asia%20PacificcategoryChina%20military%20says%20it%20monitored%20US%20warship%20in,top%20aviation%20safety%20rating10%3A42%20PM%20UTC%20%C2%B7%20Updated%20ago)

## What would change the view

My base case is to withhold judgment on a premium, not to call a top. First verify the claimed lead using dividend-adjusted returns for Exelon and XLU from a common start date through 2025-05-21; the supplied material has no matched return series. Then compare the change in Exelon’s forward earnings multiple relative to utility peers with revisions to its regulated earnings outlook. The strongest case for a durable premium would be rate approvals that raise expected earnings relative to peers, followed by results that deliver those gains. A widening premium with unchanged earnings expectations would favor momentum, though it would not date a peak. This test belongs to the transmission and distribution business, not the former generation fleet. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1288944724)

question: Despite Zebra Technologies beating Q1 EPS estimates and receiving significant capital inflows from Norges Bank and GAMMA Investing, major analysts like Truist and Barclays sharply reduced price targets in June 2025. What underlying debt-to-equity risks and segment growth decelerations justify this bearish shift in valuation?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-06-10

**Research question**
Despite Zebra Technologies beating Q1 EPS estimates and receiving significant capital inflows from Norges Bank and GAMMA Investing, major analysts like Truist and Barclays sharply reduced price targets in June 2025. What underlying debt-to-equity risks and segment growth decelerations justify this bearish shift in valuation?

## Answer

As of 2025-06-10, the supplied record does not verify that Truist or Barclays cut its ZBRA price target between the start of June and the cutoff. Neither the size of either reported cut nor its rationale is established. The passages document a retail product showcase and past acquisitions, not analyst actions. That leaves the June timing unconfirmed, not disproved. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250306102900/https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/zebra-technologies-to-unveil-new-solutions-at-nrf-2024-advancing-the-modern-store#:~:text=Company%20will%20showcase%20solutions%20that%20empower%20retailers%20to%20elevate,providing%20the%20agility%20needed%20to%20adapt%20for%20the%20future.) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1280238497)

## Evidence

Leverage could justify a lower equity valuation if debt obligations left shareholders more exposed to a decline in operating cash flow. But the $3.45 billion Motorola enterprise transaction was an acquisition price, not a current debt balance. The record gives neither current debt nor book equity, so it cannot establish a high or rising debt-to-equity ratio. Interest coverage and cash flow would help distinguish genuine repayment pressure from a ratio elevated by a small equity base. [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1280238497)

Slower segment sales growth could warrant lower forward earnings estimates even after a quarterly EPS beat, but product announcements are not sales results. The record lacks comparable segment growth rates across successive quarters. The reported Q1 EPS beat and significant inflows from Norges Bank and GAMMA Investing are unverified question premises. Even confirmed purchases of existing shares would not put cash on Zebra’s balance sheet or reduce its debt. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250306102900/https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/zebra-technologies-to-unveil-new-solutions-at-nrf-2024-advancing-the-modern-store#:~:text=Engage%20Associates%20to%20Drive%20Productivity%20Eight%20in%2010%20retail,cost%20of%20lost%20devices%20and%20driving%20productivity%20for%20retailers.) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250306102900/https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/zebra-technologies-to-unveil-new-solutions-at-nrf-2024-advancing-the-modern-store#:~:text=Launching%20at%20NRF%2C%20the%20new%20AI-powered%20Workcloud%20Modeling%20Studio,visibility%20to%20maximize%20accuracy%20without%20an%20expensive%20infrastructure%20investment.)

## What would change the view

The base case is to make no valuation adjustment on these claims alone. The strongest bearish alternative is that slowing demand reduced expected operating cash flow while debt service remained fixed. Sustained declines in comparable segment growth and weakening interest coverage would support that interpretation; stable growth and improving coverage would weaken it. To settle the separate timing and attribution questions, look for each broker’s dated note, prior and revised targets, and stated reasons: a June recap of an earlier action would not establish a June cut. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250306102900/https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/zebra-technologies-to-unveil-new-solutions-at-nrf-2024-advancing-the-modern-store#:~:text=Company%20will%20showcase%20solutions%20that%20empower%20retailers%20to%20elevate,providing%20the%20agility%20needed%20to%20adapt%20for%20the%20future.) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1280238497)

question: How did the unexpected Q1 2025 U.S. economic contraction reported by the Bureau of Economic Analysis, characterized by record trade-related drags and softening consumer spending, recalibrate growth forecasts and interest rate expectations for the remainder of 2025?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-06-10

**Research question**
How did the unexpected Q1 2025 U.S. economic contraction reported by the Bureau of Economic Analysis, characterized by record trade-related drags and softening consumer spending, recalibrate growth forecasts and interest rate expectations for the remainder of 2025?

## Answer

As of 2025-06-10, the available evidence does not establish that professional forecasters cut their growth estimates for the rest of 2025 or that traders priced in earlier or deeper Fed cuts. Neither the direction nor the size of either revision is documented. The unexpected contraction, record trade drag and softer spending are unverified question premises. The investment distinction is whether the report lowered the starting level of output or also changed the expected pace of growth. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1283573385) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1169493481) [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1285063953)

## Evidence

A lower full-year forecast would not, by itself, show that forecasters had become more pessimistic about the remaining quarters. A weaker first quarter can lower average output for the year even if subsequent quarterly growth rates are unchanged. The relevant test is to compare the same forecasters’ quarter-by-quarter estimates before and after the release. The material describes the Philadelphia Fed survey but supplies neither set of estimates; later downgrades alone would not isolate the report’s effect. [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1169493481)

The late-April market reaction and the June outlook require separate comparisons. Meeting-specific fed funds futures prices immediately before and after the release would show whether traders brought the first expected cut forward. The implied year-end rate would show whether they also expected more easing overall. Comparing those post-release prices with prices on 2025-06-10 would test whether the move lasted, not whether GDP caused every intervening change. The material identifies the Fed’s policy target but supplies no prices for any of those observations. [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1285063953)

## Outlook

Conditional on the question’s premises, a temporary import surge is the more plausible explanation for the headline contraction; weaker consumption is the stronger reason to cut the forward growth outlook. Imports are subtracted to exclude foreign production already counted in spending, while slower consumption growth can still contribute positively to GDP. The import-led base case predicts a rebound as imports normalize, with real purchases by domestic consumers and businesses continuing to grow. The strongest alternative is persistent demand weakness: spending would remain weak even after the trade drag fades. The BEA description supplies neither component contributions to rank the initial drags nor subsequent spending data to decide between those paths. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1283573385)

## Sources

1. [Bureau of Economic Analysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1283573385), available by 2025-04-02.
2. [Survey of Professional Forecasters](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1169493481), available by 2023-08-09.
3. [Federal Open Market Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1285063953), available by 2025-04-11.

question: How does Robert Ohmes' significant mid-2025 downward revision of Target Corporation (TGT) price targets signal a broader shift in BofA's consumer retail outlook, particularly when contrasted with his earlier 2025 bullishness on Walmart (WMT) and Sprouts Farmers Market (SFM)?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-08-05

**Research question**
How does Robert Ohmes' significant mid-2025 downward revision of Target Corporation (TGT) price targets signal a broader shift in BofA's consumer retail outlook, particularly when contrasted with his earlier 2025 bullishness on Walmart (WMT) and Sprouts Farmers Market (SFM)?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Evidence

Ohmes’s reported rationale centered on how weak sales could erode Target’s margins: a delayed recovery in comparable sales would mean more markdowns, while tariffs added pressure. Target’s own results give that concern context. Adjusted earnings per share fell to $1.30 from $2.03 a year earlier, even as GAAP earnings rose to $2.27. Target also lowered its full-year adjusted earnings guidance. That was management’s forecast revision, distinct from Ohmes’s stock call. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250720161512/https://www.benzinga.com/analyst-ratings/analyst-color/25/05/45573176/target-under-pressure-from-tariffs-rising-competitive-gaps-analysts#:~:text=Ongoing%20margin%20pressures%20are%20likely%2C%20and%20he%20flags%20increased,vacation%20rentals%20for%20as%20little%20as%20%24100.%20Get%20Started) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250722050740/https://corporate.target.com/press/release/2025/05/target-corporation-reports-first-quarter-earnings#:~:text=For%20additional%20media%20materials%2C%20please%20visit%3A%20https%3A%2F%2Fcorporate.target.com%2Fnews-features%2Farticle%2F2025%2F05%2Fq1-2025-earnings%20Target%20Corporation,All%20earnings%20per%20share%20figures%20refer%20to%20diluted%20EPS.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250720161512/https://www.benzinga.com/analyst-ratings/analyst-color/25/05/45573176/target-under-pressure-from-tariffs-rising-competitive-gaps-analysts#:~:text=The%20retail%20giant%20lowered%20its%20FY2025%20adjusted%20EPS%20guidance,Perform%2C%20decreasing%20the%20price%20forecast%20from%20%24130%20to%20%24110.)

## Outlook

The base case is selective pressure rather than uniform retail weakness. If Target’s comparable sales remain soft and markdowns weigh on margins while Walmart holds or gains share in overlapping categories, that would support a relative preference for Walmart. The share observation came from Telsey’s Joseph Feldman, not Ohmes; it makes the comparison plausible without verifying a BofA recommendation. There is no comparable evidence here for Sprouts. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250720161512/https://www.benzinga.com/analyst-ratings/analyst-color/25/05/45573176/target-under-pressure-from-tariffs-rising-competitive-gaps-analysts#:~:text=Ongoing%20margin%20pressures%20are%20likely%2C%20and%20he%20flags%20increased,vacation%20rentals%20for%20as%20little%20as%20%24100.%20Get%20Started)

## What would change the view

The strongest alternative is that tariffs and weak goods demand made Target an early example of a broader retail earnings squeeze. Yet a shared risk need not produce a shared downgrade: JPMorgan’s Horvers argued tariffs could shift share toward value retailers such as Walmart. Comparable cuts by Ohmes across retailers on the same demand or margin grounds would favor the broader interpretation; an explicit BofA sector-rating change would establish it directly. Dated Walmart and Sprouts notes showing Buy ratings before and after the Target cut would instead verify the widening preference. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250720161512/https://www.benzinga.com/analyst-ratings/analyst-color/25/05/45573176/target-under-pressure-from-tariffs-rising-competitive-gaps-analysts#:~:text=JP%20Morgan%3A%20Per%20Horvers%2C%20Target%20continues%20to%20hold%20relevance,Walmart%20Inc.%2C%20and%20Amazon.com%2C%20Inc.%20AMZN%29%2C%20the%20analyst%20notes.)

question: How does Ascentage Pharma's aggressive 2025 capital strategy, involving its U.S. IPO and subsequent oversubscribed Hong Kong placement, impact its ability to scale commercial operations for Lisaftoclax and Olverembatinib while funding a broad multi-asset clinical pipeline?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-08-20

**Research question**
How does Ascentage Pharma's aggressive 2025 capital strategy, involving its U.S. IPO and subsequent oversubscribed Hong Kong placement, impact its ability to scale commercial operations for Lisaftoclax and Olverembatinib while funding a broad multi-asset clinical pipeline?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-08-20, Ascentage Pharma’s closed U.S. IPO raised approximately $126.4 million gross. That gives Ascentage more room to launch lisaftoclax in China, expand sales of olverembatinib and keep priority trials moving. It does not establish that the commercial expansion and the full trial portfolio are funded. The base case is that the IPO buys time before another financing decision; the available evidence does not show when, or whether, another raise will be necessary. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250316051336/https://www.ascentage.com/ascentage-pharma-announces-closing-of-u-s-initial-public-offering/#:~:text=Ascentage%20Pharma%20Announces%20Closing%20of%20U.S.%20Initial%20Public%20Offering,Citigroup%20acted%20as%20joint%20book-running%20managers%20for%20the%20offering.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250804060852/https://www.ascentage.com/ascentage-pharma-announces-its-novel-bcl-2-inhibitor-lisaftoclax-approved-by-china-nmpa-ushering-in-a-new-era-for-the-treatment-of-cll-sll/#:~:text=Lisaftoclax%20is%20a%20proprietary%2C%20novel%20orally%20administered%20small-molecule%20Bcl-2,incidence%20of%20non-hematologic%20toxicities%20which%20were%20mostly%20grade%201-2.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250804060852/https://www.ascentage.com/ascentage-pharma-announces-its-novel-bcl-2-inhibitor-lisaftoclax-approved-by-china-nmpa-ushering-in-a-new-era-for-the-treatment-of-cll-sll/#:~:text=Ascentage%20Pharma%20%28NASDAQ%3A%20AAPG%3B%20HKEX%3A%206855%29%20is%20a%20global,study%20in%20patients%20with%20newly%20diagnosed%20higher%20risk%20MDS.)

## Evidence

Count only the closed IPO, and distinguish its size from spendable cash. Ascentage sold 7,325,000 ADSs at $17.25 per ADS; the gross figure excludes fees and expenses, and the underwriters’ option was granted, not confirmed exercised. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250316051336/https://www.ascentage.com/ascentage-pharma-announces-closing-of-u-s-initial-public-offering/#:~:text=Ascentage%20Pharma%20Announces%20Closing%20of%20U.S.%20Initial%20Public%20Offering,Citigroup%20acted%20as%20joint%20book-running%20managers%20for%20the%20offering.) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250316051336/https://www.ascentage.com/ascentage-pharma-announces-closing-of-u-s-initial-public-offering/#:~:text=Ascentage%20Pharma%20is%20a%20global%2C%20integrated%20biopharmaceutical%20company%20engaged,Market%20under%20the%20ticker%20symbol%20%E2%80%9CAAPG%E2%80%9D%20since%20January%202025.)

The strongest commercial argument is that Ascentage need not build a hematology sales operation from scratch. Olverembatinib already has Chinese reimbursement coverage for its approved CML business; existing hospital relationships could lower the incremental cost of introducing lisaftoclax. But lisaftoclax’s July conditional approval is for previously treated CLL/SLL, including prior BTK inhibitor therapy. Olverembatinib’s reimbursement does not transfer to lisaftoclax, and marketing authorization alone establishes neither uptake nor cash collections. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250804060852/https://www.ascentage.com/ascentage-pharma-announces-its-novel-bcl-2-inhibitor-lisaftoclax-approved-by-china-nmpa-ushering-in-a-new-era-for-the-treatment-of-cll-sll/#:~:text=Ascentage%20Pharma%20%28NASDAQ%3A%20AAPG%3B%20HKEX%3A%206855%29%20is%20a%20global,study%20in%20patients%20with%20newly%20diagnosed%20higher%20risk%20MDS.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250804060852/https://www.ascentage.com/ascentage-pharma-announces-its-novel-bcl-2-inhibitor-lisaftoclax-approved-by-china-nmpa-ushering-in-a-new-era-for-the-treatment-of-cll-sll/#:~:text=Lisaftoclax%20is%20a%20proprietary%2C%20novel%20orally%20administered%20small-molecule%20Bcl-2,incidence%20of%20non-hematologic%20toxicities%20which%20were%20mostly%20grade%201-2.) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250804060852/https://www.ascentage.com/ascentage-pharma-announces-its-novel-bcl-2-inhibitor-lisaftoclax-approved-by-china-nmpa-ushering-in-a-new-era-for-the-treatment-of-cll-sll/#:~:text=Ascentage%20Pharma%20Announces%20Its%20Novel%20Bcl-2%20Inhibitor%20Lisaftoclax%20Approved,in%20China%2C%20and%20the%20second%20Bcl-2%20inhibitor%20approved%20globally.)

## Outlook

Trial breadth makes prioritization more credible than an across-the-board acceleration. Olverembatinib has global registrational studies in CML, Ph-positive ALL and SDH-deficient GIST, while lisaftoclax has 4 global registrational studies spanning CLL/SLL, AML and MDS. The base case would be supported if priority studies meet enrollment milestones while lower-priority expansion is staged or new capital is sought. Without unrestricted cash, operating cash burn and remaining trial commitments, there is no defensible estimate of how long the IPO can support both sales expansion and development. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250804060852/https://www.ascentage.com/ascentage-pharma-announces-its-novel-bcl-2-inhibitor-lisaftoclax-approved-by-china-nmpa-ushering-in-a-new-era-for-the-treatment-of-cll-sll/#:~:text=Ascentage%20Pharma%20%28NASDAQ%3A%20AAPG%3B%20HKEX%3A%206855%29%20is%20a%20global,study%20in%20patients%20with%20newly%20diagnosed%20higher%20risk%20MDS.)

## What would change the view

The strongest alternative is that additional equity and rising product cash receipts cover the launch and carry priority trials to their next milestones without another raise. First require a Hong Kong completion filing stating shares issued and net proceeds, and separate book-demand disclosure before accepting oversubscription. The decisive operating signal would be rising cash collections and narrowing operating cash burn while priority trials stay on schedule, with unrestricted cash sufficient for the remaining milestone budgets. A strong order book alone would not meet that test. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250316051336/https://www.ascentage.com/ascentage-pharma-announces-closing-of-u-s-initial-public-offering/#:~:text=Ascentage%20Pharma%20Announces%20Closing%20of%20U.S.%20Initial%20Public%20Offering,Citigroup%20acted%20as%20joint%20book-running%20managers%20for%20the%20offering.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250804060852/https://www.ascentage.com/ascentage-pharma-announces-its-novel-bcl-2-inhibitor-lisaftoclax-approved-by-china-nmpa-ushering-in-a-new-era-for-the-treatment-of-cll-sll/#:~:text=Lisaftoclax%20is%20a%20proprietary%2C%20novel%20orally%20administered%20small-molecule%20Bcl-2,incidence%20of%20non-hematologic%20toxicities%20which%20were%20mostly%20grade%201-2.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250804060852/https://www.ascentage.com/ascentage-pharma-announces-its-novel-bcl-2-inhibitor-lisaftoclax-approved-by-china-nmpa-ushering-in-a-new-era-for-the-treatment-of-cll-sll/#:~:text=Ascentage%20Pharma%20%28NASDAQ%3A%20AAPG%3B%20HKEX%3A%206855%29%20is%20a%20global,study%20in%20patients%20with%20newly%20diagnosed%20higher%20risk%20MDS.)

## Sources

[Ascentage Pharma Announces Closing of U.S. Initial Public Offering -](https://web.archive.org/web/20250316051336/https://www.ascentage.com/ascentage-pharma-announces-closing-of-u-s-initial-public-offering/#:~:text=Ascentage%20Pharma%20Announces%20Closing%20of%20U.S.%20Initial%20Public%20Offering,Citigroup%20acted%20as%20joint%20book-running%20managers%20for%20the%20offering.), available by 2025-03-16.

question: Despite Microsoft’s Azure reporting 33% revenue growth in FY25 Q3 driven by AI services, why has the options market exhibited persistent bearish sentiment through call sweeps at $400, $440, and $490 strikes? Does this suggest a valuation disconnect or anticipation of rising infrastructure costs?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-07-16

**Research question**
Despite Microsoft’s Azure reporting 33% revenue growth in FY25 Q3 driven by AI services, why has the options market exhibited persistent bearish sentiment through call sweeps at $400, $440, and $490 strikes? Does this suggest a valuation disconnect or anticipation of rising infrastructure costs?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

No. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250614215141/https://www.theocc.com/getmedia/a151a9ae-d784-4a15-bdeb-23a029f50b70/riskstoc.pdf#:~:text=7%20EXERCISE%20PRICE%20%E2%80%94%20In%20the%20case%20of%20a,market%20on%20which%20each%20series%20is%20traded%20before%20the) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1282937596)

## Evidence

Even a confirmed seller-initiated sweep would be ambiguous. Selling a previously purchased call removes upside exposure without opening a short position. Selling a call against shares can leave the investor net long, and a call sale paired with another option can have a different payoff from the sale in isolation. The strongest bearish alternative would be repeated sales opening new short-call positions without offsetting legs. [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1282937596)

The base case for Microsoft’s cloud business is that new capacity supported growth; its effect on profitability remains open. In the fiscal third quarter, Azure and other cloud services revenue grew 33% as reported and 35% in constant currency, with 16 points of growth from AI services. Microsoft also reported stronger non-AI enterprise growth and said AI capacity came online faster than expected. That explains how investment could lift sales, but revenue growth does not measure the cost of serving them. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250702033707/https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor/events/fy-2025/earnings-fy-2025-q3#:~:text=Next%2C%20the%20Intelligent%20Cloud%20segment.%20Revenue%20was%20%2426.8%20billion,reflective%20of%20the%20continued%20customer%20shift%20to%20cloud%20offerings.)

## Outlook

Infrastructure margin pressure is the better-grounded risk to monitor, not the better-established trading motive. Microsoft planned to invest $80 billion in AI and data centers in fiscal 2025. That annual investment plan is not a quarterly expense: margins could narrow if depreciation and operating costs rise faster than revenue from new capacity. A declining cloud gross margin that management attributes to those costs would support that case. Stable margins alongside a share-price decline relative to unchanged forward earnings estimates would favor the valuation alternative. The record supplies neither the margin trend nor a contemporaneous earnings multiple. [4](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1298945178) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250702033707/https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor/events/fy-2025/earnings-fy-2025-q3#:~:text=Next%2C%20the%20Intelligent%20Cloud%20segment.%20Revenue%20was%20%2426.8%20billion,reflective%20of%20the%20continued%20customer%20shift%20to%20cloud%20offerings.)

## What would change the view

To upgrade the flow from ambiguous to bearish, look for dated trades across sessions with contract sizes, expiries and execution prices relative to the bid and ask. Opening-sale records, checked against linked stock and option legs, would show whether traders repeatedly added net downside exposure. Rising open interest alone would not identify which side initiated the trades; even confirmed bearish exposure would not distinguish a valuation thesis from a margin thesis. [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1282937596)

## Sources

1. [Archived PDF](https://web.archive.org/web/20250614215141/https://www.theocc.com/getmedia/a151a9ae-d784-4a15-bdeb-23a029f50b70/riskstoc.pdf#:~:text=7%20EXERCISE%20PRICE%20%E2%80%94%20In%20the%20case%20of%20a,market%20on%20which%20each%20series%20is%20traded%20before%20the), available by 2025-06-14.
2. [Option (finance)](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1282937596), available by 2025-03-29.
3. [Microsoft Fiscal Year 2025 Third Quarter Earnings Conference Call](https://web.archive.org/web/20250702033707/https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor/events/fy-2025/earnings-fy-2025-q3#:~:text=Next%2C%20the%20Intelligent%20Cloud%20segment.%20Revenue%20was%20%2426.8%20billion,reflective%20of%20the%20continued%20customer%20shift%20to%20cloud%20offerings.), available by 2025-07-02.
4. [Microsoft Azure](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1298945178), available by 2025-07-05.

question: Given INEGI’s data on Mexico’s Q4 2024 GDP contraction and deteriorating business confidence, how will the 25% US tariffs scheduled for March 2025 impact Mexico’s near-term growth outlook and its critical bilateral trade in crude oil and corn?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-03-03

**Research question**
Given INEGI’s data on Mexico’s Q4 2024 GDP contraction and deteriorating business confidence, how will the 25% US tariffs scheduled for March 2025 impact Mexico’s near-term growth outlook and its critical bilateral trade in crude oil and corn?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-03-03, I would lower Mexico’s near-term growth forecast relative to a baseline that already reflects the weak fourth quarter but assumes no new tariff. The United States is the destination for nearly 80 percent of Mexican exports, so even a temporary duty could weaken orders, especially for manufacturers serving the U.S. market. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1277190848)

## Evidence

The fourth-quarter contraction and deteriorating business confidence described in the question belong in the starting forecast, not in the estimated cost of a duty that had yet to be collected. Confidence may already reflect some anticipation of tariffs. The incremental risk is that U.S. customers now reduce orders or Mexican firms defer investment beyond what that earlier weakness implied. The available INEGI material is a household survey, not the GDP or confidence release, so it cannot verify the size of either decline or isolate an anticipation effect. [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250303221708/https://www.inegi.org.mx/contenidos/saladeprensa/boletines/2023/ENIGH/ENIGH2022.pdf#:~:text=COMUNICACI%C3%93N%20SOCIAL%20Temas%20sobresalientes%20captados%20por%20la%20ENIGH%20%E2%80%A2,la%20ENIGH%202022%20se%20puede%20consultar%20en%3A%20https%3A%2F%2Fwww.inegi.org.mx%2Fcontenidos%2Fproductos%2Fprod_serv%2Fcontenidos%2Fespanol%2Fbvinegi%2Fproduc%20tos%2Fnueva_estruc%2F889463901204.pdf) [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1277190848)

Mexican crude entering the United States is directly exposed under the stated all-goods scenario. The U.S. importer would owe the duty; the cost to Mexico would depend on whether refiners absorb it, negotiate a lower price from Mexican sellers or switch suppliers. Lower export receipts need not mean lower Mexican real output if barrels can be sold elsewhere. The sources establish oil trade, but not a binding crude-specific rate, current shipment volumes or how readily refiners and exporters could redirect purchases and sales. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1277190848) [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1257939031)

U.S. corn entering Mexico crosses the border in the opposite direction and would not incur the U.S. import duty. A direct tariff cost for Mexican corn buyers would require a separate Mexican measure covering corn; a signal that Mexico might retaliate is not a product list. Without retaliation, a weaker peso could still make dollar-priced corn dearer. With it, higher feed costs could reach Mexican livestock producers while U.S. growers risk losing sales. Household cereal spending shows why food costs matter, but does not measure U.S. corn imports or predict retail price increases. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1277190848) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250303221708/https://www.inegi.org.mx/contenidos/saladeprensa/boletines/2023/ENIGH/ENIGH2022.pdf#:~:text=COMUNICADO%20DE%20PRENSA%20N%C3%9AM.%20420%2F23%2026%20DE%20JULIO%20DE,de%20M%C3%A9xico%20obtuvieron%20el%20mayor%20ingreso%20corriente%20promedio%20trimestral)

## What would change the view

The base case is slower growth, not necessarily another contraction: a broad duty sustained for long enough to affect orders should show up in weaker U.S.-bound manufacturing shipments and either wider discounts on Mexican crude or lower U.S. purchases. The strongest alternative is a delay or broad exemptions that leave trade largely intact. Check U.S. customs coverage and collections first, then orders, shipments and crude prices; a waiver accompanied by stable orders would favor removing the tariff-related cut while retaining the weak starting forecast. Count a corn duty only if Mexico publishes one. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1277190848)

question: How does the strengthening technology partnership and project backlog with Petrobras influence the margin trajectory and EBITDA growth of TechnipFMC's Subsea segment, given the segment's role in driving the company's recent earnings outperformance and beating consensus estimates?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-06-25

**Research question**
How does the strengthening technology partnership and project backlog with Petrobras influence the margin trajectory and EBITDA growth of TechnipFMC's Subsea segment, given the segment's role in driving the company's recent earnings outperformance and beating consensus estimates?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-06-25, keep TechnipFMC’s Subsea adjusted EBITDA and margin forecasts unchanged. One Petrobras award worth between $250 million and $500 million was designated for the third quarter of 2024 inbound orders. That is evidence of future work, not a new order in the latest quarter or a disclosed profit contribution. The partnership improves revenue visibility; it does not yet establish that Petrobras work will earn more per dollar of revenue than the projects it replaces. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250421022244/https://www.technipfmc.com/en/investors/financial-news-releases/press-release/technipfmc-awarded-subsea-contracts-by-petrobras-for-brazil-s-pre-salt-fields/#:~:text=All%20equipment%20and%20products%20will%20be%20manufactured%20and%20serviced,in%20inbound%20orders%20in%20the%20third%20quarter%20of%202024.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20241223091948/https://www.offshore-energy.biz/fresh-multimillion-dollar-gigs-take-technipfmc-to-petrobras-oil-fields-in-brazilian-waters/#:~:text=Fresh%20multimillion-dollar%20gigs%20take%20TechnipFMC%20to%20Petrobras%E2%80%99%20oil%20fields,the%20supply%20of%20associated%20services%2C%20including%20packing%20and%20storage.)

## Evidence

The stronger operating-profit result is not contradictory evidence of adjusted EBITDA growth. Subsea operating profit rose 7.8 percent sequentially, helped by a $12.6 million reduction in restructuring, impairment and other charges, better backlog mix and strong execution. On the adjusted EBITDA measure, execution largely offset, but did not overcome, lower services activity and fleet downtime for scheduled maintenance. Those are segment-wide explanations, not customer-level margin disclosures. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250604223840/https://www.technipfmc.com/en/investors/financial-news-releases/press-release/technipfmc-announces-first-quarter-2025-results/#:~:text=Subsea%20reported%20first-quarter%20revenue%20of%20%241%2C936.2%20million%2C%20a%20decrease,EBITDA%20margin%20increased%2080%20basis%20points%20to%2017.3%20percent.)

## Outlook

The base case is that Petrobras work supports revenue as deliveries proceed, with EBITDA growth depending on realized project margins and the return of service and vessel activity. Do not add the company’s $15.8 billion backlog to its outlook for more than $10 billion of Subsea inbound in 2025: the former is outstanding work across the company, the latter expected new segment orders, and neither is Petrobras-specific. Management kept the full-year company adjusted EBITDA guidance midpoint unchanged. That is consistent with holding forecasts, not proof that Subsea margins are flat. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250519123354/https://www.shippingherald.com/technipfmc-announces-first-quarter-2025-results/#:~:text=%E2%80%9COur%20revenue%20is%20derived%20from%20diverse%20sources%E2%80%94which%20include%20not,value%20for%20our%20clients%2C%20our%20Company%2C%20and%20our%20shareholders.%E2%80%9D) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250519123354/https://www.shippingherald.com/technipfmc-announces-first-quarter-2025-results/#:~:text=Pferdehirt%20added%2C%20%E2%80%9CWhile%20commodity%20prices%20are%20a%20primary%20variable,generated%20from%20activity%20outside%20of%20the%20U.S.%20land%20market.%E2%80%9D)

## What would change the view

The strongest upside case is that reusing a proven equipment platform reduces engineering effort, local manufacturing sustains utilization, and installation support leads to profitable life-of-field service work. Additional equipment and services are optional, not secured revenue. Raise the margin forecast if TechnipFMC shows that repeat Brazilian deliveries are earning above the existing backlog mix; raise EBITDA dollars if that advantage is material at the scheduled delivery volumes. A segment rebound as vessels return would support an execution recovery, but would not by itself establish a Petrobras margin premium. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250421022244/https://www.technipfmc.com/en/investors/financial-news-releases/press-release/technipfmc-awarded-subsea-contracts-by-petrobras-for-brazil-s-pre-salt-fields/#:~:text=All%20equipment%20and%20products%20will%20be%20manufactured%20and%20serviced,in%20inbound%20orders%20in%20the%20third%20quarter%20of%202024.) [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20241223091948/https://www.offshore-energy.biz/fresh-multimillion-dollar-gigs-take-technipfmc-to-petrobras-oil-fields-in-brazilian-waters/#:~:text=In%20addition%2C%20the%20deal%20entails%20installation%20support%20and%20life-of-field,our%20extensive%20in-country%20operations%20to%20deliver%20on%20these%20contracts.%E2%80%9D) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250604223840/https://www.technipfmc.com/en/investors/financial-news-releases/press-release/technipfmc-announces-first-quarter-2025-results/#:~:text=Subsea%20reported%20first-quarter%20revenue%20of%20%241%2C936.2%20million%2C%20a%20decrease,EBITDA%20margin%20increased%2080%20basis%20points%20to%2017.3%20percent.)

question: Given that Raytheon was the only RTX segment to underperform in Q1 2025, how do the significant contract awards for the Standard Missile-3, Tomahawk, and SM-6 programs, coupled with expanded Foreign Military Sales to Europe, impact the segment’s profitability and revenue trajectory for FY2025?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-07-21

**Research question**
Given that Raytheon was the only RTX segment to underperform in Q1 2025, how do the significant contract awards for the Standard Missile-3, Tomahawk, and SM-6 programs, coupled with expanded Foreign Military Sales to Europe, impact the segment’s profitability and revenue trajectory for FY2025?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

Raytheon was RTX’s only segment with lower year-over-year sales, reported operating profit and reported operating margin in the first quarter of 2025. Reported and adjusted sales fell 5 percent to $6,340 million, but rose 2 percent excluding the divested cybersecurity business. Reported operating profit fell 32 percent to $678 million, largely because the prior quarter a year earlier included a $375 million sale gain. Adjusted profit instead rose 8 percent to $678 million. Reported and adjusted margins thus ended at the same 10.694, but reported margin fell and adjusted margin rose. This was weakness against the prior year on specific measures, not evidence of a miss against expectations. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250624151109/https://www.rtx.com/news/news-center/2025/04/22/rtx-reports-q1-2025-results#:~:text=Pratt%20%26%20Whitney%20reported%20operating%20profit%20of%20%24580%20million,which%20was%20divested%20at%20the%20end%20of%20Q1%202024.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250624151109/https://www.rtx.com/news/news-center/2025/04/22/rtx-reports-q1-2025-results#:~:text=Collins%20Aerospace%20first%20quarter%202025%20reported%20and%20adjusted%20sales,higher%20volume%20on%20the%20F135%20Engine%20Core%20Upgrade%20program.)

## Evidence

The peer comparison confirms that Raytheon lagged on growth, not that it had the lowest margin. Against the same quarter a year earlier, Collins’ reported and adjusted sales rose 8 percent to $7,217 million; reported and adjusted operating profit rose 28 percent and 17 percent, respectively. Both margins therefore increased, to 15.0755 reported and 17.0015 adjusted. Pratt & Whitney’s sales on both bases rose 14 percent to $7,366 million; reported and adjusted profit rose 41 percent and 37 percent, lifting margins to 7.874 and 8.0098, respectively. Raytheon’s margin sat between its peers’ on either basis, and its adjusted profit and margin improved alongside theirs. [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250624151109/https://www.rtx.com/news/news-center/2025/04/22/rtx-reports-q1-2025-results#:~:text=Collins%20Aerospace%20first%20quarter%202025%20reported%20and%20adjusted%20sales,higher%20volume%20on%20the%20F135%20Engine%20Core%20Upgrade%20program.) [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250624151109/https://www.rtx.com/news/news-center/2025/04/22/rtx-reports-q1-2025-results#:~:text=Pratt%20%26%20Whitney%20reported%20operating%20profit%20of%20%24580%20million,which%20was%20divested%20at%20the%20end%20of%20Q1%202024.)

## Outlook

Base case as of 2025-07-21: the $1 billion ceiling on Raytheon’s SM-3 award supports backlog beyond 2025; the potential $2.19bn Dutch Tomahawk sale strengthens the European pipeline, not firm backlog. Neither warrants raising Raytheon’s FY2025 sales growth, operating profit or margin forecast on the available evidence. Early contract work could add sales and profit, but its scale is undisclosed. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250701050609/https://defensearchives.com/news/raytheon-awarded-1-billion-contract-to-continue-sm-3-ib-production-for-additional-year/#:~:text=Raytheon%20awarded%20%241%20billion%20contract%20to%20continue%20SM-3%20IB,delivered%20during%20the%20Research%2C%20Development%2C%20Test%20%26%20Evaluation%20phase.) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250701050609/https://defensearchives.com/news/raytheon-awarded-1-billion-contract-to-continue-sm-3-ib-production-for-additional-year/#:~:text=Production%20of%20the%20FY%202024%20lot%20was%20not%20even,seems%20likely%20that%20the%20IB%20is%20here%20to%20stay.) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250517030228/https://www.naval-technology.com/news/us-approves-2-19bn-sale-of-tomahawk-missiles-to-netherlands/#:~:text=The%20US%20State%20Department%20has%20given%20its%20approval%20for,been%20named%20as%20the%20principal%20contractor%20of%20the%20deal.)

## What would change the view

The strongest upside case is that early funded work adds meaningful sales this year and uninterrupted production reduces costs. Profitable incremental work would lift operating profit dollars; it would lift segment margin only if its margin exceeded what Raytheon would otherwise earn. Favorable mix and productivity helped the first quarter, but unsettled pricing and early execution costs make that outcome uncertain. RTX’s sales outlook of $83 billion to $84.0 billion is company-wide, not a Raytheon forecast. Revisit the sales call on disclosure of material in-year work or a signed European order with an in-year performance schedule; revisit the margin call when final pricing, cost estimates or updated segment guidance show that work improving the profit rate. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250701050609/https://defensearchives.com/news/raytheon-awarded-1-billion-contract-to-continue-sm-3-ib-production-for-additional-year/#:~:text=Production%20of%20the%20FY%202024%20lot%20was%20not%20even,seems%20likely%20that%20the%20IB%20is%20here%20to%20stay.) [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250624151109/https://www.rtx.com/news/news-center/2025/04/22/rtx-reports-q1-2025-results#:~:text=Pratt%20%26%20Whitney%20reported%20operating%20profit%20of%20%24580%20million,which%20was%20divested%20at%20the%20end%20of%20Q1%202024.) [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20250721233118/https://www.govconwire.com/articles/rtx-collins-raytheon-prattwhitney-financial-results-2025#:~:text=Only%20Raytheon%20saw%20its%20sales%20drop%20in%20Q1%20to,total%20sales%20of%20between%20%2483%20billion%20and%20%2484.0%20billion.)

## Checked calculations

Ratio percent (%) — 1,088 ÷ 7,217 × 100 ≈ 15.075516 [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250624151109/https://www.rtx.com/news/news-center/2025/04/22/rtx-reports-q1-2025-results#:~:text=Collins%20Aerospace%20first%20quarter%202025%20reported%20and%20adjusted%20sales,higher%20volume%20on%20the%20F135%20Engine%20Core%20Upgrade%20program.)

question: Given the persistent valuation discount (P/B 0.54) and recent analyst downgrades by UBS and Barclays, how should a portfolio manager assess MBGYY's sustainability as a high-yield dividend play relative to its operational inventory management and EV supply chain dependencies?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-09-29

**Research question**
Given the persistent valuation discount (P/B 0.54) and recent analyst downgrades by UBS and Barclays, how should a portfolio manager assess MBGYY's sustainability as a high-yield dividend play relative to its operational inventory management and EV supply chain dependencies?

## Answer

Avoid MBGYY for the portion of the portfolio that must deliver dependable income as of 2025-09-29. If retained elsewhere, cap the position so that losing its entire dividend would not breach the portfolio’s income floor. That is a sizing stress, not a forecast of suspension. The supplied Mercedes-Benz interim-report capture contains no financial results, and the alleged UBS and Barclays downgrades are unverified question premises. The reason for caution is that payout coverage has not been demonstrated, not that a cut has been established. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250702085222/https://group.mercedes-benz.com/investors/reports-news/interim-reports/q2-2025/#:~:text=The%20URL%20is%20correct.%20The%20content%20is%20not%20available%20yet.)

## Evidence

Neither the quoted price-to-book multiple nor the persistence of the discount is verified; both are question premises. To test the multiple, match the ordinary-share closing price to parent-attributable common equity per outstanding ordinary share on the same date, excluding treasury shares. For MBGYY, convert that book value using the depositary’s ordinary-shares-per-receipt ratio and same-date exchange rate. The supplied sources lack those inputs and a comparable price-to-book history. Even a confirmed discount would not establish dividend capacity: group book equity includes the financing business and is not cash available from industrial operations. [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1311150174) [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250702085222/https://group.mercedes-benz.com/investors/reports-news/interim-reports/q2-2025/#:~:text=The%20URL%20is%20correct.%20The%20content%20is%20not%20available%20yet.)

Give neither alleged analyst action weight in the income decision yet. No dated UBS or Barclays note is supplied. For each bank separately, identify the security and compare the old and new recommendation, price target and dividend estimate. A lower target with an unchanged rating is not a rating downgrade; even a rating downgrade need not imply a lower dividend forecast. The available corporate account discusses management’s valuation objective, not either bank’s call. [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1311150174)

The decisive inventory test is whether industrial free cash flow covers the annual common cash dividend without a stock drawdown. Compare reported industrial free cash flow with the dividend in euros, then repeat after subtracting the signed industrial inventory cash contribution: remove cash released by destocking or add back cash absorbed by a build. Use a full operating cycle and the cash-flow bridge, not the change between balance-sheet inventory totals. Coverage only after a release is fragile; coverage only before a build is promising but not spendable until the stock sells. The supplied capture gives neither flow, the inventory bridge nor the payout, so neither coverage result can be asserted. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250702085222/https://group.mercedes-benz.com/investors/reports-news/interim-reports/q2-2025/#:~:text=The%20URL%20is%20correct.%20The%20content%20is%20not%20available%20yet.) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1311150174)

## Outlook

Use no recurring inventory release in the base case. For the downside, stress the delivered cost of battery cells: China processes over 90% of the world’s graphite, a common anode input, and has imposed export restrictions on graphite products used in electrode manufacturing. Deduct the incremental cash cost on exposed purchases after contract protection and customer price recovery, plus any separate cash absorbed by buffer stocks. If that drain exceeds the base-case surplus over dividends, industrial cash flow no longer funds the payout. These are industry exposures, not Mercedes procurement shares; supplier contracts, volumes and pricing power are missing, so a company-specific loss cannot be quantified. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250905140233/https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=65305#:~:text=Battery%20mineral%20processing%20and%20processed%20battery%20minerals%20trade%20China,of%20the%20world%E2%80%99s%20battery%20material%20export%20trade%20in%202023.) [4](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1309159177)

## What would change the view

The strongest case for holding MBGYY is that inventory absorbs cash temporarily, vehicles subsequently sell without margin-eroding discounts, and battery contracts limit cost increases. Upgrade it to a sustainable income holding if successive industrial cash-flow bridges show the dividend covered both as reported and without inventory releases, with enough surplus to absorb a contract-based battery-cost stress. Falling inventory alone is not the signal: falling stock accompanied by weaker realized prices could improve current cash while impairing the next payout. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250702085222/https://group.mercedes-benz.com/investors/reports-news/interim-reports/q2-2025/#:~:text=The%20URL%20is%20correct.%20The%20content%20is%20not%20available%20yet.) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250905140233/https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=65305#:~:text=Battery%20materials%20are%20then%20used%20to%20produce%20battery%20components,the%20world%E2%80%99s%20battery%20cell%20production%20capacity%20by%20monetary%20value.)

## Sources

question: How do the leadership transition under CEO Carlos Piani and recent institutional inflows impact SABESP's (SBS) valuation outlook, particularly in light of ARSESP regulatory deliberation 1621/24 and its shift from a value-focused utility to a Zacks Rank #1 momentum stock?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-05-27

**Research question**
How do the leadership transition under CEO Carlos Piani and recent institutional inflows impact SABESP's (SBS) valuation outlook, particularly in light of ARSESP regulatory deliberation 1621/24 and its shift from a value-focused utility to a Zacks Rank #1 momentum stock?

## Answer

As of 2025-05-27, retain SABESP’s value-utility baseline. In May, Zacks placed SBS in the top 5% of its ranked universe, supporting a near-term momentum trade rather than a lasting valuation premium. The CEO transition to Carlos Piani, the reported institutional inflows and the applicability of the cited ARSESP deliberation are unverified question premises. Buying could lift the share price, but it would not establish that Piani can reduce water losses at a cost that leaves more cash for shareholders or that tariffs will allow SABESP to recover that investment. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250518014108/https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2472772/what-makes-sabesp-sbs-a-good-fit-for-trend-investing#:~:text=Moreover%2C%20SBS%20is%20currently%20trading%20at%2092.7%25%20of%20its,today%27s%20Zacks%20Rank%20%231%20%28Strong%20Buy%29%20stocks%20here%20%3E%3E%3E%3E) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1291205606)

## Evidence

The apparent shift from value to momentum is better understood as a change in the trading case than in the business. SBS moved from 88.6% of its rolling high-low range in April to 92.7% in May, but Zacks had already reported 96.3% and the same top rank the previous August. Those are snapshots of relative price strength, not a shareholder return or a valuation multiple. The rank reflects earnings-estimate revisions and surprises; it does not measure the return SABESP can earn on new infrastructure. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250415032703/https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2448267/sabesp-sbs-is-on-the-move-heres-why-the-trend-could-be-sustainable#:~:text=Moreover%2C%20SBS%20is%20currently%20trading%20at%2088.6%25%20of%20its,today%27s%20Zacks%20Rank%20%231%20%28Strong%20Buy%29%20stocks%20here%20%3E%3E%3E%3E) [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250518014108/https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2472772/what-makes-sabesp-sbs-a-good-fit-for-trend-investing#:~:text=Moreover%2C%20SBS%20is%20currently%20trading%20at%2092.7%25%20of%20its,today%27s%20Zacks%20Rank%20%231%20%28Strong%20Buy%29%20stocks%20here%20%3E%3E%3E%3E) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20240830141911/https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2323601/heres-why-momentum-in-sabesp-sbs-should-keep-going#:~:text=Moreover%2C%20SBS%20is%20currently%20trading%20at%2096.3%25%20of%20its,today%27s%20Zacks%20Rank%20%231%20%28Strong%20Buy%29%20stocks%20here%20%3E%3E%3E%3E)

Piani’s potential contribution is operational: if management reduces water losses, SABESP could deliver more billable water from the same supply. But the cost of fixing pipes matters as much as the savings. Historical reporting identifies leakage and underinvestment; it does not establish current losses or improvements under Piani. Likewise, without the ARSESP deliberation’s text, effective terms and tariff impact, there is no basis to assume customers will fund the investment on terms that reward shareholders. [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1291205606)

## Outlook

Treat the reported institutional buying as a possible source of demand, not independent confirmation of higher fair value. No holdings filings, purchase amounts, ownership changes or trading dates are supplied. Even if purchases are confirmed, buyers could be following the same price and earnings signals Zacks screens for rather than anticipating better regulated returns. In the base case, weakening estimate revisions would remove a reason to own the trade without changing the utility valuation. [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250518014108/https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2472772/what-makes-sabesp-sbs-a-good-fit-for-trend-investing#:~:text=Most%20of%20us%20have%20heard%20the%20dictum%20%22the%20trend,high-low%20range%2C%20which%20is%20usually%20an%20indicator%20of%20bullishness.) [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250518014108/https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2472772/what-makes-sabesp-sbs-a-good-fit-for-trend-investing#:~:text=Moreover%2C%20SBS%20is%20currently%20trading%20at%2092.7%25%20of%20its,today%27s%20Zacks%20Rank%20%231%20%28Strong%20Buy%29%20stocks%20here%20%3E%3E%3E%3E)

## What would change the view

The strongest alternative is that buyers are anticipating a durable improvement before it shows up in cash flow. I would reconsider a premium if published ARSESP terms show how efficiently deployed capital will be recovered and successive results show lower water losses and stronger cash flow after required investment, with returns above the cost of capital. Historical growth in cash generation is not that test. Dated holdings disclosures would verify the buying; the operating and regulatory evidence would justify paying more. [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20120309230919/http://exame.abril.com.br/negocios/empresas/noticias/lucro-da-sabesp-sobe-12-7-no-4o-tri-para-r-574-9-mi#:~:text=No%20ano%2C%20a%20gera%C3%A7%C3%A3o%20de%20caixa%20cresceu%2018%2C2%20por,em%202009.%20Visite%20a%20p%C3%A1gina%20de%20EXAME.com%20no%20Facebook) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1291205606)

question: Given the divestiture of the French Workwear unit to H.I.G. Capital and divergent institutional flows, how should Rentokil Initial’s (RTO) valuation of 25 times earnings be reconciled with its shifting business mix and JPMorgan’s cautious neutral rating?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-06-05

**Research question**
Given the divestiture of the French Workwear unit to H.I.G. Capital and divergent institutional flows, how should Rentokil Initial’s (RTO) valuation of 25 times earnings be reconciled with its shifting business mix and JPMorgan’s cautious neutral rating?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-06-05, JPMorgan’s neutral stance is better supported than a premium for Rentokil Initial. The French Workwear sale to H.I.G. Capital and the rating are unverified question premises. Taking the sale as given, Rentokil loses a business that earned £41m in adjusted operating profit at actual exchange rates in 2024. The benefit of a tighter focus on pest control and hygiene is plausible, but the main North American margin opportunity still depends on completing the Terminix integration. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250408055523/https://www.rentokil-initial.com/~/media/Files/R/Rentokil/documents/2024-preliminary-results.pdf#:~:text=11%20France%20Workwear%202024%20AER%20%C2%A3m%20AER%20Growth%202024,up%204.6ppt%20to%2082.0%25.%20All%20Regions%20except%20Europe%20improved) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250408055523/https://www.rentokil-initial.com/~/media/Files/R/Rentokil/documents/2024-preliminary-results.pdf#:~:text=8%20Three%20years%20post%20the%20acquisition%20announcement%20of%20Terminix%2C,%C2%A3m%20AER%20Growth%202024%20CER%20%C2%A3m%20CER%20Growth%20Organic)

## Evidence

The mix shift is not an automatic growth or margin upgrade. In 2024, French Workwear grew organically by 7.1% at a 17.7% adjusted operating margin. Retained Hygiene & Wellbeing grew organically by only 3.1%; its margin was higher at 18.1%, but fell 30bps. The sale therefore removes a faster-growing contributor than Hygiene, not an obvious margin drag. These segment comparisons do not establish the growth rate or margin of the whole remaining group. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250408055523/https://www.rentokil-initial.com/~/media/Files/R/Rentokil/documents/2024-preliminary-results.pdf#:~:text=11%20France%20Workwear%202024%20AER%20%C2%A3m%20AER%20Growth%202024,up%204.6ppt%20to%2082.0%25.%20All%20Regions%20except%20Europe%20improved) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250408055523/https://www.rentokil-initial.com/~/media/Files/R/Rentokil/documents/2024-preliminary-results.pdf#:~:text=Growth%202024%20CER%20%C2%A3m%20CER%20Growth%20Organic%20Growth%20Revenue,revenues%20of%20c.%C2%A350m%20in%20the%20year%20prior%20to%20purchase.)

## Outlook

The neutral base case gives Terminix savings credit as they appear in results, not at the sale date. Management expects c.$100m of remaining one-time integration costs through 2026. Its estimate of $100m in lower spending *after* integration is measured against 2024 spending; it is not an immediate net earnings gain. Management also retired the group adjusted margin target of more than 19% by 2026. That matters when group free cash flow had already fallen to £410m from £500m in the preceding year. [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250408055523/https://www.rentokil-initial.com/~/media/Files/R/Rentokil/documents/2024-preliminary-results.pdf#:~:text=8%20Three%20years%20post%20the%20acquisition%20announcement%20of%20Terminix%2C,%C2%A3m%20AER%20Growth%202024%20CER%20%C2%A3m%20CER%20Growth%20Organic) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250408055523/https://www.rentokil-initial.com/~/media/Files/R/Rentokil/documents/2024-preliminary-results.pdf#:~:text=25.1%25%29.%2013%20Net%20debt%20and%20cash%20flow%20%C2%A3m%20at,%283%2C146%29%20%283%2C279%29%20133%20Closing%20net%20debt%20%283%2C208%29%20%283%2C146%29%20%2862%29)

## What would change the view

The strongest premium case is that combining branches makes technicians more productive while organic growth recovers. The observable test is sustained North American organic growth improvement alongside operating margins above 20% from 2027, management’s regional expectation rather than a replacement group target. If that improvement translates into stronger group cash flow, a premium on verified continuing earnings would have support. [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250408055523/https://www.rentokil-initial.com/~/media/Files/R/Rentokil/documents/2024-preliminary-results.pdf#:~:text=8%20Three%20years%20post%20the%20acquisition%20announcement%20of%20Terminix%2C,%C2%A3m%20AER%20Growth%202024%20CER%20%C2%A3m%20CER%20Growth%20Organic)

## Sources

[Archived PDF](https://web.archive.org/web/20250408055523/https://www.rentokil-initial.com/~/media/Files/R/Rentokil/documents/2024-preliminary-results.pdf#:~:text=11%20France%20Workwear%202024%20AER%20%C2%A3m%20AER%20Growth%202024,up%204.6ppt%20to%2082.0%25.%20All%20Regions%20except%20Europe%20improved), available by 2025-04-08.

question: How should institutional investors interpret the divergence between heavy accumulation by funds like Point72 and VR Adviser and the insider selling by CEO Michael Henderson and CMO Carl Dambkowski, as Apogee Therapeutics approaches its critical Phase 2 APEX clinical data readout for APG777?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-06-29

**Research question**
How should institutional investors interpret the divergence between heavy accumulation by funds like Point72 and VR Adviser and the insider selling by CEO Michael Henderson and CMO Carl Dambkowski, as Apogee Therapeutics approaches its critical Phase 2 APEX clinical data readout for APG777?

## Answer

Hold an existing Apogee position through APEX if the portfolio can absorb a disappointing result; otherwise trim to the risk limit. As of 2025-06-29, heavy accumulation by Point Seventy Two and VR Adviser and sales by CEO Michael Henderson and CMO Carl Dambkowski are unverified premises of the question. The supplied record establishes neither the size of the trades nor whether they occurred in the same period. That apparent divergence warrants a filing check, not a change in the odds assigned to APEX. Apogee’s May update said the interim 16-week dermatitis data were expected midyear; it did not report patient outcomes. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250514105705/https://last10k.com/sec-filings/apge/0000950170-25-068513.htm#:~:text=Apogee%20Therapeutics%20Provides%20Business%20Update%2C%20Pipeline%20Progress%20and%20Reports,in%20mild-to-moderate%20asthma%20with%20readout%20expected%20in%201H%202026) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250406051447/https://investors.apogeetherapeutics.com/news-releases/news-release-details/apogee-therapeutics-announces-positive-interim-phase-1-results#:~:text=APG990%20interim%20Phase%201%20pharmacokinetic%20%28PK%29%20data%20showed%20a,dosing%20and%20efficacy%20across%20AD%20and%20broader%20I%26I%20diseases.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250406051447/https://investors.apogeetherapeutics.com/news-releases/news-release-details/apogee-therapeutics-announces-positive-interim-phase-1-results#:~:text=In%20addition%2C%20preclinical%20studies%20of%20the%20combination%20of%20APG777,with%20data%20expected%20in%20the%20second%20half%20of%202026.)

## Evidence

For Henderson and Dambkowski, the company identifies their roles, but the supplied materials contain no insider transaction filings. Check each executive’s transaction date, shares sold and retained, and filing footnotes for option exercises, tax withholding or a prearranged trading plan. A routine sale can coexist with a fund increasing exposure. The strongest contrary interpretation is that executives chose to reduce their personal risk before APEX: unusually large discretionary sales relative to their remaining stakes, outside prior patterns, would lend that view weight. Even then, the sales would not establish knowledge of an adverse result. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250514105705/https://last10k.com/sec-filings/apge/0000950170-25-068513.htm#:~:text=San%20Francisco%2C%20CA%20and%20Waltham%2C%20MA%2C%20May%2012%2C%202025,market%20leader%20in%20the%20rapidly%20expanding%20AD%20biologic%20space%3A) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250406051447/https://investors.apogeetherapeutics.com/news-releases/news-release-details/apogee-therapeutics-announces-positive-interim-phase-1-results#:~:text=In%20addition%2C%20preclinical%20studies%20of%20the%20combination%20of%20APG777,with%20data%20expected%20in%20the%20second%20half%20of%202026.)

To test the accumulation claim, compare APGE share counts in each manager’s consecutive quarter-end holdings filings, including amendments. A rise in market value alone could reflect price appreciation. A substantial rise in shares would support the narrower conclusion that the manager held a larger reported long position at quarter-end. It would not establish purchase dates, net exposure after hedges, or the position still held at readout. Managers generally have 45 days after quarter-end to file, so compare the holdings dates—not the filing dates—with the executives’ transaction dates before treating the trades as opposing bets. [5](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1223018657)

## Outlook

The clinical base case is a credible target with unproven product differentiation. APG777 inhibits IL-13, and lebrikizumab’s approval in atopic dermatitis supports the therapeutic rationale, not a claim of comparable efficacy. Apogee’s reported half-life of approximately 60 days belongs to APG990, the combination partner, not the APEX drug. It supports testing infrequent combination dosing; it is not evidence that patients on monotherapy will achieve or maintain disease control. [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20250406051447/https://investors.apogeetherapeutics.com/news-releases/news-release-details/apogee-therapeutics-announces-positive-interim-phase-1-results#:~:text=Webcast%20Details%20Apogee%20Therapeutics%E2%80%99%20live%20webcast%20of%20the%20APG990,of%20Type%201-3%20inflammation%20through%20APG990%E2%80%99s%20inhibition%20of%20OX40L.) [7](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1297103465) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250406051447/https://investors.apogeetherapeutics.com/news-releases/news-release-details/apogee-therapeutics-announces-positive-interim-phase-1-results#:~:text=APG990%20interim%20Phase%201%20pharmacokinetic%20%28PK%29%20data%20showed%20a,dosing%20and%20efficacy%20across%20AD%20and%20broader%20I%26I%20diseases.)

## What would change the view

Consider adding if APEX Part A shows a clinically meaningful improvement over control on prespecified dermatitis outcomes, with consistent responses and acceptable tolerability. Weak separation or a material safety imbalance would favor trimming even if the fund purchases were confirmed. A positive induction result would strengthen the efficacy case without settling maintenance durability or superiority to DUPIXENT: the planned head-to-head study tests APG279, the combination, not APEX monotherapy. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250514105705/https://last10k.com/sec-filings/apge/0000950170-25-068513.htm#:~:text=Apogee%20Therapeutics%20Provides%20Business%20Update%2C%20Pipeline%20Progress%20and%20Reports,in%20mild-to-moderate%20asthma%20with%20readout%20expected%20in%201H%202026) [8](https://web.archive.org/web/20250514105705/https://last10k.com/sec-filings/apge/0000950170-25-068513.htm#:~:text=APG279%20on%20track%20to%20initiate%20Phase%201b%20head-to-head%20trial,2%20inflammation%20that%20is%20associated%20with%20exacerbations%20in%20asthma)

question: How do the record results in the Caesars Digital segment and significant institutional accumulation in Q4 2024 reconcile with the Q1 2025 earnings miss and the reported revenue decline in the core Las Vegas segment for Caesars Entertainment (CZR)?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-05-21

**Research question**
How do the record results in the Caesars Digital segment and significant institutional accumulation in Q4 2024 reconcile with the Q1 2025 earnings miss and the reported revenue decline in the core Las Vegas segment for Caesars Entertainment (CZR)?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-05-21, Caesars shows operating improvement, not a demonstrated companywide recovery. In Q1 2025, Caesars Digital set a first-quarter Adjusted EBITDA record, up 38 year over year. Regional operations also grew, and consolidated Adjusted EBITDA rose 4%. Those results are compatible with an earnings miss: growth compares Caesars with its prior year, while a miss compares actual earnings with expectations. The evidence does not show that Las Vegas weakness outweighed Digital’s gain. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250501193752/https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250429095340/en/Caesars-Entertainment-Inc.-Reports-First-Quarter-2025-Results#:~:text=Caesars%20Digital%20Adjusted%20EBITDA%20of%20%2443%20million%20versus%20%245,First%20Quarter%202025%20Financial%20Results%20Summary%20and%20Segment%20Information) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250501193752/https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250429095340/en/Caesars-Entertainment-Inc.-Reports-First-Quarter-2025-Results#:~:text=Adjusted%20EBITDA%20%28described%20below%29%2C%20a%20non-GAAP%20financial%20measure%2C%20has,Caesars%20is%20attached%20at%20the%20end%20of%20this%20press)

## Evidence

Significant institutional accumulation in Q4 2024 is an unverified question premise. The available holdings material describes delayed quarter-end disclosures but supplies no CZR share counts for the relevant managers across successive quarters. Even if those counts confirmed net buying, they would establish that managers increased exposure before the earnings release, not that they expected a quarterly beat or bought because of Digital. [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1223018657)

## What would change the view

The base case is that Digital and Regional are improving operations, with a broader recovery still to prove. Sustained consolidated Adjusted EBITDA growth alongside a narrowing net loss would strengthen that thesis. The strongest alternative is that Las Vegas is weakening enough to offset Digital, with Regional masking the effect. A comparable-period Las Vegas Adjusted EBITDA decline larger than 38 in the quarter under review would establish that offset; a revenue decline alone would not. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250501193752/https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250429095340/en/Caesars-Entertainment-Inc.-Reports-First-Quarter-2025-Results#:~:text=Caesars%20Digital%20Adjusted%20EBITDA%20of%20%2443%20million%20versus%20%245,First%20Quarter%202025%20Financial%20Results%20Summary%20and%20Segment%20Information) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250501193752/https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250429095340/en/Caesars-Entertainment-Inc.-Reports-First-Quarter-2025-Results#:~:text=Adjusted%20EBITDA%20%28described%20below%29%2C%20a%20non-GAAP%20financial%20measure%2C%20has,Caesars%20is%20attached%20at%20the%20end%20of%20this%20press)

## Checked calculations

Increase in Caesars Digital Adjusted EBITDA, Q1 2025 versus Q1 2024 (USD millions) — 43 − 5 = 38 [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250501193752/https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250429095340/en/Caesars-Entertainment-Inc.-Reports-First-Quarter-2025-Results#:~:text=Caesars%20Digital%20Adjusted%20EBITDA%20of%20%2443%20million%20versus%20%245,First%20Quarter%202025%20Financial%20Results%20Summary%20and%20Segment%20Information)

question: What factors drove the significant surge in institutional accumulation of the Invesco Variable Rate Preferred ETF (VRP) during Q4 2024 and Q1 2025, and how does this concentrated positioning reflect professional sentiment regarding interest rate volatility and banking sector credit risk?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-06-25

**Research question**
What factors drove the significant surge in institutional accumulation of the Invesco Variable Rate Preferred ETF (VRP) during Q4 2024 and Q1 2025, and how does this concentrated positioning reflect professional sentiment regarding interest rate volatility and banking sector credit risk?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Evidence

The test is a change in shares, not in reported market value. Compare each manager’s VRP shares at the September, December and March quarter-ends, reconciling amendments and excluding option positions. For each quarter, report the aggregate net change relative to starting shares, then rank managers by shares added. Show the largest buyers’ additions both as a share of gross additions and, if holdings rose, as a share of the net increase. Sales by other managers can make the latter ratio look large even when buying was spread across many firms. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1223018657) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250517133050/https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1649339/000187920225000025/xslForm13F_X02/primary_doc.xml#:~:text=Signature%2C%20Place%2C%20and%20Date%20of%20Signing%3A%20Please%20note%20that,13f-1%28c%29%20%5B17%20CFR%20240.13f-1%28c%29%5D%20Report%20Type%20%28Check%20only%20one.%29%3A)

## Outlook

If accumulation is verified, the rate explanation is the better-supported hypothesis to test. Treasury yields rose after the December Fed announcement; by March, more officials expected no cuts that year. Those observations concern different things—a market reaction and a policy outlook—but both gave managers reason to reconsider fixed-rate exposure. A shift into resetting dividends could reduce sensitivity to rising yields while retaining preferred income. That is not the same as a hedge that profits from volatility, and the policy news does not establish a buyer’s motive. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250618210758/https://www.cnbc.com/2024/12/18/fed-rate-decision-december-2024-.html#:~:text=%22Today%20was%20a%20closer%20call%20but%20we%20decided%20it,think%20going%20forward%20obviously%20we%27re%20moving%20slower%2C%22%20Powell%20said.) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250607182556/https://www.cnbc.com/2025/03/19/fed-rate-decision-march-2025.html#:~:text=The%20group%20downgraded%20its%20collective%20outlook%20for%20economic%20growth,rate%20settles%20in%20at%20a%20longer-run%20level%20around%203%25.) [5](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1255556769)

## What would change the view

The strongest competing interpretation is willingness to take more bank credit risk for income. A dividend reset can change the payout rate without protecting the payout itself. To distinguish the explanations, verify VRP’s bank issuer weights and examine the buyers’ other holdings: sales of fixed-rate preferreds from comparable issuers alongside VRP additions, with total bank exposure little changed, would favor rate management. Broad additions to bank preferreds across coupon types would favor a credit allocation. Even then, concentration among a few managers would describe those managers’ positioning, not professional sentiment generally. [5](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1255556769) [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1223018657)

## Sources

1. [Form 13F](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1223018657), available by 2024-05-09.
2. [SEC FORM 13F-HR](https://web.archive.org/web/20250517133050/https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1649339/000187920225000025/xslForm13F_X02/primary_doc.xml#:~:text=Signature%2C%20Place%2C%20and%20Date%20of%20Signing%3A%20Please%20note%20that,13f-1%28c%29%20%5B17%20CFR%20240.13f-1%28c%29%5D%20Report%20Type%20%28Check%20only%20one.%29%3A), available by 2025-05-17.

[Fed meeting December 2024: Fed cuts rate by a quarter point](https://web.archive.org/web/20250618210758/https://www.cnbc.com/2024/12/18/fed-rate-decision-december-2024-.html#:~:text=%22Today%20was%20a%20closer%20call%20but%20we%20decided%20it,think%20going%20forward%20obviously%20we%27re%20moving%20slower%2C%22%20Powell%20said.), available by 2025-06-18.
4.
