question: Following the August 2025 ATTAIN-1 data release and subsequent share price correction, how does orforglipron's 12.4% weight loss efficacy affect Eli Lilly’s competitive positioning against Novo Nordisk and its ability to capture the $10 billion annual sales forecasted by analysts?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-08-20

**Research question**
Following the August 2025 ATTAIN-1 data release and subsequent share price correction, how does orforglipron's 12.4% weight loss efficacy affect Eli Lilly’s competitive positioning against Novo Nordisk and its ability to capture the $10 billion annual sales forecasted by analysts?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Evidence

The trial succeeded against placebo, not against Novo. In ATTAIN-1, all doses met the primary and key secondary endpoints in adults with obesity, or overweight with a weight-related condition, without diabetes. At 72 weeks, 36 mg once daily produced 12.4% mean weight loss from baseline versus 0.9% on placebo. The efficacy estimand asks what would happen if participants stayed on assigned treatment. The headline is therefore neither a placebo-adjusted result nor the average loss to expect among everyone who starts the pill in practice. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250819203344/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/lillys-oral-glp-1--orforglipron-delivers-weight-loss-of-up-to-an-average-of-27-3-lbs-in-first-of-two-pivotal-phase-3-trials-in-adults-with-obesity-302523649.html#:~:text=With%20these%20results%2C%20Lilly%20is%20on%20track%20to%20submit,global%20launch%20to%20address%20this%20urgent%20public%20health%20need.%22) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250819203344/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/lillys-oral-glp-1--orforglipron-delivers-weight-loss-of-up-to-an-average-of-27-3-lbs-in-first-of-two-pivotal-phase-3-trials-in-adults-with-obesity-302523649.html#:~:text=About%20ATTAIN-1%20and%20ATTAIN%20clinical%20trial%20program%20ATTAIN-1%20%28NCT05869903%29,began%20in%202023%20with%20additional%20results%20anticipated%20this%20year.)

Lilly shares fell 14% in early trading on the Aug. 7, 2025 release day, despite stronger-than-expected Mounjaro and Zepbound sales and higher company guidance. That contrast supports an interpretation of disappointment relative to investors’ expectations, not clinical failure. The reported move is neither a closing return nor the cumulative decline through the cutoff; it does not measure how much future pill revenue was lost. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250819203344/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/lillys-oral-glp-1--orforglipron-delivers-weight-loss-of-up-to-an-average-of-27-3-lbs-in-first-of-two-pivotal-phase-3-trials-in-adults-with-obesity-302523649.html#:~:text=With%20these%20results%2C%20Lilly%20is%20on%20track%20to%20submit,global%20launch%20to%20address%20this%20urgent%20public%20health%20need.%22) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250819184305/https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/eli-lilly-orforglipron-obesity-data-q2-2025-earnings/757049/#:~:text=Study%20participants%20given%20the%20highest%20dose%20of%20the%20drug%2C,became%20the%20most-prescribed%20drug%20of%20its%20kind%20in%20diabetes.) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250819184305/https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/eli-lilly-orforglipron-obesity-data-q2-2025-earnings/757049/#:~:text=Mounjaro%20and%20Zepbound%2C%20the%20obesity%20drug%20that%20shares%20the,of%20Wegovy%20Novo%E2%80%99s%20advancing%20also%20achieved%2015%25%20weight%20loss.)

Novo has a timing advantage as well as a numerical efficacy advantage: its pill was already under FDA review, while Lilly planned to file by year-end. Injectable Wegovy and Lilly’s own Zepbound also set benchmarks of up to 15% and 21% weight loss, respectively. These comparisons weaken the case for choosing orforglipron for maximum weight loss, but do not prove inferiority: separate trials can differ in patient mix, duration and how they handle discontinuations. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250819184305/https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/eli-lilly-orforglipron-obesity-data-q2-2025-earnings/757049/#:~:text=Study%20participants%20given%20the%20highest%20dose%20of%20the%20drug%2C,became%20the%20most-prescribed%20drug%20of%20its%20kind%20in%20diabetes.) [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250819203344/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/lillys-oral-glp-1--orforglipron-delivers-weight-loss-of-up-to-an-average-of-27-3-lbs-in-first-of-two-pivotal-phase-3-trials-in-adults-with-obesity-302523649.html#:~:text=With%20these%20results%2C%20Lilly%20is%20on%20track%20to%20submit,global%20launch%20to%20address%20this%20urgent%20public%20health%20need.%22) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250819184305/https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/eli-lilly-orforglipron-obesity-data-q2-2025-earnings/757049/#:~:text=Mounjaro%20and%20Zepbound%2C%20the%20obesity%20drug%20that%20shares%20the,of%20Wegovy%20Novo%E2%80%99s%20advancing%20also%20achieved%2015%25%20weight%20loss.)

C4. Change percent (%) — (14 − 22) ÷ |22| × 100 ≈ -36.363636 [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250819184305/https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/eli-lilly-orforglipron-obesity-data-q2-2025-earnings/757049/#:~:text=Custer%E2%80%99s%20message%20didn%E2%80%99t%20resonate%20with%20Wall%20Street%20investors%2C%20however.,to%20those%20willing%20to%20pay%20cash.%20purchase%20licensing%20rights)

## Outlook

Base case: lower expected sales, but retain a credible route to the requested annual threshold through adoption rather than superior weight loss. If approved, a once-daily pill without food or water restrictions could attract patients who decline injections or find dosing routines burdensome. Easier manufacturing could help Lilly serve those patients. The limiting factor may be how long they stay: adverse events led 10.3% to stop at the highest dose versus 2.6% on placebo. Convenience can win a prescription without winning the refill. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250819203344/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/lillys-oral-glp-1--orforglipron-delivers-weight-loss-of-up-to-an-average-of-27-3-lbs-in-first-of-two-pivotal-phase-3-trials-in-adults-with-obesity-302523649.html#:~:text=With%20these%20results%2C%20Lilly%20is%20on%20track%20to%20submit,global%20launch%20to%20address%20this%20urgent%20public%20health%20need.%22) [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20250809074429/https://www.cnbc.com/2025/04/17/eli-lilly-weight-loss-pill-orforglipron-clears-first-late-stage-trial.html#:~:text=Eli%20Lilly%20on%20Thursday%20said%20its%20daily%20obesity%20pill,of%20some%20analysts%27%20estimates%20for%20a%20key%20diabetes%20metric.) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250819184305/https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/eli-lilly-orforglipron-obesity-data-q2-2025-earnings/757049/#:~:text=Custer%E2%80%99s%20message%20didn%E2%80%99t%20resonate%20with%20Wall%20Street%20investors%2C%20however.,to%20those%20willing%20to%20pay%20cash.%20purchase%20licensing%20rights)

## What would change the view

The strongest downside case is that a Novo price cut forces Lilly to discount while insurers still restrict coverage. At a lower net price, Lilly needs more months of paid treatment to reach the same sales; weak refills would compound the shortfall. The next obesity and diabetes trial results can clarify tolerability, but not reimbursement. After any launch, broad formulary access, reliable supply and sustained refills at a viable net price would restore confidence; narrow coverage and rapid refill attrition despite discounting would warrant a further cut. question: Does Encompass Health's (EHC) strategic expansion in Florida and robust EPS performance justify the recent valuation premium and price target hikes to $135, given the conflicting institutional sentiment seen in major Q4 2024 divestments by William Blair and Wellington Management?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-06-10

**Research question**
Does Encompass Health's (EHC) strategic expansion in Florida and robust EPS performance justify the recent valuation premium and price target hikes to $135, given the conflicting institutional sentiment seen in major Q4 2024 divestments by William Blair and Wellington Management?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Evidence

The purported conflict between analysts and institutions is not established. Verification would require dated broker notes showing the prior and revised targets, and each manager’s consecutive quarter-end filings showing a decline in EHC shares held, not merely in market value. The Wellington material describes its advisory business, not its EHC position; no corresponding William Blair holdings or broker revisions are supplied. Even if confirmed, a year-end reduction predates EHC’s April results, and a portfolio decision does not reveal the manager’s view of fair value. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1287097379) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250425052413/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/encompass-health-reports-results-for-first-quarter-2025-302437643.html#:~:text=Increases%20full-year%20guidance%20BIRMINGHAM%2C%20Ala.%2C%20April%2024%2C%202025%20%2FPRNewswire%2F,March%2031%2C%202025.%20%28In%20Millions%2C%20Except%20Per%20Share%20Data%29)

Expansion is documented at the company level, not at the Florida level. EHC opened a 40-bed hospital and added 25 beds at existing facilities during the quarter, but the release does not locate those additions in Florida. The Florida-specific reference concerns a historical sale of an acute-care hospital, not a new rehabilitation facility. I would assign no incremental Florida earnings until openings, admissions and costs can be tied to named sites. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250425052413/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/encompass-health-reports-results-for-first-quarter-2025-302437643.html#:~:text=Adjusted%20EBITDA%20increased%2014.9%25%20from%20increased%20revenue%20and%20expense,business.%22%20The%20Company%20increased%20its%20full-year%20guidance%20as%20follows%3A) [4](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1290217977)

## Outlook

My base case is continued revenue growth as new beds fill, without assuming that EPS will grow at the recent Adjusted EBITDA pace. Management raised full-year guidance, but the excerpt gives neither an EPS range nor a comparable EPS history. New facilities can contribute EBITDA before depreciation and financing costs are covered. The test is whether rising admissions produce sustained growth in diluted GAAP EPS and cash flow after capital spending, not just higher adjusted earnings. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250425052413/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/encompass-health-reports-results-for-first-quarter-2025-302437643.html#:~:text=Adjusted%20EBITDA%20increased%2014.9%25%20from%20increased%20revenue%20and%20expense,business.%22%20The%20Company%20increased%20its%20full-year%20guidance%20as%20follows%3A) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250425052413/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/encompass-health-reports-results-for-first-quarter-2025-302437643.html#:~:text=The%20financial%20data%20contained%20in%20the%20press%20release%20and,the%20other%20reconciling%20GAAP%20measures%20could%20be%20reasonably%20predicted%3A)

## What would change the view

The strongest case for paying more than for peers is that EHC can repeatedly fill new hospitals fast enough to spread fixed costs and earn superior returns on the capital invested. I would reconsider if Florida facilities show rising occupancy and margins after staffing costs, and if their contribution lifts per-share earnings and cash flow enough to support the observed forward multiple against comparable operators. Rising admissions without margin gains would favor the more cautious view, particularly if nurse and therapist shortages persist. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250425052413/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/encompass-health-reports-results-for-first-quarter-2025-302437643.html#:~:text=Adjusted%20EBITDA%20increased%2014.9%25%20from%20increased%20revenue%20and%20expense,business.%22%20The%20Company%20increased%20its%20full-year%20guidance%20as%20follows%3A) [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20250425052413/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/encompass-health-reports-results-for-first-quarter-2025-302437643.html#:~:text=the%20administrative%20appeals%20process%20on%20a%20timely%20basis%3B%20Encompass,filed.%20Media%20Contact%20Polly%20Manuel%2C%20205%20969-4532%20%5Bemail%20protected%5D)

question: How does TotalEnergies' strategic realignment—marked by the divestment of European retail assets to Circle K and heavy investment in Suriname and Indonesian renewables—affect its long-term capacity to sustain shareholder returns exceeding 40% of cash flow amidst rising capital expenditure for low-carbon projects?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-07-21

**Research question**
How does TotalEnergies' strategic realignment—marked by the divestment of European retail assets to Circle K and heavy investment in Suriname and Indonesian renewables—affect its long-term capacity to sustain shareholder returns exceeding 40% of cash flow amidst rising capital expenditure for low-carbon projects?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Evidence

Taking the Circle K sale as described in the question, selling European retail assets can release cash for investment, but the proceeds cannot fund a recurring payout indefinitely. The lasting effect depends on whether avoided retail investment and cash earned on reinvested proceeds outweigh the operating cash flow surrendered. The available filing notice establishes that the annual report was filed; it supplies neither sale proceeds nor foregone retail cash flow. I would therefore exclude disposal receipts from payout coverage and leave the recurring effect unquantified. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250430005638/https://corporate.totalenergies.us/news/totalenergies-releases-its-universal-registration-document-2024-and-its-form-20-f-2024-well#:~:text=the%20reports%20from%20the%20statutory%20auditors.%20TotalEnergies%20SE%E2%80%99s%20Form,place%20Jean%20Millier%2C%20La%20D%C3%A9fense%206%2C%2092400%20Courbevoie%2C%20France.)

Separate Suriname oil development from Indonesian low-carbon power. Suriname would require cash before production and would ultimately expose returns to oil prices; the evidence here establishes neither TotalEnergies’ spending schedule nor future oil receipts. The Indonesian project, by contrast, is an equally owned venture with RGE for solar generation, battery storage and a subsea connection. Its conditional licence covers imports of 1 GW into Singapore, not a dollar commitment by TotalEnergies. The scale of spending and the rise in group low-carbon capex remain unverified question premises. [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250613034231/https://totalenergies.sg/newsroom/indonesia-singapore-totalenergies-and-rge-reach-new-milestone-large-scale-solar-and#:~:text=The%20project%20will%20also%20supply%20electricity%20to%20local%20industry,French%20President%20Emmanuel%20Macron%20and%20Indonesian%20President%20Prabowo%20Subianto.)

## Outlook

My base case is that investment competes with buybacks before new projects contribute cash. Singa aims to operate from 2029 onwards; its licence is a development milestone, not evidence of current electricity receipts. The strongest alternative is that stronger hydrocarbon cash generation covers construction and distributions until new oil and power sales contribute. That is plausible, but the reported funding gap and debt increase weigh against assuming it. Neither observation alone proves a permanent deficit or identifies which project caused it. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250610024030/https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/companies-markets/ema-grants-conditional-licence-rge-totalenergies-indonesian-solar-project-import-electricity#:~:text=Singa%20Renewables%2C%20which%20aims%20to%20achieve%20commercial%20operations%20from,about%2040%20per%20cent%20of%20the%20country%E2%80%99s%20carbon%20emissions.) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20230823130024/https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/total-back-pre-pandemic-profit-levels-oil-prices-rise-2021-04-29/#:~:text=Eyes%20higher%20cash%20flow%20in%202021%2C%20dividend%20stable%20PARIS%2C,from%20this%20drive%20as%20areas%20like%20oil%20refining%20suffered.) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250514071758/https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/totalenergies-q1-profits-fall-lower-oil-prices-weak-refining-margins-2025-04-30/#:~:text=Net%20debt%20rises%20to%20%2420.1%20billion%2C%20up%2042%25%20vs,Editing%20by%20Aidan%20Lewis%2C%20Mark%20Potter%20and%20Elaine%20Hardcastle)

## What would change the view

I would upgrade the assessment if, across the construction years and a period of weaker oil prices, reported operating cash flow less cash investment before disposals consistently covered dividends and buybacks, the payout exceeded the proposed share of operating cash flow, and net debt stayed flat or fell. A higher payout ratio alone would not suffice: falling operating cash flow can lift the ratio while leaving less cash to distribute. Separate disclosures of Suriname cash outlays and Singa funding calls would show how much of the remaining cash each project absorbs. [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250514071758/https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/totalenergies-q1-profits-fall-lower-oil-prices-weak-refining-margins-2025-04-30/#:~:text=Net%20debt%20rises%20to%20%2420.1%20billion%2C%20up%2042%25%20vs,Editing%20by%20Aidan%20Lewis%2C%20Mark%20Potter%20and%20Elaine%20Hardcastle) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250613034231/https://totalenergies.sg/newsroom/indonesia-singapore-totalenergies-and-rge-reach-new-milestone-large-scale-solar-and#:~:text=The%20project%20will%20also%20supply%20electricity%20to%20local%20industry,French%20President%20Emmanuel%20Macron%20and%20Indonesian%20President%20Prabowo%20Subianto.)

question: How will Airbus’s definitive agreement to acquire Spirit AeroSystems’ A350-related assets and the concurrent $200 million credit facility impact the manufacturer's ability to achieve its 2028 A350 production target of 12 aircraft per month while managing the operational risks of integrating distressed supplier facilities?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-06-10

**Research question**
How will Airbus’s definitive agreement to acquire Spirit AeroSystems’ A350-related assets and the concurrent $200 million credit facility impact the manufacturer's ability to achieve its 2028 A350 production target of 12 aircraft per month while managing the operational risks of integrating distressed supplier facilities?

## Answer

As of 2025-06-10, yes: Airbus’s agreement with Spirit and its $200 million credit commitment make 12 aircraft per month in 2028 materially more achievable for the A350, but I would still expect Airbus to reach that rate later. The deal addresses a supplier that the March assessment identified as a reason passenger-jet production was unlikely to exceed six aircraft per month in 2025, against earlier expectations of approximately nine. Credit can keep parts moving before closing; ownership can help Airbus raise output afterward. Neither demonstrates that the plants can sustain the target rate. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250317061047/https://flightplan.forecastinternational.com/2025/02/26/supply-chain-challenges-limit-a350-production-to-six-aircraft-per-month-a350f-deliveries-delayed-to-2027/#:~:text=WASHINGTON%20D.C.%20%E2%80%93%20Ongoing%20supply%20chain%20challenges%20at%20Airbus,a%20slower-than-expected%20growth%20in%20production%20in%20the%20post-pandemic%20environment.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250317061047/https://flightplan.forecastinternational.com/2025/02/26/supply-chain-challenges-limit-a350-production-to-six-aircraft-per-month-a350f-deliveries-delayed-to-2027/#:~:text=Forecast%20International%E2%80%99s%202025%20production%20forecast%20for%20the%20A350%20was,the%20full%20A350%20report%20will%20be%20available%20in%20May.) [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1290078628) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250601212019/https://www.wsj.com/business/airlines/airbus-reaches-deal-to-buy-spirit-aerosystems-plants-2e1a2810#:~:text=Airbus%20AIR%200.14%25increase%3B%20green%20up%20pointing%20triangle%20agreed%20to,fuselage%20sections%20and%20other%20components%20for%20Airbus%E2%80%99s%20commercial%20aircraft.)

## Evidence

The definitive agreement signed in April covers the A350 fuselage-section sites in Kinston, North Carolina, and St. Nazaire, France, plus production assets for A320 and A350 wing components in Prestwick, Scotland—not the whole Prestwick site. Signing did not transfer operational control. Closing was expected in the third quarter of 2025 alongside Boeing’s acquisition of Spirit, subject to regulatory approvals and other conditions. Delay would shorten the time Airbus has to stabilize production; failure to close would deny it the planned control. [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1290078628) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250429173656/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/spirit-aerosystems-signs-divestiture-agreement-with-airbus-302439157.html#:~:text=WICHITA%2C%20Kan.%2C%20April%2028%2C%202025%20%2FPRNewswire%2F%20--%20Spirit%20AeroSystems,Airbus%20will%20take%20ownership%20of%20the%20following%20Spirit%20assets%3A)

Airbus is the lender and Spirit the borrower under non-interest-bearing credit lines totaling $200 million for ongoing Airbus programs during the transition, not solely for the A350. Access to working capital can help Spirit pay suppliers and retain workers rather than interrupt a production run for lack of cash. The amount is credit committed, not cash shown to have been drawn or earmarked for new capacity. It is distinct from transaction compensation; the available terms establish neither drawdowns nor any separate compensation amount. [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1290078628)

After closing, the main gain would be the ability to schedule fuselage sets against final-assembly needs and direct investment to whichever operation limits completed sets. The handover itself could undermine that gain: losing skilled staff, interrupting supplier contracts or production systems, or increasing rework could leave Airbus with fewer usable parts even if more enter production. Airbus should retain key teams, maintain contract and systems continuity, and increase schedules only when tooling and quality checks support repeatable output. These are risks to manage, not documented failures at each site. [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1290078628) [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20250429173656/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/spirit-aerosystems-signs-divestiture-agreement-with-airbus-302439157.html#:~:text=Important%20factors%20that%20could%20cause%20actual%20results%20to%20differ,treatment%20of%20the%20Transactions%3B%20litigation%20or%20other%20legal%20or)

## Outlook

My base case is that supply stabilizes before capacity catches up, with the target rate reached after 2028. The March production assessment is an outlook, not a measured June run rate. Forecast International’s 73 projected deliveries in 2025 measure customer handovers, not factory output. Its expectation of reaching the target in 2029 is a useful pre-agreement benchmark, not a verdict on the deal. Even if Spirit’s sites recover promptly, engines, cabin equipment or final assembly could set the pace instead: none is part of the acquired fuselage and wing work, and the evidence does not identify which, if any, will constrain output. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250317061047/https://flightplan.forecastinternational.com/2025/02/26/supply-chain-challenges-limit-a350-production-to-six-aircraft-per-month-a350f-deliveries-delayed-to-2027/#:~:text=WASHINGTON%20D.C.%20%E2%80%93%20Ongoing%20supply%20chain%20challenges%20at%20Airbus,a%20slower-than-expected%20growth%20in%20production%20in%20the%20post-pandemic%20environment.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250317061047/https://flightplan.forecastinternational.com/2025/02/26/supply-chain-challenges-limit-a350-production-to-six-aircraft-per-month-a350f-deliveries-delayed-to-2027/#:~:text=Forecast%20International%E2%80%99s%202025%20production%20forecast%20for%20the%20A350%20was,the%20full%20A350%20report%20will%20be%20available%20in%20May.) [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1290078628)

## What would change the view

The strongest on-time case is that Spirit’s disruption, rather than a shortage of capacity elsewhere, was the decisive constraint. I would move to that case on a timely close followed by sustained increases in complete, on-time fuselage sets and wing components passing inspection without mounting rework, with final assembly converting them into aircraft at a matching rate. Closing alone—or a short-lived rise in customer deliveries—would not establish that. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250317061047/https://flightplan.forecastinternational.com/2025/02/26/supply-chain-challenges-limit-a350-production-to-six-aircraft-per-month-a350f-deliveries-delayed-to-2027/#:~:text=WASHINGTON%20D.C.%20%E2%80%93%20Ongoing%20supply%20chain%20challenges%20at%20Airbus,a%20slower-than-expected%20growth%20in%20production%20in%20the%20post-pandemic%20environment.) question: Given Cboe Global Markets' strong segment growth and significant new positions from institutional investors like Norges Bank, how should the recent downgrades from Goldman Sachs and BofA, combined with executive selling activity, inform an assessment of CBOE’s valuation and growth sustainability into the middle of 2025?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-05-06

**Research question**
Given Cboe Global Markets' strong segment growth and significant new positions from institutional investors like Norges Bank, how should the recent downgrades from Goldman Sachs and BofA, combined with executive selling activity, inform an assessment of CBOE’s valuation and growth sustainability into the middle of 2025?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-05-06, the evidence did not establish that projected earnings growth through mid-2025 justified Cboe’s share price. That does not mean the stock was overpriced: neither the cutoff price nor a contemporaneous earnings forecast is supplied. In the first quarter of 2023, net revenue rose 13% to $471.4 million as market turmoil lifted trading volumes. That result shows how much Cboe benefited in a volatile quarter, not how much it could earn in calmer markets. The reported Goldman Sachs and BofA downgrades, new Norges Bank holding and executive sales are unverified question premises; none changes that judgment on the available evidence. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1280062201) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20230515011816/https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/exchange-operator-cboe-profit-rises-market-volatility-lifts-trading-volumes-2023-05-05/#:~:text=Cboe%20last%20week%20launched%20a%20one-day%20volatility%20index%20linked,client%20note.%20Net%20revenue%20rose%2013%25%20to%20%24471.4%20million.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20230515011816/https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/exchange-operator-cboe-profit-rises-market-volatility-lifts-trading-volumes-2023-05-05/#:~:text=May%205%20%28Reuters%29%20-%20Cboe%20Global%20Markets%20%28CBOE.Z%29%20on,cents%20above%20analysts%27%20mean%20estimate%2C%20according%20to%20Refinitiv%20data.)

## Evidence

The evidence supports a trading-volume explanation, not a recurring-revenue growth rate. Management attributed the historical result to proprietary index options. Same-day-expiry contracts accounted for nearly 43% of first-quarter SPX volume and nearly 45% in April. That share shows customers used the product; it does not show that total contracts or fee revenue would hold up if hedging demand fell. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20230515011816/https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/exchange-operator-cboe-profit-rises-market-volatility-lifts-trading-volumes-2023-05-05/#:~:text=%22These%20record-breaking%20first-quarter%20results%20were%20driven%20by%20strong%20volumes,Chief%20Executive%20Ed%20Tilly%20said%20on%20an%20analyst%20call.) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20230515011816/https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/exchange-operator-cboe-profit-rises-market-volatility-lifts-trading-volumes-2023-05-05/#:~:text=Investors%20turned%20to%20the%20Chicago-based%20company%27s%20proprietary%20products%2C%20such,or%20take%20a%20position%20in%20short-term%20moves%2C%22%20Tilly%20said.)

The reported downgrades would matter most if Goldman Sachs or BofA cut earnings estimates because they expected lower volumes or weaker margins. A downgrade based on price alone would instead question the return available to a new buyer, not the durability of Cboe’s business. Neither bank’s dated note, estimate revision or valuation rationale is supplied. The analyst comment in the record is from CFRA and concerns a then-untradeable volatility index; it cannot establish what either bank expected at the cutoff. [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20230515011816/https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/exchange-operator-cboe-profit-rises-market-volatility-lifts-trading-volumes-2023-05-05/#:~:text=Cboe%20last%20week%20launched%20a%20one-day%20volatility%20index%20linked,client%20note.%20Net%20revenue%20rose%2013%25%20to%20%24471.4%20million.)

Do not treat the reported Norges Bank purchase and executive sales as opposing votes on fair value. The documented Norges investment concerns offshore wind farms, not Cboe shares; the executive report documents a promotion, not a disposal. A dated holdings filing and prior-period comparison would establish whether the Cboe stake was new and material, not why it was bought. For the sales, the useful checks are the fraction of each executive’s stake sold and whether the trades were prearranged. Without those disclosures, neither signal changes the earnings assessment. [6](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1286393933) [7](https://web.archive.org/web/20250306102204/https://www.thetradenews.com/cboe-global-markets-makes-series-of-senior-leadership-changes-with-promotions-and-relocations/#:~:text=Cboe%20Global%20Markets%20has%20made%20several%20changes%20to%20its,president%20of%20Cboe%20Global%20Markets%2C%20effective%2012%20May%202022.)

## What would change the view

The base case is to value recurring fees separately and use ordinary trading volumes rather than a stress quarter to estimate transaction earnings. The strongest alternative is that same-day options have become a routine tool, raising volumes even when markets are quiet. The distinguishing signal would be sustained contracts per day and net fees per contract in calmer months, alongside separately reported recurring-fee growth. If those inputs supported the midyear earnings forecast at normal margins, compare the cutoff price against those normalized earnings and peer multiples. That test would carry more weight than a rating or a share sale. [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20230515011816/https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/exchange-operator-cboe-profit-rises-market-volatility-lifts-trading-volumes-2023-05-05/#:~:text=Investors%20turned%20to%20the%20Chicago-based%20company%27s%20proprietary%20products%2C%20such,or%20take%20a%20position%20in%20short-term%20moves%2C%22%20Tilly%20said.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20230515011816/https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/exchange-operator-cboe-profit-rises-market-volatility-lifts-trading-volumes-2023-05-05/#:~:text=May%205%20%28Reuters%29%20-%20Cboe%20Global%20Markets%20%28CBOE.Z%29%20on,cents%20above%20analysts%27%20mean%20estimate%2C%20according%20to%20Refinitiv%20data.)

question: Given Beth Hammack’s characterization of policy as 'modestly restrictive' and the European Central Bank’s transition from seven rate cuts to a cautious neutral stance by August 2025, how will this central bank divergence affect EUR/USD exchange rate stability and Eurozone fixed-income risk premiums through year-end?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-09-02

**Research question**
Given Beth Hammack’s characterization of policy as 'modestly restrictive' and the European Central Bank’s transition from seven rate cuts to a cautious neutral stance by August 2025, how will this central bank divergence affect EUR/USD exchange rate stability and Eurozone fixed-income risk premiums through year-end?

## Answer

As of 2025-09-02, keep EUR/USD hedge coverage at its existing strategic level through December 2025. The evidence does not show that expected Federal Reserve and ECB rate paths are moving apart enough to justify a larger hedge. For new bond purchases, require more spread over Bunds to add French sovereign exposure while the fiscal outlook is unsettled. Do not raise the required premium across all euro-area sovereigns or corporates: the observed repricing is French, not market-wide. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250605122808/https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/pr/date/2025/html/ecb.mp250605~3b5f67d007.en.html#:~:text=The%20Governing%20Council%20is%20determined%20to%20ensure%20that%20inflation,purchase%20programme%20%28APP%29%20and%20pandemic%20emergency%20purchase%20programme%20%28PEPP%29) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250829140531/https://think.ing.com/downloads/pdf/article/market-impact-of-french-political-turmoil#:~:text=Article%20%7C%2027%20August%202025%201%20THINK%20economic%20and,the%20uncertainty%20from%20both%20a%20political%20and%20fiscal%20perspective.)

## Evidence

Hammack’s “modestly restrictive” characterization and the account of a run of ECB cuts ending in a cautious neutral stance by August are unverified question premises. Even taken at face value, they describe policy levels, not the next moves: a restrictive Fed could cut while a neutral ECB holds. The ECB’s June decision lowered its deposit rate to 2.00% but left later meetings open. The US market-pricing report concerns Hammack’s appointment in 2024, not this year’s December contracts. Neither it nor one policymaker’s assessment establishes the FOMC’s expected path. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250605122808/https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/pr/date/2025/html/ecb.mp250605~3b5f67d007.en.html#:~:text=The%20Governing%20Council%20is%20determined%20to%20ensure%20that%20inflation,purchase%20programme%20%28APP%29%20and%20pandemic%20emergency%20purchase%20programme%20%28PEPP%29) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250724175633/https://www.cnbc.com/2024/05/29/goldman-sachs-partner-beth-hammack-to-succeed-mester-as-cleveland-fed-leader.html#:~:text=%22Beth%20has%20a%20deep%20understanding%20of%20financial%20markets%20and,six%20cuts.%20Don%E2%80%99t%20miss%20these%20insights%20from%20CNBC%20PRO) [4](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1276135291)

## Outlook

The FX base case is episodic volatility rather than a sustained policy-driven fall in the euro. Test it by comparing the move from current overnight rates to December rates implied by same-date dollar and euro overnight index swaps, then tracking revisions to that gap. An unchanged dollar rate advantage is not fresh news for spot. The strongest dollar-bullish alternative is that markets remove expected Fed cuts while adding ECB cuts; a persistent widening in the dollar’s favour would justify increasing protection on euro receipts measured in dollars. Faster expected Fed easing would point the other way. Without paired curves or option prices, neither the direction of repricing nor a trading range is established. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250605122808/https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/pr/date/2025/html/ecb.mp250605~3b5f67d007.en.html#:~:text=The%20Governing%20Council%20is%20determined%20to%20ensure%20that%20inflation,purchase%20programme%20%28APP%29%20and%20pandemic%20emergency%20purchase%20programme%20%28PEPP%29) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250829140531/https://think.ing.com/downloads/pdf/article/market-impact-of-french-political-turmoil#:~:text=Article%20%7C%2027%20August%202025%201%20THINK%20economic%20and,the%20uncertainty%20from%20both%20a%20political%20and%20fiscal%20perspective.)

For sovereigns, the base case is a persistent French premium, not disorderly euro-area fragmentation. The late-August OAT–Bund widening measures French underperformance at matched maturity; a parallel rise in French and German yields would not. The ECB’s portfolio runoff removes reinvestment demand, while its Transmission Protection Instrument addresses disorderly markets, not every fiscal repricing. A credible French budget followed by sustained OAT–Bund narrowing would weaken the case for extra compensation. Rapid widening that spreads to other sovereigns would instead justify broader protection and raise the risk of an FX shock. [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250829140531/https://think.ing.com/downloads/pdf/article/market-impact-of-french-political-turmoil#:~:text=Article%20%7C%2027%20August%202025%201%20THINK%20economic%20and,the%20uncertainty%20from%20both%20a%20political%20and%20fiscal%20perspective.) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250605122808/https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/pr/date/2025/html/ecb.mp250605~3b5f67d007.en.html#:~:text=The%20APP%20and%20PEPP%20portfolios%20are%20declining%20at%20a,at%20a%20press%20conference%20starting%20at%2014%3A45%20CET%20today.)

## What would change the view

For corporates, distinguish refinancing risk from a higher risk-free yield. A rise in corporate yields that matches the euro swap curve is not evidence of a wider credit premium; equally, falling swap rates can mask spread widening. Scrutinise trade-exposed issuers first: the ECB flagged weaker investment and exports but also more favourable financing conditions. Require more compensation broadly if weaker earnings or refinancing access coincides with sustained widening in option-adjusted spreads across rating and maturity peers. No corporate spread series is supplied to show that this has happened or to size the premium. [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20250605122808/https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/pr/date/2025/html/ecb.mp250605~3b5f67d007.en.html#:~:text=Staff%20see%20real%20GDP%20growth%20averaging%200.9%25%20in%202025%2C,inflation%20would%20be%20higher%20than%20in%20the%20baseline%20projections.)

## Sources

1. [Monetary policy decisions](https://web.archive.org/web/20250605122808/https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/pr/date/2025/html/ecb.mp250605~3b5f67d007.en.html#:~:text=The%20Governing%20Council%20is%20determined%20to%20ensure%20that%20inflation,purchase%20programme%20%28APP%29%20and%20pandemic%20emergency%20purchase%20programme%20%28PEPP%29), available by 2025-06-05.

question: How does the aggressive institutional accumulation of POOL shares by Berkshire Hathaway and Wellington Management through Q1 2025 reconcile with significant insider liquidation by Manuel Perez de la Mesa and a reported short interest of 8.88% of float?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-05-11

**Research question**
How does the aggressive institutional accumulation of POOL shares by Berkshire Hathaway and Wellington Management through Q1 2025 reconcile with significant insider liquidation by Manuel Perez de la Mesa and a reported short interest of 8.88% of float?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Evidence

Test accumulation separately for each manager. The Berkshire excerpt names insurance affiliates; the Wellington profile describes an adviser to institutions. Neither shows a change in POOL holdings. Compare quarter-end POOL share counts with the preceding quarter for the same reporting entities, without double-counting affiliates, and check when each filing became public. A large ending stake can be an old position, and a rise in its dollar value can reflect price rather than purchases. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20241109161851/https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1067983/000095012324008740/xslForm13F_X02/primary_doc.xml#:~:text=SEC%20File%20No.%20%28if%20applicable%29%20Berkshire%20Hathaway%20Homestate%20Insurance%20Co.%20Berkshire%20Hathaway%20Life%20Insurance%20Co%20of%20Nebraska) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20241109161851/https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1067983/000095012324008740/xslForm13F_X02/primary_doc.xml#:~:text=Number%20of%20Other%20Included%20Managers%3A%20Form%2013F%20Information%20Table%20Entry%20Total%3A%20Form%2013F%20Information%20Table%20Value%20Total%3A) [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1287097379)

Even if confirmed, the three positions would not contradict one another. A manager can add shares while an insider reduces personal exposure and other investors maintain shorts. No insider transaction filing is supplied: the useful test is what fraction of Perez de la Mesa’s prior stake he sold, what he retained and whether the sales were prearranged. Short interest, meanwhile, measures open positions on a settlement date, not new bearish trades during the quarter. The supplied definition gives neither a POOL balance nor a matching float denominator. Without those and a prior observation, neither the reported level nor a rise in bearish positioning is established. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20190902131743/https://www.nasdaq.com/quotes/short-interest.aspx#:~:text=The%20total%20number%20of%20shares%20of%20a%20security%20that,as%20of%20the%20settlement%20date.%20Average%20Daily%20Share%20Volume) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20190902131743/https://www.nasdaq.com/quotes/short-interest.aspx#:~:text=About%20the%20Short%20Interest%20Page%20Short%20selling%20is%20the,is%20used%20for%20accounting%20for%20long%20or%20short%20positions.)

## What would change the view

The base case is to give ownership no directional weight, not to infer that POOL’s business is deteriorating. The operating evidence describes a post-lockdown sales slowdown, not the quarter’s revenue, margin or earnings. The strongest bullish alternative is that both managers added materially ahead of a demand recovery while the insider reduced exposure for unrelated reasons. Comparable filings showing sizable share-count increases by both managers would establish the buying; improving sales and operating margin in company results would separately support the recovery thesis. Neither would establish the insider’s motive. [6](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1257538897) [7](https://web.archive.org/web/20250427161500/https://www.ftc.gov/legal-library/browse/cases-proceedings/1010115-pool-corporation#:~:text=Professional%20Services%20%28Non-Health%20Care%29%20Pool%20Corporation%2C%20the%20largest%20distributor,Anticompetitively%20to%20Stop%20Manufacturers%20From%20Selling%20Products%20to%20Competitors)

question: How does Eli Lilly’s resolution of the tirzepatide shortage and its legal strategy against compounding competitors like Hims & Hers affect the valuation of its GLP-1 franchise as it targets secondary indications like heart failure, sleep apnea, and MASH?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-07-16

**Research question**
How does Eli Lilly’s resolution of the tirzepatide shortage and its legal strategy against compounding competitors like Hims & Hers affect the valuation of its GLP-1 franchise as it targets secondary indications like heart failure, sleep apnea, and MASH?

## Answer

As of 2025-07-16, I would raise Lilly’s U.S. tirzepatide valuation modestly if the forecast still reflects diabetes and weight management alone. The reason is sleep apnea: approval and access through certain Medicare plans support BMO’s estimate of ~$1.4B in additional peak revenue opportunity. That is a benchmark for sales, not cash flow or present value. If the forecast already includes that access, I would hold the valuation. Neither the FDA’s shortage decision nor Novo Nordisk’s breakup with Hims & Hers establishes additional Lilly sales. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250312163528/https://www.biospace.com/policy/lilly-wins-medicare-coverage-for-zepbound-in-sleep-apnea#:~:text=The%20news%20is%20a%20%E2%80%9Csignificant%20positive%E2%80%9D%20for%20Lilly%2C%20BMO,of%20obesity%20interventions%2C%20including%20bariatric%20surgery%20and%20behavioral%20therapy.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250312163528/https://www.biospace.com/policy/lilly-wins-medicare-coverage-for-zepbound-in-sleep-apnea#:~:text=According%20to%20BMO%20Capital%20Markets%2C%20Medicare%20coverage%20of%20Lilly%E2%80%99s,for%20use%20in%20obstructive%20sleep%20apnea%2C%20according%20to%20CNBC.) [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1299635046) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250627145318/https://www.wsj.com/health/pharma/novo-nordisk-ends-partnership-with-hims-hers-bd9241cf#:~:text=Novo%20Nordisk%20abruptly%20ended%20its%20partnership%20with%20Hims%20%26,Dow%20Jones%20%26%20Company%2C%20Inc.%20All%20Rights%20Reserved.%2087990cbe856818d5eddac44c7b1cdeb8)

## Evidence

U.S. compounder recapture: carry no separate sales uplift in the base case pending evidence of switching. The FDA, not Lilly, declared the shortage over in October 2024; litigation delayed enforcement, so the declaration was not a date on which compounded prescriptions automatically became branded sales. Estimate recapture as displaced U.S. compounded tirzepatide patients who would not otherwise use the brand × share switching to Lilly × months retained × realized monthly net price. None of those inputs is quantified here. No booked uplift is a valuation choice, not an estimate that no patients switched. [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1299635046) [5](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1297260924)

Attribute no sales to a Lilly action against Hims & Hers. The reported dispute was Novo Nordisk’s termination of a Wegovy partnership over alleged copycat sales and deceptive marketing. The separate shortage litigation cited here was brought by compounders challenging the FDA decision. Neither event verifies that Lilly sued Hims, that Hims stopped dispensing tirzepatide, or that its customers moved to Lilly. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250627145318/https://www.wsj.com/health/pharma/novo-nordisk-ends-partnership-with-hims-hers-bd9241cf#:~:text=Novo%20Nordisk%20abruptly%20ended%20its%20partnership%20with%20Hims%20%26,Dow%20Jones%20%26%20Company%2C%20Inc.%20All%20Rights%20Reserved.%2087990cbe856818d5eddac44c7b1cdeb8) [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20250627145318/https://www.wsj.com/health/pharma/novo-nordisk-ends-partnership-with-hims-hers-bd9241cf#:~:text=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wsj.com%2Fhealth%2Fpharma%2Fnovo-nordisk-ends-partnership-with-hims-hers-bd9241cf%20Hims%20%26%20Hers%20Stock%20Drops%20More%20Than%2030%25,citing%20allegations%20of%20deceptive%20marketing%20practices%20and%20drug%20compounding) [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1299635046)

## Outlook

Sleep apnea is the indication to include in forecast cash flow. The December 2024 approval covers moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity; coverage for that use is not blanket Medicare coverage for weight loss. BMO’s ~$1B Medicare component is inside its peak sales estimate, not additive. Model paid treatment months that apnea coverage adds relative to the existing forecast, at realized net price; deduct incremental production, selling costs, taxes and investment, then discount the uptake schedule. The sources give no ramp or cash margin to support a dollar present value. [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1299635046) [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250312163528/https://www.biospace.com/policy/lilly-wins-medicare-coverage-for-zepbound-in-sleep-apnea#:~:text=The%20news%20is%20a%20%E2%80%9Csignificant%20positive%E2%80%9D%20for%20Lilly%2C%20BMO,of%20obesity%20interventions%2C%20including%20bariatric%20surgery%20and%20behavioral%20therapy.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250312163528/https://www.biospace.com/policy/lilly-wins-medicare-coverage-for-zepbound-in-sleep-apnea#:~:text=According%20to%20BMO%20Capital%20Markets%2C%20Medicare%20coverage%20of%20Lilly%E2%80%99s,for%20use%20in%20obstructive%20sleep%20apnea%2C%20according%20to%20CNBC.)

Heart failure has clinical value but less certain commercial value. In patients with obesity and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, the phase III trial reported a 38% relative reduction versus placebo in a composite outcome, not a mortality reduction of that size. Retain a contingent upside case: weight discounted cash flows from newly covered treatment months by the likelihood of a label and payer access. The trial does not establish either, or quantify additional paid use, so I would not add a dollar uplift to the base case. [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1299635046)

MASH merits no separate base-case cash flow on this record. Unlike sleep apnea, there is no supplied evidence of a MASH label or payer access; unlike heart failure, there is no supplied MASH trial result on which to base a probability of success. That limits the estimate, not the drug’s potential. Revisit it with indication-specific efficacy, a regulatory path and evidence of an addressable population not already receiving tirzepatide. [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1299635046)

## What would change the view

The strongest case for holding valuation even before adding apnea is that coverage changes who pays, not how long or how many patients take tirzepatide, while price-sensitive compound users stop rather than switch. Test this with linked dispensing histories, paid claims and net receipts. Remove months already forecast for branded diabetes or obesity use. Assign remaining months enabled by apnea coverage to apnea, even for a former compound user; count only residual verified switches as recapture. Apply the same rule to later labels. Sustained growth in unique paid treatment months at stable net prices supports a raise; diagnosis changes on existing fills do not. [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250312163528/https://www.biospace.com/policy/lilly-wins-medicare-coverage-for-zepbound-in-sleep-apnea#:~:text=According%20to%20BMO%20Capital%20Markets%2C%20Medicare%20coverage%20of%20Lilly%E2%80%99s,for%20use%20in%20obstructive%20sleep%20apnea%2C%20according%20to%20CNBC.) [5](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1297260924) [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1299635046) [7](https://web.archive.org/web/20240408143047/https://www.fda.gov/drugs/new-drugs-fda-cders-new-molecular-entities-and-new-therapeutic-biological-products/new-drug-therapy-approvals-2022#:~:text=Camzyos%20%28mavacamten%29%20capsules%20to%20improve%20functional%20capacity%20and%20symptoms,received%20at%20least%20two%20prior%20therapies%2C%20including%20a%20chemotherapy.)

## Sources

1. [Lilly Wins Medicare Coverage for Zepbound in Sleep Apnea - BioSpace](https://web.archive.org/web/20250312163528/https://www.biospace.com/policy/lilly-wins-medicare-coverage-for-zepbound-in-sleep-apnea#:~:text=The%20news%20is%20a%20%E2%80%9Csignificant%20positive%E2%80%9D%20for%20Lilly%2C%20BMO,of%20obesity%20interventions%2C%20including%20bariatric%20surgery%20and%20behavioral%20therapy.), available by 2025-03-12.
2. [Lilly Wins Medicare Coverage for Zepbound in Sleep Apnea - BioSpace](https://web.archive.org/web/20250312163528/https://www.biospace.com/policy/lilly-wins-medicare-coverage-for-zepbound-in-sleep-apnea#:~:text=According%20to%20BMO%20Capital%20Markets%2C%20Medicare%20coverage%20of%20Lilly%E2%80%99s,for%20use%20in%20obstructive%20sleep%20apnea%2C%20according%20to%20CNBC.), available by 2025-03-12.
3. [Tirzepatide](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1299635046), available by 2025-07-09.

question: How has MARA Holdings' strategic shift toward a Bitcoin-treasury model, characterized by debt-financed BTC accumulation and mirroring MicroStrategy’s capital structure, impacted its equity valuation and fundamental risk profile relative to its core operational mining performance and sector peers like Riot Platforms?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-06-10

**Research question**
How has MARA Holdings' strategic shift toward a Bitcoin-treasury model, characterized by debt-financed BTC accumulation and mirroring MicroStrategy’s capital structure, impacted its equity valuation and fundamental risk profile relative to its core operational mining performance and sector peers like Riot Platforms?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

By 2025-06-10, MARA had adopted MicroStrategy’s practice of borrowing to buy Bitcoin without ceasing to be a miner. Its $1 billion convertible offering helped acquire 6,474 Bitcoin, making the share price a claim on both a leveraged treasury and a mining business. The evidence establishes that change in exposure, not how the market priced it: it shows neither a June treasury premium nor a discount after separating mining value. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250225011539/https://cointelegraph.com/news/mara-purchases-6-474-bitcoin-convertible-notes-offering#:~:text=Mining%20company%20MARA%2C%20formerly%20Marathon%20Digital%2C%20updated%20investors%20on,through%20its%20recent%200%25%20%241%20billion%20convertible%20note%20offering.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250225011539/https://cointelegraph.com/news/mara-purchases-6-474-bitcoin-convertible-notes-offering#:~:text=Related%3A%20Crypto%20miner%20MARA%20wants%20US%20moving%20quicker%20to,%243%20billion%20senior%20convertible%20note%20issue%20at%200%25%20interest.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250515045038/https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/mara-reports-214m-q1-revenue-grows-bitcoin-holdings-47531-btc#:~:text=Despite%20the%20revenue%20boost%2C%20MARA%20posted%20a%20net%20loss,edge%20inference%E2%80%94including%20energy%20management%2C%20load%20balancing%2C%20and%20advanced%20cooling.%E2%80%9D) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250603202412/https://crypto.news/top-u-s-bitcoin-miners-report-strong-may-performance-and-infrastructure-growth/#:~:text=Riot%20Platforms%20mined%20514%20BTC%20in%20May%2C%20marking%20an,down%20on%20infrastructure%2C%20vertical%20integration%2C%20and%20strategic%20treasury%20management.)

## Evidence

The usable valuation anchor is gross, not debt-adjusted. At March 31, 2025, MARA’s 47,531 BTC at $82,534 each were worth about $3.9 billion, before debt and excluding the mines. That value belonged to a company with 346,279,403 outstanding common shares, up from 340,258,453 at the prior year-end. Share-count growth was already observable; it was not a measure of future note conversion. Neither the gross balance nor the later approximate BTC quote is a June equity valuation. [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250515045038/https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/mara-reports-214m-q1-revenue-grows-bitcoin-holdings-47531-btc#:~:text=MARA%20Holdings%2C%20Inc.%20%28NASDAQ%3A%20MARA%29%20has%20reported%20first%20quarter,valued%20around%20%243.9%20billion%20as%20of%20March%2031%2C%202025.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250515045038/https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/mara-reports-214m-q1-revenue-grows-bitcoin-holdings-47531-btc#:~:text=Despite%20the%20revenue%20boost%2C%20MARA%20posted%20a%20net%20loss,edge%20inference%E2%80%94including%20energy%20management%2C%20load%20balancing%2C%20and%20advanced%20cooling.%E2%80%9D) [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20250515032924/https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1507605/000150760525000009/mara-20250331.htm#:~:text=Commitments%20and%20Contingencies%20%28Note%2016%29%20Preferred%20stock%2C%20par%20value,at%20March%2031%2C%202025%20and%20December%2031%2C%202024%2C%20respectively)

The MicroStrategy analogy holds for the financing instrument, not for the entire capital structure. Both issued 0% convertibles, but MicroStrategy’s cited issue was $3 billion, and MARA used $200 million to repurchase part of an older note issue. Treating MARA’s whole offering as incremental BTC investment would therefore overstate the purchase. A zero coupon saves cash interest; it does not remove the principal claim if BTC falls or the potential for conversion to spread upside across more shares. MARA’s earlier reported BTC yield per share measured coin accumulation, not a shareholder return net of debt. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250225011539/https://cointelegraph.com/news/mara-purchases-6-474-bitcoin-convertible-notes-offering#:~:text=Mining%20company%20MARA%2C%20formerly%20Marathon%20Digital%2C%20updated%20investors%20on,through%20its%20recent%200%25%20%241%20billion%20convertible%20note%20offering.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250225011539/https://cointelegraph.com/news/mara-purchases-6-474-bitcoin-convertible-notes-offering#:~:text=Related%3A%20Crypto%20miner%20MARA%20wants%20US%20moving%20quicker%20to,%243%20billion%20senior%20convertible%20note%20issue%20at%200%25%20interest.) [7](https://web.archive.org/web/20250225011539/https://cointelegraph.com/news/mara-purchases-6-474-bitcoin-convertible-notes-offering#:~:text=According%20to%20the%20announcement%2C%20the%20company%20purchased%20an%20additional,strategy%20that%20is%20growing%20in%20popularity%20among%20corporate%20institutions.)

Mining improved on operating measures even as BTC drove the reported loss. MARA mined 2,286 BTC and bought 340 in the quarter; cost per petahash per day fell 25% to $28.5, and revenue rose to $213.9 million. Yet the $510.2 million BTC fair-value loss accounted for nearly all of the $533.4 million net loss by magnitude. The net loss is therefore a poor measure of mine performance, but subtracting the BTC mark does not yield mining profit either: it does not isolate operating expenses, corporate costs or the capital needed to sustain production. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250515045038/https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/mara-reports-214m-q1-revenue-grows-bitcoin-holdings-47531-btc#:~:text=Despite%20the%20revenue%20boost%2C%20MARA%20posted%20a%20net%20loss,edge%20inference%E2%80%94including%20energy%20management%2C%20load%20balancing%2C%20and%20advanced%20cooling.%E2%80%9D) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250515045038/https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/mara-reports-214m-q1-revenue-grows-bitcoin-holdings-47531-btc#:~:text=MARA%20Holdings%2C%20Inc.%20%28NASDAQ%3A%20MARA%29%20has%20reported%20first%20quarter,valued%20around%20%243.9%20billion%20as%20of%20March%2031%2C%202025.)

## Outlook

The base case is to value both miners’ operations separately from their coins and assign MARA no extra value merely for borrowing to hold BTC. A BTC decline can reduce both MARA’s treasury cushion and the dollar revenue from newly mined coins while note principal stays fixed. The strongest alternative is that MARA’s lower unit costs support a higher mining valuation than Riot’s. The observable signal would be sustained superior mining cash flow after sustaining investment, measured over the same periods. Riot’s 514 BTC mined in May cannot be compared directly with MARA’s quarterly output, and Riot’s data-center investment means infrastructure upside is not unique to MARA. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250515045038/https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/mara-reports-214m-q1-revenue-grows-bitcoin-holdings-47531-btc#:~:text=Despite%20the%20revenue%20boost%2C%20MARA%20posted%20a%20net%20loss,edge%20inference%E2%80%94including%20energy%20management%2C%20load%20balancing%2C%20and%20advanced%20cooling.%E2%80%9D) [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250225011539/https://cointelegraph.com/news/mara-purchases-6-474-bitcoin-convertible-notes-offering#:~:text=Mining%20company%20MARA%2C%20formerly%20Marathon%20Digital%2C%20updated%20investors%20on,through%20its%20recent%200%25%20%241%20billion%20convertible%20note%20offering.) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250603202412/https://crypto.news/top-u-s-bitcoin-miners-report-strong-may-performance-and-infrastructure-growth/#:~:text=Riot%20Platforms%20mined%20514%20BTC%20in%20May%2C%20marking%20an,down%20on%20infrastructure%2C%20vertical%20integration%2C%20and%20strategic%20treasury%20management.)

## What would change the view

To settle the June pricing question, subtract an independently estimated value of mining and other operations from each company’s same-date market capitalization. Compare the remainder with marked BTC plus nonoperating cash less debt: a remainder above that benchmark indicates a treasury premium; below it, a discount. Test conversion separately by removing converted principal and adding the resulting shares, not by charging shareholders for both. The record lacks matched closing prices, updated holdings, net debt, conversion inputs and standalone operating values for both firms. A premium would be a higher price paid, not itself compensation: the case for paying it would require stronger prospective cash flow or growth in debt-adjusted BTC value per diluted share than Riot offers. [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250515045038/https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/mara-reports-214m-q1-revenue-grows-bitcoin-holdings-47531-btc#:~:text=MARA%20Holdings%2C%20Inc.%20%28NASDAQ%3A%20MARA%29%20has%20reported%20first%20quarter,valued%20around%20%243.9%20billion%20as%20of%20March%2031%2C%202025.) question: Given the declining market conviction for a 25 bp rate cut at the December FOMC meeting compared to near-certainty in October, how are evolving economic conditions and Fed signaling impacting the terminal rate outlook for year-end 2025?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-11-10

**Research question**
Given the declining market conviction for a 25 bp rate cut at the December FOMC meeting compared to near-certainty in October, how are evolving economic conditions and Fed signaling impacting the terminal rate outlook for year-end 2025?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-11-10, retain a December Fed cut of 1/4 percentage point as the year-end 2025 base case, but raise the probability of a hold at 3-3/4 to 4 percent. Slower hiring still warrants some insurance against job losses. Chair Powell’s warning matters because it leaves the year-end target a full cut higher if the FOMC waits; it does not establish that a majority now favors waiting. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20251029182359/https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20251029a.htm#:~:text=In%20support%20of%20its%20goals%20and%20in%20light%20of,employment%20and%20returning%20inflation%20to%20its%202%20percent%20objective.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20251029182359/https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20251029a.htm#:~:text=For%20release%20at%202%3A00%20p.m.%20EDT%20Available%20indicators%20suggest,that%20downside%20risks%20to%20employment%20rose%20in%20recent%20months.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20251102151012/https://www.economicgreenfield.com/2025/10/30/jerome-powells-october-29-2025-press-conference-notable-aspects/#:~:text=In%20the%20near%20term%2C%20risks%20to%20inflation%20are%20tilted,of%20Jerome%20Powell%E2%80%99s%20responses%20as%20indicated%20to%20various%20questions%3A)

## Evidence

The October vote and Powell’s caution answer different questions. Miran wanted a larger October cut, Schmid wanted none, and the rest backed the cut that passed. Powell located the sharper disagreement in December: stronger growth forecasts and a labor market cooling gradually rather than abruptly gave members a reason to wait. October’s majority was for that meeting’s cut, not for a sequence of cuts. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20251029182359/https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20251029a.htm#:~:text=In%20assessing%20the%20appropriate%20stance%20of%20monetary%20policy%2C%20the,range%20for%20the%20federal%20funds%20rate%20at%20this%20meeting.) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20251102151012/https://www.economicgreenfield.com/2025/10/30/jerome-powells-october-29-2025-press-conference-notable-aspects/#:~:text=STEVE%20LIESMAN.%20Steve%20Liesman%2C%20CNBC.%20Mr.%20Chairman%2C%20can%20you,a%20percent%20of%20GDP%20and%20become%20a%20tightening%20factor%3F)

## What would change the view

Make a hold the base case if hiring stabilizes while successive inflation readings suggest that tariff-related price increases are spreading or persisting. That combination would weaken the employment rationale for another cut and challenge Powell’s view that tariffs mainly lift the price level once. Conversely, further slowing in hiring and rising unemployment without broader price pressure would strengthen the cut case even if spending remains resilient. [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20251102151012/https://www.economicgreenfield.com/2025/10/30/jerome-powells-october-29-2025-press-conference-notable-aspects/#:~:text=Our%20monetary%20policy%20actions%20are%20guided%20by%20our%20dual,price%20level%20does%20not%20become%20an%20ongoing%20inflation%20problem.) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20251029182359/https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20251029a.htm#:~:text=In%20assessing%20the%20appropriate%20stance%20of%20monetary%20policy%2C%20the,range%20for%20the%20federal%20funds%20rate%20at%20this%20meeting.) [7](https://web.archive.org/web/20251102151012/https://www.economicgreenfield.com/2025/10/30/jerome-powells-october-29-2025-press-conference-notable-aspects/#:~:text=VICTORIA%20GUIDA.%20Hi%2C%20Victoria%20Guida%20from%20Politico.%20On%20AI%2C,slowing%20so%20much%2C%20even%20though%20consumer%20spending%20is%20strong%3F)

question: Following the 464.6% surge in short interest and conflicting rating actions by UBS, Citigroup, and Kepler Capital Markets, what fundamental factors in Leonardo S.p.a.’s (FINMY) Italian defense and aerospace operations support its 'Moderate Buy' consensus rating and 2025 growth outlook?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-10-28

**Research question**
Following the 464.6% surge in short interest and conflicting rating actions by UBS, Citigroup, and Kepler Capital Markets, what fundamental factors in Leonardo S.p.a.’s (FINMY) Italian defense and aerospace operations support its 'Moderate Buy' consensus rating and 2025 growth outlook?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-10-28, Leonardo’s first-half orders of € 11.2 BN exceeded revenues of € 8.9 BN. That pace supports CEO Roberto Cingolani’s higher 2025 order target, and earnings growth in helicopters and defence electronics supports a cautiously positive operating view. The cash target is less secure: cash outflow narrowed, but cash generation still depends on the second half. These fundamentals are consistent with the question’s reported FINMY “Moderate Buy”; they establish neither the consensus itself nor that the shares are cheap. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250912183228/https://www.leonardo.com/en/press-release-detail/-/detail/30-07-2025-leonardo-1h2025-financial-results#:~:text=Leonardo%3A%20Board%20of%20Directors%20approved%20the%201H2025%20results.%20New,DEBT%20reduced%20Rome%2C%2030%20July%202025%2018%3A04%20Inside%20Information) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250912183228/https://www.leonardo.com/en/press-release-detail/-/detail/30-07-2025-leonardo-1h2025-financial-results#:~:text=%28%2A%29%20Not%20including%20the%20contribution%20from%20the%20Underwater%20Armaments,until%202024%20and%20sold%20to%20Fincantieri%20in%20early%202025.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250912183228/https://www.leonardo.com/en/press-release-detail/-/detail/30-07-2025-leonardo-1h2025-financial-results#:~:text=Revenues%20%28%E2%82%ACbil.%208.9%29%20increased%20compared%20to%20the%20first%20six,litigation%20on%20international%20legacy%20programmes%2C%20including%20the%20NH90%20one.)

## Evidence

The order target calls for roughly a repeat of the first half, not a sharp acceleration. Management raised its forecast from ca. € 21 billion to ca. € 22.25 – 22.75 billion on better visibility into large contracts. First-half bookings were already close to half the revised range. That makes the target credible, but a large award slipping past year-end could cause a miss even if underlying demand holds. These are group orders across domestic and international markets, not orders attributable solely to Italy. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250912183228/https://www.leonardo.com/en/press-release-detail/-/detail/30-07-2025-leonardo-1h2025-financial-results#:~:text=%28%2A%29%202024%20restated%20figure%20as%20a%20result%20of%20the,22.75%20billion%2C%20factoring%20in%20the%20acquisition%20of%20jumbo%20orders) [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250912183228/https://www.leonardo.com/en/press-release-detail/-/detail/30-07-2025-leonardo-1h2025-financial-results#:~:text=Leonardo%3A%20Board%20of%20Directors%20approved%20the%201H2025%20results.%20New,DEBT%20reduced%20Rome%2C%2030%20July%202025%2018%3A04%20Inside%20Information)

Cash supports the direction of the guidance upgrade, not its delivery. First-half free operating cash flow was € -408 MLN, a smaller outflow than a year earlier. Leonardo credits collections and working-capital management, but higher dividends received also helped, while investment and earlier supplier payments absorbed cash. The usual first-half outflow makes a second-half recovery plausible; the available disclosure identifies a higher full-year cash target without giving its amount, so it cannot establish the cash still needed. [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250912183228/https://www.leonardo.com/en/press-release-detail/-/detail/30-07-2025-leonardo-1h2025-financial-results#:~:text=The%20Net%20Result%20before%20extraordinary%20transactions%20%28%E2%82%ACmil.%20273%2C%20%2B44.4%25,acceleration%20in%20supplier%20payments%20to%20underpin%20the%20growth%20path.) [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250912183228/https://www.leonardo.com/en/press-release-detail/-/detail/30-07-2025-leonardo-1h2025-financial-results#:~:text=Leonardo%3A%20Board%20of%20Directors%20approved%20the%201H2025%20results.%20New,DEBT%20reduced%20Rome%2C%2030%20July%202025%2018%3A04%20Inside%20Information)

The purported conflicting actions by UBS, Citigroup and Kepler Capital Markets are separate unverified question premises. There are no dated broker notes identifying the security, prior and new recommendations, or whether an action changed a rating rather than a price target. Nor is there a dated FINMY analyst tally to verify “Moderate Buy.” Management’s upgrade concerned operating guidance, not an equity recommendation; it cannot resolve those gaps. [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250912183228/https://www.leonardo.com/en/press-release-detail/-/detail/30-07-2025-leonardo-1h2025-financial-results#:~:text=%28%2A%29%20Not%20including%20the%20contribution%20from%20the%20Underwater%20Armaments,until%202024%20and%20sold%20to%20Fincantieri%20in%20early%202025.) [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20250905215335/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/business/2025/01/07/royal-navy-to-test-submarine-hunting-robot-helicopter/#:~:text=TELEGRAPH%20MEDIA%20GROUP%20HOLDINGS%20Ltd%20Thank%20you%20for%20your,at%20licensing%40telegraph.co.uk%20to%20discuss%20licensing%20options.%20Reference%20ID%3A%200.13d53e17.1757109215.364a7d4b)

Leonardo’s first-half EBITA margin improved modestly on a like-for-like basis. Excluding the sold Underwater Armaments & Systems business and using restated prior-period EBITA, EBITA grew faster than revenue. With the sold business retained in the prior-period comparison, EBITA growth instead slightly lagged revenue growth. Helicopters and defence electronics more than offset weakness in Aerostructures and ATR. That supports the group earnings outlook, but not a claim that margins improved across aerospace. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250912183228/https://www.leonardo.com/en/press-release-detail/-/detail/30-07-2025-leonardo-1h2025-financial-results#:~:text=Leonardo%3A%20Board%20of%20Directors%20approved%20the%201H2025%20results.%20New,DEBT%20reduced%20Rome%2C%2030%20July%202025%2018%3A04%20Inside%20Information) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250912183228/https://www.leonardo.com/en/press-release-detail/-/detail/30-07-2025-leonardo-1h2025-financial-results#:~:text=Revenues%20%28%E2%82%ACbil.%208.9%29%20increased%20compared%20to%20the%20first%20six,litigation%20on%20international%20legacy%20programmes%2C%20including%20the%20NH90%20one.)

## What would change the view

The base case is that large awards are booked by year-end, helicopters and defence electronics sustain comparable margins, and collections reverse the seasonal cash outflow. The strongest alternative is that demand remains firm but awards arrive late and investment and supplier payments run ahead of collections. The decisive checks are full-year bookings against the revised range and free operating cash flow against management’s target: an order hit without a cash recovery would validate demand, not cash conversion. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250912183228/https://www.leonardo.com/en/press-release-detail/-/detail/30-07-2025-leonardo-1h2025-financial-results#:~:text=%28%2A%29%202024%20restated%20figure%20as%20a%20result%20of%20the,22.75%20billion%2C%20factoring%20in%20the%20acquisition%20of%20jumbo%20orders) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250912183228/https://www.leonardo.com/en/press-release-detail/-/detail/30-07-2025-leonardo-1h2025-financial-results#:~:text=Revenues%20%28%E2%82%ACbil.%208.9%29%20increased%20compared%20to%20the%20first%20six,litigation%20on%20international%20legacy%20programmes%2C%20including%20the%20NH90%20one.) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250912183228/https://www.leonardo.com/en/press-release-detail/-/detail/30-07-2025-leonardo-1h2025-financial-results#:~:text=The%20Net%20Result%20before%20extraordinary%20transactions%20%28%E2%82%ACmil.%20273%2C%20%2B44.4%25,acceleration%20in%20supplier%20payments%20to%20underpin%20the%20growth%20path.)

## Sources

1. [Leonard's Financial Results 1H2025 - 30-07-2025 | Leonardo](https://web.archive.org/web/20250912183228/https://www.leonardo.com/en/press-release-detail/-/detail/30-07-2025-leonardo-1h2025-financial-results#:~:text=Leonardo%3A%20Board%20of%20Directors%20approved%20the%201H2025%20results.%20New,DEBT%20reduced%20Rome%2C%2030%20July%202025%2018%3A04%20Inside%20Information), available by 2025-09-12.
