question: How should Marathon Petroleum’s (MPC) valuation be reconciled given the sharp divergence between significant institutional divestment by mega-cap funds and aggressive accumulation by Wellington and insiders, alongside conflicting analyst price target adjustments observed in the first half of 2025?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-06-17

**Research question**
How should Marathon Petroleum’s (MPC) valuation be reconciled given the sharp divergence between significant institutional divestment by mega-cap funds and aggressive accumulation by Wellington and insiders, alongside conflicting analyst price target adjustments observed in the first half of 2025?

## Answer

As of 2025-06-17, no margin of safety was demonstrated for MPC. The evidence does not establish that the shares were undervalued, fairly valued or overvalued. The claimed large first-half 2025 sales by mega-cap funds, aggressive purchases by Wellington and insiders, and conflicting analyst target changes are unverified question premises. The divergence that can be measured is in operations: quarterly refining and marketing adjusted EBITDA fell to $489 million from $2.0 billion a year earlier, while midstream segment adjusted EBITDA rose to $1.7 billion from $1.6 billion. Those businesses need separate valuations. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250519130047/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/marathon-petroleum-corp-reports-first-quarter-2025-results-302447046.html#:~:text=Refining%20%26%20Marketing%20%28R%26M%29%20Segment%20adjusted%20EBITDA%20was%20%24489,per%20day%20%28bpd%29%20for%20the%20first%20quarter%20of%202025.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250519130047/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/marathon-petroleum-corp-reports-first-quarter-2025-results-302447046.html#:~:text=Refining%20operating%20costs%20were%20%245.74%20per%20barrel%20for%20the,driven%20by%20higher%20throughputs%20and%20growth%20from%20equity%20affiliates.)

## Evidence

The testable refining base case is a cyclical squeeze, not a permanent loss of earning power or a full return to the prior year's profitability. MPC attributed the decline mainly to narrower crack spreads; operating cost per barrel actually fell to $5.74 from $6.06. Value refining on sustainable throughput and realized margins across a full cycle, deducting operating costs, recurring turnaround spending, sustaining capital and cash taxes. Capitalizing either quarter's reported EBITDA would miss both the cycle and a material cash cost: the weaker quarter's EBITDA excluded $454 million of planned turnarounds. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250519130047/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/marathon-petroleum-corp-reports-first-quarter-2025-results-302447046.html#:~:text=Refining%20%26%20Marketing%20%28R%26M%29%20Segment%20adjusted%20EBITDA%20was%20%24489,per%20day%20%28bpd%29%20for%20the%20first%20quarter%20of%202025.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250519130047/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/marathon-petroleum-corp-reports-first-quarter-2025-results-302447046.html#:~:text=Refining%20operating%20costs%20were%20%245.74%20per%20barrel%20for%20the,driven%20by%20higher%20throughputs%20and%20growth%20from%20equity%20affiliates.)

The decisive comparison is what MPC shareholders were paying for refining after allowing for MPLX. Start with MPC's cutoff market capitalization, subtract the cutoff market value of the MPLX units MPC owned, and add parent-level net debt and the present value of corporate costs. Compare that implied refining price with the discounted through-cycle refining cash flows. Using MPLX equity value already accounts for its debt; neither that debt nor midstream earnings should be counted again. The excerpts supply no cutoff share or unit price, stake count, current MPC share count, parent net debt or full-cycle cash-flow history. Midstream's higher throughput supports its earnings, but does not fill those valuation gaps. [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250519130047/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/marathon-petroleum-corp-reports-first-quarter-2025-results-302447046.html#:~:text=Refining%20operating%20costs%20were%20%245.74%20per%20barrel%20for%20the,driven%20by%20higher%20throughputs%20and%20growth%20from%20equity%20affiliates.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250519130047/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/marathon-petroleum-corp-reports-first-quarter-2025-results-302447046.html#:~:text=Management%20uses%20certain%20financial%20measures%20to%20evaluate%20our%20operating,comparable%20to%20similarly%20titled%20measures%20reported%20by%20other%20companies.)

Give the reported trades and target changes no independent valuation weight. Wellington's profile describes an adviser, not a dated MPC holding; no comparable fund filings, insider transaction terms or dated analyst models are supplied. MPC's own $1.1 billion of repurchases is verified, but is not insider buying and creates value per remaining share only if the purchase price is below intrinsic value. An analyst cut based on a weak quarter and a raise based on stronger midcycle margins could both be internally consistent. Without their dates, horizons and assumptions, neither establishes a change in sustainable cash flow. [4](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1287097379) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250519130047/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/marathon-petroleum-corp-reports-first-quarter-2025-results-302447046.html#:~:text=%241.3%20billion%20of%20capital%20returned%2C%20inclusive%20of%20%241.1%20billion,2024.%20Adjustments%20are%20shown%20in%20the%20accompanying%20release%20tables.)

## What would change the view

The strongest bearish alternative is that weaker realized margins persist through a recovery in benchmark spreads, making historical refining cash flows too generous. Track MPC's realized margin, utilization and cash generation after turnaround and sustaining spending as spreads recover. A sustained cash-flow shortfall would lower the refining valuation even if MPLX held its value. Conversely, if the cutoff implied price of refining were materially below a conservative value supported by those cash flows, that would establish an undervaluation case regardless of which funds sold. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250519130047/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/marathon-petroleum-corp-reports-first-quarter-2025-results-302447046.html#:~:text=Refining%20%26%20Marketing%20%28R%26M%29%20Segment%20adjusted%20EBITDA%20was%20%24489,per%20day%20%28bpd%29%20for%20the%20first%20quarter%20of%202025.)

question: Despite passing fundamental value tests and receiving multiple analyst upgrades, Edison International (EIX) faces a contradiction between significant institutional accumulation and heavy insider selling. How do these divergent signals, coupled with recent wildfire liabilities in California, impact the risk-adjusted outlook for EIX's 2025 performance?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-05-27

**Research question**
Despite passing fundamental value tests and receiving multiple analyst upgrades, Edison International (EIX) faces a contradiction between significant institutional accumulation and heavy insider selling. How do these divergent signals, coupled with recent wildfire liabilities in California, impact the risk-adjusted outlook for EIX's 2025 performance?

## Answer

Keep Edison International (EIX) at benchmark weight versus regulated utilities for the rest of 2025. As of 2025-05-27, Edison had affirmed core EPS guidance of $5.94-$6.34, but the Eaton Fire destroyed more than 9,000 buildings, and the role of its utility, Southern California Edison (SCE), remained under investigation. The damage shows the scale of potential claims, not the bill for shareholders. The available evidence does not establish that the reported valuation discount is large enough to cover that risk. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250523112041/https://newsroom.edison.com/releases/edison-international-reports-first-quarter-2025-results#:~:text=Edison%20International%20Reports%20First-Quarter%202025%20Results%20%E2%80%A2%20First-quarter%202025,Sam%20Ramraj%2C%20%28626%29%20302-2540%20Media%20Relations%3A%20%28626%29%20302-2255%20News%40sce.com) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1292255518)

## Evidence

Core earnings are the better starting point for the value case. Edison earned $1.37 per share on a core basis in the first quarter, up from $1.13 a year earlier. GAAP EPS of $3.73 included $2.36 per share of non-core items. Even the core improvement at SCE primarily reflected lower interest expense from an earlier wildfire settlement. That recovery has economic value, but extrapolating the quarterly gain would overstate the evidence for recurring growth. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250523112041/https://newsroom.edison.com/releases/edison-international-reports-first-quarter-2025-results#:~:text=ROSEMEAD%2C%20Calif.%2C%20April%2029%2C%202025%20%E2%80%94%20Edison%20International%20%28NYSE%3A,core%20earnings%20to%20basic%20GAAP%20earnings.%202025%20Earnings%20Guidance) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250523112041/https://newsroom.edison.com/releases/edison-international-reports-first-quarter-2025-results#:~:text=2025%20Earnings%20Guidance%20as%20of%20April%2029%2C%202025%20%2AThere,2025.%20First-Quarter%202025%20Earnings%20Conference%20Call%20and%20Webcast%20Details)

Separate fire causation from who pays. Edison reportedly identified a line fault near the time of ignition; residents and local governments sued SCE. Neither the fault nor the suits establish liability, and Edison's stated belief that it acted prudently is not a regulatory finding. Edison paid over $2.7 billion in settlements related to an earlier fire and mudslides, and subsequently obtained some cost recovery. That history illustrates why gross settlements can differ from shareholder losses; it supplies neither an Eaton loss estimate nor a guarantee of recovery. [5](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1292230037) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1292255518)

Passing value screens, a discount to peers, multiple analyst upgrades, institutional accumulation and heavy insider selling are unverified question premises. If accurate, the upgrades and buying could reflect confidence in regulated earnings rather than new information about Eaton. Insider sales could reflect concern or diversification. Without dated analyst assumptions, comparable holdings periods and transaction filings showing how much insiders sold relative to what they retained, the apparent disagreement cannot be resolved. None of these signals materially changes the judgment while the investigation is open. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250523112041/https://newsroom.edison.com/releases/edison-international-reports-first-quarter-2025-results#:~:text=Edison%20International%20Reports%20First-Quarter%202025%20Results%20%E2%80%A2%20First-quarter%202025,Sam%20Ramraj%2C%20%28626%29%20302-2540%20Media%20Relations%3A%20%28626%29%20302-2255%20News%40sce.com)

## Outlook

Base case: Edison earns within its affirmed core range, but investors continue to demand a discount while the shareholder share of Eaton costs is unclear. Meeting guidance alone would confirm the earnings case, not justify a peer multiple. The strongest overweight case is that SCE is cleared or a binding recovery decision leaves shareholders with a limited bill. To act on it, compare EIX's price with the value of its guided core earnings at a comparable utility multiple: the gap per share should comfortably exceed a defensible present value of unrecovered claims and financing costs per share. Neither current peer pricing nor a net Eaton cost range is available here. An adverse finding coupled with substantial recovery disallowance would instead favor an underweight. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250523112041/https://newsroom.edison.com/releases/edison-international-reports-first-quarter-2025-results#:~:text=Edison%20International%20Reports%20First-Quarter%202025%20Results%20%E2%80%A2%20First-quarter%202025,Sam%20Ramraj%2C%20%28626%29%20302-2540%20Media%20Relations%3A%20%28626%29%20302-2255%20News%40sce.com) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250523112041/https://newsroom.edison.com/releases/edison-international-reports-first-quarter-2025-results#:~:text=ROSEMEAD%2C%20Calif.%2C%20April%2029%2C%202025%20%E2%80%94%20Edison%20International%20%28NYSE%3A,core%20earnings%20to%20basic%20GAAP%20earnings.%202025%20Earnings%20Guidance) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1292255518)

question: How should portfolio managers reconcile VTMX's significant institutional reshuffling and valuation expansion between April and July 2025 against its reported oversold technical indicators and the fundamental near-shoring tailwinds within the Mexican industrial real estate sector?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-07-29

**Research question**
How should portfolio managers reconcile VTMX's significant institutional reshuffling and valuation expansion between April and July 2025 against its reported oversold technical indicators and the fundamental near-shoring tailwinds within the Mexican industrial real estate sector?

## Answer

Hold VTMX as of 2025-07-29. Vesta’s shareholders authorized a US$ 150 million buyback, and Vesta reported US$ 36.4 million of first-quarter repurchases. Vesta is the identifiable buyer; no institutional buyer or seller can be named or sized from the supplied evidence. The April–July institutional reshuffling, valuation expansion and oversold readings are unverified question premises. Renewals support holding the position, but the limited volume of new leases argues against adding on a technical signal alone. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250430044435/https://ir.vesta.com.mx/news-events/press-releases/detail/128/corporacin-inmobiliaria-vesta-reports-first-quarter-2025-earnings-results#:~:text=At%20Vesta%27s%20General%20Shareholders%27%20Meeting%20on%20March%2019%2C%202025%2C,syndicated%20loan%20the%20Company%20had%20closed%20in%20December%202024.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250430044435/https://ir.vesta.com.mx/news-events/press-releases/detail/128/corporacin-inmobiliaria-vesta-reports-first-quarter-2025-earnings-results#:~:text=Based%20on%20first%20quarter%20performance%20and%20the%20Company%27s%20current,stabilized%20and%20same-store%20occupancy%20reached%2095.3%25%20and%2097.4%25%2C%20respectively.)

## Evidence

Separate the date a position was held from the date it was disclosed. Vesta’s reported repurchases cover the quarter ended March 31, 2025; the results available in April are not evidence of April buying. Likewise, a July institutional disclosure would establish a holding as of its stated measurement date, not a July trade. Without filings for comparable holding dates, the direction and scale of any manager’s net change are unknown. Even two position snapshots would not identify the trade dates. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250430044435/https://ir.vesta.com.mx/news-events/press-releases/detail/128/corporacin-inmobiliaria-vesta-reports-first-quarter-2025-earnings-results#:~:text=Corporaci%C3%B3n%20Inmobiliaria%20Vesta%20Reports%20First%20Quarter%202025%20Earnings%20Results,to%20US%24%2040.4%20million%20in%20the%20first%20quarter%202024.) [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250430044435/https://ir.vesta.com.mx/news-events/press-releases/detail/128/corporacin-inmobiliaria-vesta-reports-first-quarter-2025-earnings-results#:~:text=At%20Vesta%27s%20General%20Shareholders%27%20Meeting%20on%20March%2019%2C%202025%2C,syndicated%20loan%20the%20Company%20had%20closed%20in%20December%202024.)

Higher FFO per share was real, but the demonstrated increase was year over year, not April to July. First-quarter after-tax FFO was US$ 0.0416 per share versus US$ 0.0377 a year earlier. To test for a rerating, compare the April and July prices with the after-tax FFO per share known at each date, using the same earnings horizon and adjusting ordinary shares to the NYSE security’s share basis. A price rise proportionate to FFO growth requires no multiple expansion; a faster price rise does. Neither endpoint price nor an updated July denominator is supplied, so the attribution remains open. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250430044435/https://ir.vesta.com.mx/news-events/press-releases/detail/128/corporacin-inmobiliaria-vesta-reports-first-quarter-2025-earnings-results#:~:text=Adjusted%20EBITDA%20for%20the%20quarter%20increased%209.3%25%20to%20US%24,to%20lower%20other%20expenses%20during%20the%20first%20quarter%202024.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250430044435/https://ir.vesta.com.mx/news-events/press-releases/detail/128/corporacin-inmobiliaria-vesta-reports-first-quarter-2025-earnings-results#:~:text=Corporaci%C3%B3n%20Inmobiliaria%20Vesta%20Reports%20First%20Quarter%202025%20Earnings%20Results,to%20US%24%2040.4%20million%20in%20the%20first%20quarter%202024.)

## Outlook

The base case is tenant retention rather than a nearshoring-led surge in demand for additional space. Proximity to US customers is a plausible advantage, but the cited nearshoring example concerns services, not industrial lease commitments. Vesta signed 139 thousand sf of new contracts against 1.3 million sf of renewals. Same-store occupancy of 97.4% supports the existing rent stream; total occupancy of 92.8% leaves room for gains if new tenants take space. Reaffirmed revenue guidance supports holding, but is not a forecast of FFO per share. [5](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1298946003) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250430044435/https://ir.vesta.com.mx/news-events/press-releases/detail/128/corporacin-inmobiliaria-vesta-reports-first-quarter-2025-earnings-results#:~:text=Based%20on%20first%20quarter%20performance%20and%20the%20Company%27s%20current,stabilized%20and%20same-store%20occupancy%20reached%2095.3%25%20and%2097.4%25%2C%20respectively.)

## What would change the view

The strongest case for adding is that a short-term selloff has obscured improving lease demand. A stock can be oversold relative to its recent price path yet expensive relative to April FFO; without a dated indicator, lookback period and price history, the technical premise cannot distinguish a bargain from a continuing decline. Add if stronger new signings lift total occupancy and after-tax FFO per share grows enough to justify the verified price. Trim if renewals weaken and occupancy and FFO per share fall: a premium multiple, if confirmed, would leave holders exposed to both lower earnings and a lower price paid for each dollar of FFO. [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250430044435/https://ir.vesta.com.mx/news-events/press-releases/detail/128/corporacin-inmobiliaria-vesta-reports-first-quarter-2025-earnings-results#:~:text=Based%20on%20first%20quarter%20performance%20and%20the%20Company%27s%20current,stabilized%20and%20same-store%20occupancy%20reached%2095.3%25%20and%2097.4%25%2C%20respectively.) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250430044435/https://ir.vesta.com.mx/news-events/press-releases/detail/128/corporacin-inmobiliaria-vesta-reports-first-quarter-2025-earnings-results#:~:text=Adjusted%20EBITDA%20for%20the%20quarter%20increased%209.3%25%20to%20US%24,to%20lower%20other%20expenses%20during%20the%20first%20quarter%202024.)

## Sources

(VTMX)](https://web.archive.org/web/20250430044435/https://ir.vesta.com.mx/news-events/press-releases/detail/128/corporacin-inmobiliaria-vesta-reports-first-quarter-2025-earnings-results#:~:text=At%20Vesta%27s%20General%20Shareholders%27%20Meeting%20on%20March%2019%2C%202025%2C,syndicated%20loan%20the%20Company%20had%20closed%20in%20December%202024.), available by 2025-04-30.

question: How is BASF SE’s strategic pivot towards battery materials and the circular economy, supported by recent capital investments in Ludwigshafen and the Hy4Chem project, influencing its margin recovery and equity valuation relative to diversified peers like Dow and Eastman Chemical?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-05-27

**Research question**
How is BASF SE’s strategic pivot towards battery materials and the circular economy, supported by recent capital investments in Ludwigshafen and the Hy4Chem project, influencing its margin recovery and equity valuation relative to diversified peers like Dow and Eastman Chemical?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-05-27, BASF’s battery-materials and circular-economy investments offered longer-term upside, not a demonstrated margin recovery. In the first quarter of 2025, BASF’s EBITDA margin before special items was 15.1 percent, versus 15.4 percent a year earlier (-30 basis points). Surface Technologies was the exception to the segment earnings decline, but BASF did not identify how much of its improvement came from batteries or recycling. That evidence does not justify paying a premium to Dow or Eastman Chemical for earnings already delivered by the pivot; nor does it establish that BASF traded at a discount. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250523094443/https://www.basf.com/global/en/media/news-releases/2025/05/p-25-082#:~:text=BASF%20Group%E2%80%99s%20sales%20in%20the%20first%20quarter%20of%202025,amortization%20amounted%20to%20%E2%82%AC981%20million%20%28prior-year%20quarter%3A%20%E2%82%AC965%20million%29.)

## Evidence

Competitive pricing and lower volumes in several businesses help explain the group result without invoking the new projects. Sales fell €151 million to €17.4 billion despite currency support; EBITDA before special items fell €87 million to €2.6 billion. Lower bonus provisions helped earnings in Other, but BASF did not quantify group cost savings or isolate project effects. Reported profitability fell more sharply than the adjusted margin: EBITDA dropped to €2.2 billion from €2.7 billion, with special charges mainly related to the wind-project stake sale, not the battery ramp. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250523094443/https://www.basf.com/global/en/media/news-releases/2025/05/p-25-082#:~:text=BASF%20Group%E2%80%99s%20sales%20in%20the%20first%20quarter%20of%202025,amortization%20amounted%20to%20%E2%82%AC981%20million%20%28prior-year%20quarter%3A%20%E2%82%AC965%20million%29.)

Neither the operating comparison nor the market price of the pivot can be measured on a common basis. The peer material does not supply Dow’s and Eastman’s earnings for the same first quarter, or same-date prices, share counts and net debt for all three companies. Compare reported EBIT divided by sales first; reconcile special items and depreciation rather than comparing BASF’s adjusted EBITDA margin with a peer’s EBIT margin. For valuation, use cutoff-date market capitalization divided by trailing net earnings for P/E, and enterprise value divided by trailing EBITDA with consistent adjustments for EV/EBITDA. Even then, Eastman’s integrated intermediates operations and BASF’s agricultural exposure make a multiple gap an imperfect measure of what investors pay for batteries. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250523094443/https://www.basf.com/global/en/media/news-releases/2025/05/p-25-082#:~:text=BASF%20Group%E2%80%99s%20sales%20in%20the%20first%20quarter%20of%202025,amortization%20amounted%20to%20%E2%82%AC981%20million%20%28prior-year%20quarter%3A%20%E2%82%AC965%20million%29.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250523094443/https://www.basf.com/global/en/media/news-releases/2025/05/p-25-082#:~:text=The%20volatility%20of%20the%20tariff%20announcements%20and%20the%20unpredictability,further%20information%20from%20the%20internet%20at%20the%20following%20addresses%3A) [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1290069432)

Cash flow and cyclical exposure are better-supported reasons for valuation caution than a claim about project returns. First-quarter free cash flow was minus €1.8 billion, versus minus €1.5 billion a year earlier. Precious-metal trading and a settlement payment of around €300 million weighed on operating cash flow; the shortfall is not a measure of battery or hydrogen capex. BASF kept its outlook unchanged and expected local production to limit direct tariff exposure, but acknowledged indirect risk to automotive demand. Those risks matter to future utilization without proving that they caused a peer discount. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250523094443/https://www.basf.com/global/en/media/news-releases/2025/05/p-25-082#:~:text=Development%20of%20cash%20flows%20in%20the%20first%20quarter%20of,of%20%E2%82%AC2.25%20per%20share%20for%20the%202024%20business%20year) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250523094443/https://www.basf.com/global/en/media/news-releases/2025/05/p-25-082#:~:text=BASF%20leaves%202025%20outlook%20unchanged%20%E2%80%9CIn%20the%20first%20quarter,BASF%E2%80%99s%20business%20at%20this%20point%20in%20time%2C%E2%80%9D%20he%20added.)

C2. Ratio percent (%) — 2.2 ÷ 17.4 × 100 ≈ 12.643678 [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250523094443/https://www.basf.com/global/en/media/news-releases/2025/05/p-25-082#:~:text=BASF%20Group%E2%80%99s%20sales%20in%20the%20first%20quarter%20of%202025,amortization%20amounted%20to%20%E2%82%AC981%20million%20%28prior-year%20quarter%3A%20%E2%82%AC965%20million%29.)

C3. Ratio percent (%) — 2.7 ÷ 17.6 × 100 ≈ 15.340909 [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250523094443/https://www.basf.com/global/en/media/news-releases/2025/05/p-25-082#:~:text=BASF%20Group%E2%80%99s%20sales%20in%20the%20first%20quarter%20of%202025,amortization%20amounted%20to%20%E2%82%AC981%20million%20%28prior-year%20quarter%3A%20%E2%82%AC965%20million%29.)

C4. Spread basis points (basis points) — (C2 − C3) × 100 ≈ -269.723093 [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250523094443/https://www.basf.com/global/en/media/news-releases/2025/05/p-25-082#:~:text=BASF%20Group%E2%80%99s%20sales%20in%20the%20first%20quarter%20of%202025,amortization%20amounted%20to%20%E2%82%AC981%20million%20%28prior-year%20quarter%3A%20%E2%82%AC965%20million%29.)

## What would change the view

The strongest alternative is that battery or recycling margins were already improving, masked at group level by weakness elsewhere. Surface Technologies’ higher earnings on flat segment volume are consistent with that interpretation, but do not distinguish project gains from changes in costs or product mix. A disclosed earnings bridge linking sustained plant utilization and recovered-material savings to incremental EBITDA would change the margin judgment. Positive incremental cash flow after ramp spending would strengthen the case for a premium; comparable cutoff-date peer multiples would still be needed to judge whether investors had already paid for it. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250523094443/https://www.basf.com/global/en/media/news-releases/2025/05/p-25-082#:~:text=BASF%20Group%E2%80%99s%20sales%20in%20the%20first%20quarter%20of%202025,amortization%20amounted%20to%20%E2%82%AC981%20million%20%28prior-year%20quarter%3A%20%E2%82%AC965%20million%29.)

## Checked calculations

- C1. Spread basis points (basis points) — (15.1 − 15.4) × 100 = -30.0 [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250523094443/https://www.basf.com/global/en/media/news-releases/2025/05/p-25-082#:~:text=BASF%20Group%E2%80%99s%20sales%20in%20the%20first%20quarter%20of%202025,amortization%20amounted%20to%20%E2%82%AC981%20million%20%28prior-year%20quarter%3A%20%E2%82%AC965%20million%29.)

## Sources

1. [Strong footprint in all regions gives BASF resilience; EBITDA before special items nearly at prior-year quarter level](https://web.archive.org/web/20250523094443/https://www.basf.com/global/en/media/news-releases/2025/05/p-25-082#:~:text=BASF%20Group%E2%80%99s%20sales%20in%20the%20first%20quarter%20of%202025,amortization%20amounted%20to%20%E2%82%AC981%20million%20%28prior-year%20quarter%3A%20%E2%82%AC965%20million%29.), available by 2025-05-23.
2. [Strong footprint in all regions gives BASF resilience; EBITDA before special items nearly at prior-year quarter level](https://web.archive.org/web/20250523094443/https://www.basf.com/global/en/media/news-releases/2025/05/p-25-082#:~:text=The%20volatility%20of%20the%20tariff%20announcements%20and%20the%20unpredictability,further%20information%20from%20the%20internet%20at%20the%20following%20addresses%3A), available by 2025-05-23.
3. [Eastman Chemical Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1290069432), available by 2025-05-12.

question: How will PGIM's consolidation of its fixed income and private credit units into a $1 trillion platform under CEO Jacques Chappuis, combined with its strategic capital partnerships with Affirm and SoFi, drive AUM growth and influence Prudential Financial's broader asset management profitability through late 2025?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-07-21

**Research question**
How will PGIM's consolidation of its fixed income and private credit units into a $1 trillion platform under CEO Jacques Chappuis, combined with its strategic capital partnerships with Affirm and SoFi, drive AUM growth and influence Prudential Financial's broader asset management profitability through late 2025?

## Answer

As of 2025-07-21, keep both late-2025 forecasts unchanged: PGIM’s fee-earning AUM and its adjusted operating income contribution to Prudential Financial. The consolidation under Jacques Chappuis, the claimed trillion-dollar size of the combined credit platform and the capital partnerships with Affirm and SoFi are unverified premises of the question. The documented figure of more than $1 trillion covered all of PGIM as of December 2019, not the proposed credit platform. Even if the initiatives proceed as described, regrouping existing mandates adds no AUM, and access to loans does not establish that clients have deployed new fee-paying capital or that PGIM will earn enough in fees to cover its additional costs. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1301125242) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1299425876) [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1294406411)

## Evidence

The historical figures establish the scale of the businesses being regrouped, not a new inflow. PGIM Fixed Income reported $968 billion and PGIM Private Capital managed $101 billion at December 31, 2020. Neither figure measures current fee-earning assets or establishes which mandates fall inside the proposed platform. Likewise, the historical reference naming David Hunt as CEO does not establish who leads PGIM at the cutoff. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1301125242)

## Outlook

The strongest upside case is that a combined public and private credit team wins fresh client mandates because it can source Affirm point-of-sale loans and draw on SoFi’s lending business. Loan purchases alone would not confirm that case: buying loans with cash already in a PGIM mandate changes the portfolio, not its AUM. For the base case, exclude undeployed commitments and count only incremental deployed balances that earn PGIM fees and remain outstanding after repayments or sales. [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1299425876) [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1294406411)

## What would change the view

Raise the AUM forecast on disclosure of funded net new client balances attributable to the partnerships, reconciled to fee-earning AUM and separated from internal transfers. Raise the income forecast only when fees on average deployed balances, plus demonstrable operating savings, exceed incremental underwriting and integration costs during the forecast period. A late deployment could lift closing AUM with little in-period profit. Affirm’s merchant commissions and borrower interest are not PGIM management fees; the available evidence supplies no PGIM fee rate, deployment schedule or net expense benefit. [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1299425876) [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1301125242)

## Sources

1. [PGIM](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1301125242), available by 2025-07-18.
2. [Affirm Holdings](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1299425876), available by 2025-07-08.
3. [SoFi](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1294406411), available by 2025-06-07.

question: How is Aston Martin's turnaround strategy, led by CEO Adrian Hallmark, balancing immediate operational headwinds—such as vehicle recalls and workforce reductions—against the capital-intensive requirements of its hypercar program and EV transition, given the company's widening pre-tax losses?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-05-11

**Research question**
How is Aston Martin's turnaround strategy, led by CEO Adrian Hallmark, balancing immediate operational headwinds—such as vehicle recalls and workforce reductions—against the capital-intensive requirements of its hypercar program and EV transition, given the company's widening pre-tax losses?

## Answer

As of 2025-05-11, CEO Adrian Hallmark’s credible course is to prioritise Aston Martin’s Valhalla hybrid launch and spread battery-electric investment over a longer period. The planned £125 million capital package and the move to 2030 for the first EV give him room to do that, but they do not establish that both programmes are funded. The base case is a launch supported by external capital, not a turnaround already paying for itself. Neither another raise nor another delay is yet demonstrably necessary. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1287882819) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1285707238)

## Evidence

“Widening pre-tax losses” is an unverified question premise and is wrong for the latest comparable quarters. In the first quarter of 2025, the pre-tax loss narrowed to £79.6 million from £138.9 million a year earlier, an improvement of 59.3. Yet operating losses grew and revenue fell 13 per cent to £233.9 million. The distinction matters: the pre-tax result improved despite weaker operations, and the difference is not cash saved for Valhalla. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250503235516/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/business/aston-martin-us-sales-trump-b2742153.html#:~:text=It%20came%20as%20the%20firm%20also%20reported%20that%20operating,13%20per%20cent%20to%20%C2%A3233.9%20million%20for%20the%20quarter.)

The EV delay separates two different investment decisions. Aston Martin had targeted 2027 for its first electric vehicle before Hallmark moved production to 2030. Valhalla, by contrast, was redesigned around an AMG engine and electric motors. Launching it would put a hybrid on the road without waiting for the battery-electric programme. Deferral can reduce overlap in spending; neither the production date nor the powertrain design tells investors how much development cash is still due. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1287882819) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1285707238)

The financing history shows why delivery timing matters. After warning about weaker Chinese demand and then delayed Valiant deliveries, Aston Martin announced £210 million of shares and debt. The subsequent March package included a planned £52.5 million Yew Tree equity injection and a sale of racing-team shares. The equity injection is part of the £125 million, not additional to it. Announced proceeds are not cash on hand, and an asset sale cannot be repeated indefinitely to finance development. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1287882819)

The clearest near-term risk to cash available for Valhalla is slower US wholesale receipts. Hallmark is limiting imports exposed to a 25 per cent tariff and relying on dealer stock in a market that accounts for around 30 per cent of sales. Selling a car already held by a dealer need not generate a new payment to Aston Martin; the signal to watch is whether dealers place replacement orders. Recall and workforce-reduction costs, by contrast, are unverified question premises: the reporting establishes neither their size nor their payment dates. If repair bills or severance payments fall due before launch receipts arrive, they would reduce available cash; later payroll savings would not meet those earlier bills. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250503235516/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/business/aston-martin-us-sales-trump-b2742153.html#:~:text=Rather%20than%20exporting%20new%20vehicles%20to%20the%20US%2C%20which,to%20changes%20in%20the%20operating%20environment%20as%20they%20materialise.%22) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250503235516/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/business/aston-martin-us-sales-trump-b2742153.html#:~:text=Aston%20Martin%20is%20among%20European%20car%20manufacturers%20that%20have,that%20the%20ramifications%20of%20the%20tariffs%20are%20still%20%E2%80%9Cuncertain%E2%80%9D.)

## What would change the view

The strongest downside case is a Valhalla delivery slip that postpones customer receipts while launch bills still fall due, repeating the financing pressure seen with Valiant. Test it with a cash forecast: start with unrestricted cash and committed undrawn facilities, count financing proceeds only when available, and track operating cash flow after working-capital movements against development spending, debt service and any recall or severance payments. Sustained headroom through customer deliveries would support the phased plan; a projected shortfall before receipts arrive would argue for new capital or deferrable EV spending. Management’s confidence in its targets is encouraging, but the evidence supplies neither that cash forecast nor the liquidity balance needed to size a gap. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1287882819) [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20250503235516/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/business/aston-martin-us-sales-trump-b2742153.html#:~:text=Despite%20the%20challenges%20posed%20by%20the%20tariffs%2C%20Aston%20Martin,and%20expressed%20confidence%20in%20achieving%20its%202025%20financial%20targets.)

## Checked calculations

- C1. Q1 2025 vs Q1 2024: narrowing of pre-tax loss; not a measure of cash saved (£ million) — 138.9 − 79.6 = 59.3 [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250503235516/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/business/aston-martin-us-sales-trump-b2742153.html#:~:text=It%20came%20as%20the%20firm%20also%20reported%20that%20operating,13%20per%20cent%20to%20%C2%A3233.9%20million%20for%20the%20quarter.)

question: How is LG Electronics' strategic pivot into B2B sectors—specifically AI-integrated robotics, HVAC infrastructure, and smart ecosystems—redefining its growth profile and valuation following its mobile exit, the 2025 acquisition of Bear Robotics, and the Microsoft AI partnership?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-06-10

**Research question**
How is LG Electronics' strategic pivot into B2B sectors—specifically AI-integrated robotics, HVAC infrastructure, and smart ecosystems—redefining its growth profile and valuation following its mobile exit, the 2025 acquisition of Bear Robotics, and the Microsoft AI partnership?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-06-10, LG Electronics merits credit for ending a loss-making handset business in 2021, but the evidence does not yet justify a sustained higher valuation multiple. LG has hundreds of millions of smart products in use and a Microsoft partnership that extends to data-centre cooling. Those assets give LG ways to grow beyond consumer hardware; they do not establish how much additional business-to-business operating profit or free cash flow LG earns from cooling, robotics or connected services. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1291773150) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20230224194941/https://programmingnation.in/2021/04/05/lg-mobile-division-withdraws-from-business/#:~:text=South%20Korean%20manufacturer%20will%20be%20shutting%20LG%20Mobile%20Division,to%20sell%20the%20mobile%20business%2C%20but%20it%20didn%E2%80%99t%20work.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250511183513/https://www.avinteractive.com/news/ai/lg-announces-ai-partnership-with-microsoft-at-ces-2025-07-01-2025/#:~:text=Connected%20devices%20also%20form%20part%20of%20the%20plan.%20Not,real-time%20spatial%20sensing%20and%20insights%20into%20customer%20lifestyle%20patterns.) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250511183513/https://www.avinteractive.com/news/ai/lg-announces-ai-partnership-with-microsoft-at-ces-2025-07-01-2025/#:~:text=Plans%20also%20include%20developing%20AI%20agents%20that%20not%20only,its%20vision%20of%20%22affectionate%20intelligence%22%2C%20or%20AI%20with%20empathy.)

## Evidence

The mobile exit changed the earnings baseline, not the growth rate investors should assume thereafter. At the time, LG expected lower near-term revenue, while analysts estimated that withdrawal could lift operating profit by 1 trillion won. Those views are compatible: shedding loss-making sales can raise profit as revenue falls. The estimate was not a reported saving, and even a permanent saving would not demonstrate growth in the remaining businesses. [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20230224194941/https://programmingnation.in/2021/04/05/lg-mobile-division-withdraws-from-business/#:~:text=LG%20has%20to%20be%20one%20of%20the%20most%20innovative,loss-making%20mobile%20business.%20LG%20LG%20Mobile%20Division%20Programming%20Nation)

HVAC has the clearest route to industrial sales because LG already makes cooling equipment. The Microsoft collaboration identifies a specific application for LG chillers: removing heat from AI data centres. But Microsoft's infrastructure investment is evidence of potential demand, not a purchase order for LG. Without awarded contracts, delivery schedules and margins after installation and warranty costs, there is no basis here for forecasting the profit LG will retain. [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20200531213421/http://www.lgnewsroom.com:80/about-lg-electronics/#:~:text=LG%20Electronics%20Inc.%20is%20a%20global%20innovator%20in%20technology,Collection%20and%20Use%20of%20Personal%20Information%20for%20Delivering%20Newsletter%3E) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250511183513/https://www.avinteractive.com/news/ai/lg-announces-ai-partnership-with-microsoft-at-ces-2025-07-01-2025/#:~:text=Plans%20also%20include%20developing%20AI%20agents%20that%20not%20only,its%20vision%20of%20%22affectionate%20intelligence%22%2C%20or%20AI%20with%20empathy.) [7](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1294811662)

In smart ecosystems, Athom gives LG connectivity with devices from over 170 global brands, while Microsoft adds speech capabilities for services LG intends to offer in homes, vehicles and commercial spaces. This could let LG sell a service across equipment it did not manufacture. The installed base is a distribution advantage, however, not a count of paying business customers. The evidence does not disclose commercial subscriptions, renewal rates or margins after software and support costs. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250511183513/https://www.avinteractive.com/news/ai/lg-announces-ai-partnership-with-microsoft-at-ces-2025-07-01-2025/#:~:text=Connected%20devices%20also%20form%20part%20of%20the%20plan.%20Not,real-time%20spatial%20sensing%20and%20insights%20into%20customer%20lifestyle%20patterns.) [8](https://web.archive.org/web/20250511183513/https://www.avinteractive.com/news/ai/lg-announces-ai-partnership-with-microsoft-at-ces-2025-07-01-2025/#:~:text=LG%20has%20adopted%20Microsoft%20voice%20recognition%20and%20speech%20synthesis,with%20Microsoft%E2%80%99s%20AI%20technology%20to%20implement%20%E2%80%9Cempathetic%20AI-integrated%20services%E2%80%9D.)

## What would change the view

My base case credits the handset exit in normalized earnings but assigns no multiple premium for the new businesses yet. The strongest alternative is that chiller installations and robot fleets become a durable source of paid software and maintenance renewals, making earnings less dependent on the next equipment sale. I would favor that view if LG showed orders converting into revenue, customers renewing services, and a material rise in business-to-business operating profit that persists as free cash flow after capital spending and working-capital needs. Partnership plans and device reach alone cannot test that case or support a specific valuation target. [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20230224194941/https://programmingnation.in/2021/04/05/lg-mobile-division-withdraws-from-business/#:~:text=LG%20has%20to%20be%20one%20of%20the%20most%20innovative,loss-making%20mobile%20business.%20LG%20LG%20Mobile%20Division%20Programming%20Nation) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250511183513/https://www.avinteractive.com/news/ai/lg-announces-ai-partnership-with-microsoft-at-ces-2025-07-01-2025/#:~:text=Plans%20also%20include%20developing%20AI%20agents%20that%20not%20only,its%20vision%20of%20%22affectionate%20intelligence%22%2C%20or%20AI%20with%20empathy.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250511183513/https://www.avinteractive.com/news/ai/lg-announces-ai-partnership-with-microsoft-at-ces-2025-07-01-2025/#:~:text=Connected%20devices%20also%20form%20part%20of%20the%20plan.%20Not,real-time%20spatial%20sensing%20and%20insights%20into%20customer%20lifestyle%20patterns.)

question: Despite PACB's 38.3% year-to-date underperformance and looming threats to NIH grant funding, major institutional investors like SoftBank and Millennium Management significantly increased their stakes. Does this aggressive accumulation suggest an institutional consensus on valuation that contradicts the current market trajectory and insider selling activity?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-05-11

**Research question**
Despite PACB's 38.3% year-to-date underperformance and looming threats to NIH grant funding, major institutional investors like SoftBank and Millennium Management significantly increased their stakes. Does this aggressive accumulation suggest an institutional consensus on valuation that contradicts the current market trajectory and insider selling activity?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

No. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250504014341/https://www.pacb.com/press_releases/pacbio-announces-preliminary-first-quarter-2025-revenue-and-reiterates-2025-revenue-guidance-of-155-million-to-170-million/#:~:text=Q1%202025%20Earnings%20Conference%20Call%20Scheduled%20for%20May%208%2C,quarter%20ended%20March%2031%2C%202025.%20Preliminary%20First%20Quarter%20Results)

## Evidence

Neither the claimed year-to-date underperformance nor the reported insider sales contradicts the alleged buying. Both are unverified question premises. A manager can add shares while other investors sell at successively lower prices; the price path does not reveal either side’s estimate of fair value. The documented price decline concerns 2011, not the current year, and the equity-plan excerpt identifies an award agreement, not an executed sale. Without dated price and benchmark data or insider transaction disclosures, neither the relative return nor the timing and nature of the sales can be checked. [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20230928012721/https://www.genomeweb.com/clinical-sequencing/michael-hunkapiller-hugh-martin-out-ceo-pacific-biosciences#:~:text=The%20Menlo%20Park%2C%20Calif.-based%20firm%20said%20that%20Martin%20resigned,in%20order%20to%20lure%20investors%20to%20purchase%20its%20stock.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250414205355/https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1299130/000129913024000169/pacb-20240630.htm#:~:text=Pacific%20Biosciences%20of%20California%2C%20Inc.%202020%20Equity%20Incentive%20Plan%2C,of%20California%2C%20Inc.%202020%20Equity%20Incentive%20Plan%2C%20as%20amended)

## Outlook

The base case is that Vega demand and funding risk coexist, leaving room for different valuations. PacBio said preliminary revenue met its expectations and Vega orders accelerated sequentially despite NIH funding uncertainty. That is evidence of customer interest, not proof that grant cuts will occur or that orders will become revenue. The near-term test is whether customers take delivery or instead delay or cancel purchases as funding decisions unfold. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250504014341/https://www.pacb.com/press_releases/pacbio-announces-preliminary-first-quarter-2025-revenue-and-reiterates-2025-revenue-guidance-of-155-million-to-170-million/#:~:text=Cash%2C%20cash%20equivalents%2C%20and%20investments%20Our%20preliminary%20revenue%20for,point%20enabled%20purchases%20from%20both%20new%20and%20existing%20customers.) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250504014341/https://www.pacb.com/press_releases/pacbio-announces-preliminary-first-quarter-2025-revenue-and-reiterates-2025-revenue-guidance-of-155-million-to-170-million/#:~:text=This%20press%20release%20contains%20%E2%80%9Cforward-looking%20statements%E2%80%9D%20within%20the%20meaning,products%20may%20be%20smaller%20than%20expected%3B%20risks%20related%20to)

## What would change the view

The strongest bullish alternative is that the market has discounted a larger demand setback than PacBio will experience, and the named managers recognized that early. Sustained revenue from new and existing Vega customers would strengthen the business case. To strengthen the separate claim about institutional valuation, look for comparable filings showing persistent net additions across a broad set of independent managers and investor commentary attributing those purchases to price relative to business value. Holdings alone cannot supply that motive. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250504014341/https://www.pacb.com/press_releases/pacbio-announces-preliminary-first-quarter-2025-revenue-and-reiterates-2025-revenue-guidance-of-155-million-to-170-million/#:~:text=Cash%2C%20cash%20equivalents%2C%20and%20investments%20Our%20preliminary%20revenue%20for,point%20enabled%20purchases%20from%20both%20new%20and%20existing%20customers.) question: How do Pascal Soriot’s strategic pivot toward U.S. and Chinese markets and the divestment of neuroscience impact AstraZeneca’s ability to achieve its 10.23 non-GAAP EPS target, especially considering his warnings about the deteriorating business environment and pricing pressures in Europe?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-06-29

**Research question**
How do Pascal Soriot’s strategic pivot toward U.S. and Chinese markets and the divestment of neuroscience impact AstraZeneca’s ability to achieve its 10.23 non-GAAP EPS target, especially considering his warnings about the deteriorating business environment and pricing pressures in Europe?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Evidence

If the proposed threshold means Core EPS for FY 2025 on the same share basis as the FY 2024 result, reaching it from $8.21 would require growth well above guidance at unchanged exchange rates. Reported EPS of $4.54 is not the appropriate starting point for that comparison. A later-year consensus estimate would have more time to be reached and need not conflict with guidance, but that interpretation requires a dated consensus source specifying the period, share unit and earnings definition. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250514221813/https://www.astrazeneca.com/content/dam/az/PDF/2024/fy/Full-year-and-Q4-2024-results-announcement.pdf#:~:text=1%20AstraZeneca%206%20February%202025%20Full%20Year%20and%20Q4,2030%2C%20many%20of%20which%20have%20now%20entered%20pivotal%20trials.%E2%80%9D) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250514221813/https://www.astrazeneca.com/content/dam/az/PDF/2024/fy/Full-year-and-Q4-2024-results-announcement.pdf#:~:text=6%20Upcoming%20pipeline%20catalysts%20For%20recent%20trial%20starts%20and,economic%20interest%2C%20continue%20to%20be%20recorded%20in%20Other%20operating)

## Outlook

U.S. and Chinese demand could offset European price cuts, but the test is incremental profit, not sales growth. My base case uses management’s group growth guidance: Soriot cited rising demand across key regions, not a quantified shift toward the U.S. and China. The risk disclosure acknowledges pricing and access pressures but does not quantify European price erosion or verify the Europe-specific warning attributed to Soriot. The strongest downside case is that lower European net prices reduce profit on existing sales faster than new U.S. and Chinese sales add profit after launch costs. Regional sales changes split by volume and net price, together with their margin effects, would distinguish the cases. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250514221813/https://www.astrazeneca.com/content/dam/az/PDF/2024/fy/Full-year-and-Q4-2024-results-announcement.pdf#:~:text=1%20AstraZeneca%206%20February%202025%20Full%20Year%20and%20Q4,2030%2C%20many%20of%20which%20have%20now%20entered%20pivotal%20trials.%E2%80%9D) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250514221813/https://www.astrazeneca.com/content/dam/az/PDF/2024/fy/Full-year-and-Q4-2024-results-announcement.pdf#:~:text=for%20medicine%20development%20or%20approval%3B%20%E2%80%92%20the%20risk%20of,on%20the%20Group%E2%80%99s%20operations%2C%20financial%20results%20or%20financial%20condition.)

## What would change the view

I assign no incremental earnings benefit to a neuroscience divestment. The documented Spirogen transaction was an oncology purchase, not evidence of which neuroscience assets AstraZeneca sold. To revise the estimate, I would need a disposal disclosure identifying the assets and closing date, then a reconciliation showing recurring costs saved less earnings forgone and costs retained. Any sale gain should be assessed separately: booking disposal income would not by itself demonstrate a sustainable increase in Core EPS. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20230827162755/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-astrazeneca-spirogen-idUSBRE99E03Y20131015#:~:text=AstraZeneca%20buys%20oncology-focused%20Spirogen%20for%20up%20to%20%24440%20million,target%20cancer%20tumors%20while%20safeguarding%20healthy%20cells%2C%20AstraZeneca%20said.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250514221813/https://www.astrazeneca.com/content/dam/az/PDF/2024/fy/Full-year-and-Q4-2024-results-announcement.pdf#:~:text=6%20Upcoming%20pipeline%20catalysts%20For%20recent%20trial%20starts%20and,economic%20interest%2C%20continue%20to%20be%20recorded%20in%20Other%20operating)
