# Investment research memo

As of 2025-04-28

**Research question**
How is the operational integration of Inmarsat Maritime influencing Viasat’s (VSAT) path to profitability, specifically concerning the widening quarterly EPS loss of $1.23 reported in February 2025 compared to the previous year’s performance?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Evidence

Solvang’s Mar 20, 2025 commitment to use NexusWave fleetwide is the clearest evidence of maritime demand. It came after the earnings announcement, so it helps assess the outlook rather than explain the reported quarter. The acquisition combined spectrum and network assets; if deployed vessels use spare capacity, additional service revenue could carry a higher margin. The commitment does not establish how many vessels are active and paying, what they pay, or what Viasat spends to serve them. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250409225358/https://investors.viasat.com/#:~:text=Mar%2025%2C%202025%20Summary%20ToggleTo%20the%20Moon%3A%20Viasat%20Selected,and%20Business%20Connectivity%20Minimum%2015%20minutes%20delayed.%20Source%3A%20LSEG) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250115090343/https://news.viasat.com/newsroom/press-releases/viasat-completes-acquisition-of-inmarsat#:~:text=The%20closing%20of%20the%20Inmarsat%20acquisition%20enables%20the%20companies,as%20legal%20advisors%20to%20Inmarsat%20and%20its%20majority%20shareholders.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250406072928/https://www.viasat.com/news/latest-news/corporate/2025/viasat-releases-third-quarter-fiscal-year-2025-financial-results/#:~:text=Viasat%20Releases%20Third%20Quarter%20Fiscal%20Year%202025%20Financial%20Results,and%20International%20%28646%29%20307-1963.%20Please%20reference%20conference%20ID%202357759.)

## Outlook

Base case: maritime service revenue rises over the next several quarters as commitments turn into billable service, but a consolidated earnings recovery remains unproven. The strongest alternative is that deployments add traffic without enough profit: competition from Starlink could constrain pricing, while service costs could absorb the incremental revenue. That is a risk, not evidence of an observed maritime price cut. Viasat itself identifies acquisition savings as an expected benefit rather than a realized result. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250409225358/https://investors.viasat.com/#:~:text=Mar%2025%2C%202025%20Summary%20ToggleTo%20the%20Moon%3A%20Viasat%20Selected,and%20Business%20Connectivity%20Minimum%2015%20minutes%20delayed.%20Source%3A%20LSEG) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20231104015126/https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/business/story/2023-05-31/carlsbads-viasat-boosts-satellite-internet-footprint-globally-with-completion-of-inmarsat-acquisition#:~:text=%E2%80%9CThe%20combination%20of%20our%20companies%20brings%20together%20the%20people%2C,Starlink%20fleet%20but%20also%20including%20Amazon%2C%20OneWeb%20and%20others.) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250115090343/https://news.viasat.com/newsroom/press-releases/viasat-completes-acquisition-of-inmarsat#:~:text=Forward-Looking%20Statements%20This%20press%20release%20contains%20forward-looking%20statements%20that,covenants%3B%20and%20other%20factors%20affecting%20the%20communications%20industry%20generally.)

## What would change the view

A delayed fleet rollout would weaken the revenue case; rising vessel activations alongside flat or falling maritime margins would favor the low-profit alternative. To conclude that integration is improving Viasat’s path to profitability, look for paying deployments and higher maritime operating profit, then a same-basis EPS reconciliation showing how much of that gain remains after integration costs, interest and other consolidated items. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250409225358/https://investors.viasat.com/#:~:text=Mar%2025%2C%202025%20Summary%20ToggleTo%20the%20Moon%3A%20Viasat%20Selected,and%20Business%20Connectivity%20Minimum%2015%20minutes%20delayed.%20Source%3A%20LSEG) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250115090343/https://news.viasat.com/newsroom/press-releases/viasat-completes-acquisition-of-inmarsat#:~:text=Forward-Looking%20Statements%20This%20press%20release%20contains%20forward-looking%20statements%20that,covenants%3B%20and%20other%20factors%20affecting%20the%20communications%20industry%20generally.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250115090343/https://news.viasat.com/newsroom/press-releases/viasat-completes-acquisition-of-inmarsat#:~:text=The%20closing%20of%20the%20Inmarsat%20acquisition%20enables%20the%20companies,as%20legal%20advisors%20to%20Inmarsat%20and%20its%20majority%20shareholders.)

report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-04-23

**Research question**
Following the divestiture of Versace in April 2025, can Capri Holdings’ strategic pivot to focus resources on Michael Kors successfully reverse brand stagnation and stabilize group margins within the Retail - Apparel and Shoes sector?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-04-23, Capri had signed a definitive agreement to sell Versace to Prada, not completed the sale. The cash price was based on an enterprise value of €1,25 billion, subject to adjustment at closing. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250414171512/https://tg24.sky.it/economia/2025/04/10/prada-versace-accordo#:~:text=Il%20gruppo%20guidato%20da%20Patrizio%20Bertelli%20e%20Andrea%20Guerra,approvazioni%20regolamentari.%20Bertelli%3A%20%22Avviamo%20un%20nuovo%20capitolo%20per%20Versace%22) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1284957983)

## Evidence

The strongest recovery case is that Kors mispriced its merchandise rather than exhausted demand for it. Setting initial prices closer to what core customers will pay could lift unit sales without another round of promotions. The return to jet-set branding and 150 planned renovations give Kors a way to test that proposition in stores. The counterargument is that customers were buying only at the discounted price: lowering the ticket could merely formalize that price, leaving fewer gross-profit dollars per sale unless volume or product mix improves. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250321064409/https://www.glossy.co/fashion/luxury/capri-holdings-pivots-michael-kors-pricing-strategy-after-missteps-bets-on-versace-luxury/#:~:text=%E2%80%9CThe%20merger%20was%20highly%20distracting%20for%20the%20management%20team%2C,the%20price%20points%20where%20she%20would%20buy%20the%20brand.%E2%80%9D) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250321064409/https://www.glossy.co/fashion/luxury/capri-holdings-pivots-michael-kors-pricing-strategy-after-missteps-bets-on-versace-luxury/#:~:text=At%20the%20same%20time%2C%20Michael%20Kors%20is%20undergoing%20a,movement%20that%20has%20dominated%20high%20fashion%20in%20recent%20years.) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250321064409/https://www.glossy.co/fashion/luxury/capri-holdings-pivots-michael-kors-pricing-strategy-after-missteps-bets-on-versace-luxury/#:~:text=Jimmy%20Choo%20reported%20%24600%20million%20in%20revenue%20for%20fiscal,retail%20%E2%80%94%20it%20didn%E2%80%99t%2C%20but%20we%E2%80%99re%20sticking%20with%20it.%E2%80%9D)

A better reported group margin after closing would not necessarily mean Kors had recovered. Removing loss-making Versace could improve the brand mix, but management already expected Versace to approach break-even; Jimmy Choo was expected to remain slightly loss-making. Store closures and workforce cuts could help, but corporate costs formerly supported by Versace would then fall on a smaller revenue base unless eliminated. Capri’s Q3 FY25 gross margin moved -0.6 percentage points year over year. That is a gross-margin change, not evidence of a stable operating margin for the remaining group. The available figures do not quantify stranded overhead or net savings. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250321064409/https://www.glossy.co/fashion/luxury/capri-holdings-pivots-michael-kors-pricing-strategy-after-missteps-bets-on-versace-luxury/#:~:text=At%20the%20same%20time%2C%20Michael%20Kors%20is%20undergoing%20a,movement%20that%20has%20dominated%20high%20fashion%20in%20recent%20years.) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250321064409/https://www.glossy.co/fashion/luxury/capri-holdings-pivots-michael-kors-pricing-strategy-after-missteps-bets-on-versace-luxury/#:~:text=Jimmy%20Choo%20reported%20%24600%20million%20in%20revenue%20for%20fiscal,retail%20%E2%80%94%20it%20didn%E2%80%99t%2C%20but%20we%E2%80%99re%20sticking%20with%20it.%E2%80%9D) [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20250416011100/https://www.retail-insight-network.com/news/capri-revenue-q3-fy25/#:~:text=The%20gold%20standard%20of%20business%20intelligence.%20Capri%20Holdings%20chairman,reported%20in%20the%20same%20quarter%20of%20the%20previous%20year.)

## Outlook

My base case is that Capri can slow the deterioration at Kors, but a sustained recovery in comparable sales without deeper markdowns is not yet the likely near-term outcome. The clearest test so far was distribution: Capri removed about $200 million in wholesale business, yet management saw no corresponding shift into retail. Cutting distribution can protect pricing; it does not by itself give customers a reason to buy. Management also identified strengthening Capri’s balance sheet as a goal of the sale, not a specific reinvestment budget for Kors. [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250321064409/https://www.glossy.co/fashion/luxury/capri-holdings-pivots-michael-kors-pricing-strategy-after-missteps-bets-on-versace-luxury/#:~:text=Jimmy%20Choo%20reported%20%24600%20million%20in%20revenue%20for%20fiscal,retail%20%E2%80%94%20it%20didn%E2%80%99t%2C%20but%20we%E2%80%99re%20sticking%20with%20it.%E2%80%9D) [7](https://web.archive.org/web/20250414171512/https://tg24.sky.it/economia/2025/04/10/prada-versace-accordo#:~:text=%22L%27acquisizione%20di%20Versace%20rappresenta%20un%20passo%20ulteriore%20nel%20percorso,termine%20di%20Michael%20Kors%20e%20Jimmy%20Choo%22%20ha%20concluso.)

## What would change the view

I would turn more positive if Kors reported sustained positive comparable sales alongside better full-price sell-through and stable markdown depth, with gains extending beyond renovated stores. The reported improvement in full-price sell-through was at Versace, not Kors; Capri’s group retail decline is not a Kors comparable-sales measure either. For the margin call, I would also need a post-close reconciliation showing that realized savings cover retained overhead and reinvestment, with operating margin holding up on the same Kors-and-Choo basis. A margin lift solely from removing Versace, or a sales rebound purchased with promotions, would not meet those tests. [8](https://web.archive.org/web/20250321064409/https://www.glossy.co/fashion/luxury/capri-holdings-pivots-michael-kors-pricing-strategy-after-missteps-bets-on-versace-luxury/#:~:text=One%20of%20Versace%E2%80%99s%20key%20adjustments%20is%20rebalancing%20its%20price,said%2C%20noting%20that%20demand%20for%20formal%20footwear%20remains%20sluggish.) [9](https://web.archive.org/web/20250416011100/https://www.retail-insight-network.com/news/capri-revenue-q3-fy25/#:~:text=Capri%20Holdings%2C%20owner%20of%20the%20Versace%2C%20Jimmy%20Choo%20and,group%E2%80%99s%20performance%20was%20impacted%20across%20its%20entire%20brand%20portfolio.) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250321064409/https://www.glossy.co/fashion/luxury/capri-holdings-pivots-michael-kors-pricing-strategy-after-missteps-bets-on-versace-luxury/#:~:text=Jimmy%20Choo%20reported%20%24600%20million%20in%20revenue%20for%20fiscal,retail%20%E2%80%94%20it%20didn%E2%80%99t%2C%20but%20we%E2%80%99re%20sticking%20with%20it.%E2%80%9D)

## Checked calculations

- C1. Capri gross margin change, Q3 FY25 versus Q3 FY24 (not operating margin) (percentage points) — 64.4 − 65 = -0.6 [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20250416011100/https://www.retail-insight-network.com/news/capri-revenue-q3-fy25/#:~:text=The%20gold%20standard%20of%20business%20intelligence.%20Capri%20Holdings%20chairman,reported%20in%20the%20same%20quarter%20of%20the%20previous%20year.)

question: Given Fitch Ratings' repeated downward revisions to 2025 U.S. GDP growth forecasts and Olu Sonola's analysis of tariff-driven volatility, how should institutional fixed-income investors assess the sustainability of the U.S. AA+ sovereign credit rating and the potential for a negative outlook shift in late 2025?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-04-23

**Research question**
Given Fitch Ratings' repeated downward revisions to 2025 U.S. GDP growth forecasts and Olu Sonola's analysis of tariff-driven volatility, how should institutional fixed-income investors assess the sustainability of the U.S. AA+ sovereign credit rating and the potential for a negative outlook shift in late 2025?

## Answer

As of 2025-04-23, institutional fixed-income investors should retain U.S. sovereign exposure at its current weight and monitor for a possible Fitch negative outlook in late 2025. The Fed cut its growth forecast from 2.1% to 1.7%, but a weaker growth forecast does not establish that debt will rise materially faster or that interest will consume materially more revenue. A negative outlook would flag greater risk of a future downgrade; it would not itself lower the rating. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1287066496)

## Evidence

Fitch’s AA+ baseline, its repeated forecast cuts and Olu Sonola’s interpretation of tariff volatility are unverified question premises. The available March forecasts support the direction of the growth concern, not its size relative to Fitch’s baseline: the OECD still projected 2.2% growth in 2025, with its weaker 1.6% projection applying to 2026. Neither forecast is Fitch’s, and the evidence contains no Sonola statement or Fitch fiscal projection against which to measure the shock. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1287066496)

The auto tariffs illustrate why gross customs receipts and net fiscal gains can differ. After an initial delay for qualifying vehicles, the 25% imported-car tariff took effect on April 3. The White House projected higher tax revenue, while Stellantis announced temporary closures and layoffs affecting 900 American employees. These are not contradictory: customs collections can rise while lost wages and profits erode other tax receipts. A company announcement shows a channel for losses, not their economy-wide scale. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1287066496)

## Outlook

The base case is that the rating holds through late 2025: weaker real growth need not cause a lasting deterioration in debt affordability. The dollar’s reserve role supports demand for dollar assets, but does not cap Treasury refinancing costs. The strongest alternative is persistent weakness in tax receipts alongside costly refinancing. The Fed raised its inflation expectations even as it cut its growth forecast, so investors should not assume slower growth will bring enough interest relief to offset lost revenue. [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1287028422) [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1287066496)

## What would change the view

Obtain Fitch’s fiscal baseline and compare successive fiscal releases and projections on the same government coverage and horizon. Track the primary deficit after actual customs receipts, debt relative to nominal GDP, and interest expense relative to revenue as debt rolls over. Reduce exposure if a persistent primary shortfall puts debt on a materially steeper path than Fitch assumed and refinancing pushes the interest share above baseline without a credible fiscal offset. That combination would strengthen the case for a negative outlook before a downgrade. Until then, a gross tariff-revenue projection is no substitute for collections, and the available evidence cannot establish the size of a fiscal gap or the timing of Fitch action. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1287066496)

## Sources

1. [Tariffs in the second Trump administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1287066496), available by 2025-04-23.
2. [United States dollar](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1287028422), available by 2025-04-23.

question: Can Oliver Blume’s restructuring and cost-cutting initiatives in Germany sufficiently offset the margin compression caused by Volkswagen Group’s (VWAGY) persistent market share loss and 9.5% sales decline in China, given the intensifying competition from local new energy vehicle (NEV) manufacturers?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-04-23

**Research question**
Can Oliver Blume’s restructuring and cost-cutting initiatives in Germany sufficiently offset the margin compression caused by Volkswagen Group’s (VWAGY) persistent market share loss and 9.5% sales decline in China, given the intensifying competition from local new energy vehicle (NEV) manufacturers?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-04-23, I would not count on Oliver Blume’s German restructuring to offset Volkswagen Group’s near-term China earnings pressure. German savings can cushion Group operating margin, but the announced €10 billion cost-cutting plan is not a measure of net German savings already reaching earnings. Nor would German savings restore profit at the equity-accounted Chinese joint ventures. The investment case is for a partial cushion, not a demonstrated full offset. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1284609502) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1285398123)

## Evidence

For **Group operating margin**, the right comparison is German expense reductions actually recognized, less restructuring charges in the same period, against China-related operating losses inside the consolidated business. The cost plan announced in 2023 and plant proposals reported in October 2024 are different in scope and timing; neither establishes completed closures or a schedule of net savings. The reported 64% quarterly profit drop is not a Group operating-margin change or a China-only loss. Without a margin breakdown, it cannot serve as the amount Germany needs to offset. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1284609502)

For **equity-accounted Chinese joint ventures**, VW’s share of earnings sits outside Group operating profit. A venture can defend deliveries with discounts yet earn less per car; domestic new energy vehicle competition therefore threatens earnings even if unit share stabilizes. German savings could counterbalance weaker venture income in Group pretax profit, but cannot repair the ventures’ margins. The evidence identifies the local venture structure and the discounting, not the change in VW’s equity income needed to quantify that comparison. [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1285808533) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1285398123)

## What would change the view

The strongest upside case is that German savings arrive while better local products reduce the need for discounts, shrinking the earnings gap from both sides. VW’s Hefei investment and its aim to shorten development cycles by around 30% give that case a mechanism, not a realized return. I would revise the base case on two distinct signals: a same-period Group operating-profit breakdown showing German savings after charges exceeding consolidated China pressure, and separately reported Chinese venture earnings stabilizing alongside VW-specific share without deeper discounts. [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1285808533) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1285398123)

## Sources

1. [Volkswagen Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1284609502), available by 2025-04-08.
2. [Automotive industry in China](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1285398123), available by 2025-04-13.
3. [Volkswagen Group China](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1285808533), available by 2025-04-15.

question: Considering ICON plc's (ICLR) persistent stock underperformance despite meeting EPS targets and launching AI-driven initiatives in 1H 2025, how do the divergent institutional flows—specifically the massive Q4 2024 exits by Boston Partners versus Q1/Q2 2025 additions by Artisan Partners and Sequoia Fund—signal a shift in valuation sentiment?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-07-21

**Research question**
Considering ICON plc's (ICLR) persistent stock underperformance despite meeting EPS targets and launching AI-driven initiatives in 1H 2025, how do the divergent institutional flows—specifically the massive Q4 2024 exits by Boston Partners versus Q1/Q2 2025 additions by Artisan Partners and Sequoia Fund—signal a shift in valuation sentiment?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Evidence

None of the supplied records gives comparable quarter-end ICON share counts for these managers, so neither the direction nor the scale of any position change can be verified. A drop in dollar value is not evidence of an exit if the stock price also fell. Attribution matters too: Ruane Cunniff manages accounts beyond Sequoia, so an adviser-level increase would not by itself establish a Sequoia Fund purchase. No supplied fund commentary says that Artisan or Sequoia bought because ICON was cheap; that would be an inference even if the purchases were confirmed. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1300899383)

ICON’s earnings performance and its weaker outlook are consistent. Management attributed first-quarter earnings in line with its own expectations to cost control and resource utilization, not a recovery in demand. Net book-to-bill fell from 1.18 to 1.01, and the revised full-year revenue range implied a decline even at the high end. That gives investors a reason to discount future earnings despite the quarterly result. Persistent share-price underperformance and the first-half AI launches remain unverified question premises; the record shows neither benchmark-relative returns nor an incremental earnings contribution from AI. [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250707235722/https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250430194955/en/ICON-Reports-First-Quarter-2025-Results#:~:text=Updating%20full-year%202025%20financial%20revenue%20guidance%20in%20the%20range,resource%20utilization%20and%20strong%20cost%20control%20across%20the%20business.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250624232711/https://investor.iconplc.com/static-files/f99e18cc-b179-4415-b3e4-f7daa2f89c0f#:~:text=ICON%20Reports%20Fourth%20Quarter%20and%20Full%20Year%202024%20Results,and%20transaction%20-related%20%2F%20integrated%20-related%20adjustments.%20Dublin%2C%20Ireland%2C) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250707235722/https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250430194955/en/ICON-Reports-First-Quarter-2025-Results#:~:text=ICON%20Reports%20First%20Quarter%202025%20Results%20Net%20business%20wins,net%20book%20to%20bill%20in%20the%20quarter%20of%201.01.)

## Outlook

The base case is disagreement over how long the slowdown will last, not a demonstrated change in valuation sentiment. The strongest alternative is that later buyers judged the weakness temporary: year-end backlog of $24.7 billion and annual free cash flow of $1.1 billion give that thesis substance. Its operating test is whether cancellations ease and the backlog converts into revenue without another guidance cut. Its sentiment test is separate: fund-level share increases across successive disclosures, paired with a manager’s explanation that the purchase price discounted more weakness than expected. The former would support the economics; the latter would establish why that manager bought. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250624232711/https://investor.iconplc.com/static-files/f99e18cc-b179-4415-b3e4-f7daa2f89c0f#:~:text=ICON%20Reports%20Fourth%20Quarter%20and%20Full%20Year%202024%20Results,and%20transaction%20-related%20%2F%20integrated%20-related%20adjustments.%20Dublin%2C%20Ireland%2C) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250707235722/https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250430194955/en/ICON-Reports-First-Quarter-2025-Results#:~:text=Updating%20full-year%202025%20financial%20revenue%20guidance%20in%20the%20range,resource%20utilization%20and%20strong%20cost%20control%20across%20the%20business.)

## Sources

2. [ICON Reports First Quarter 2025 Results](https://web.archive.org/web/20250707235722/https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250430194955/en/ICON-Reports-First-Quarter-2025-Results#:~:text=Updating%20full-year%202025%20financial%20revenue%20guidance%20in%20the%20range,resource%20utilization%20and%20strong%20cost%20control%20across%20the%20business.), available by 2025-07-07.

question: How should institutional portfolios balance traditional hedges like Gold against emerging digital assets like a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve, given the Federal Reserve's persistent difficulty in anchoring inflation at 2% and the projected fiscal pressures from the Trump administration's economic policies?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-05-06

**Research question**
How should institutional portfolios balance traditional hedges like Gold against emerging digital assets like a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve, given the Federal Reserve's persistent difficulty in anchoring inflation at 2% and the projected fiscal pressures from the Trump administration's economic policies?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-05-06, the investment committee should retain gold as the core hedge and transfer none of its risk budget to Bitcoin. Gold’s long monetary history is a reason to keep it, not a promise that it will preserve purchasing power in every inflation shock. Bitcoin has not shown that it can replace gold when the rest of the portfolio is losing money. If the institution wants exposure to Bitcoin adoption, fund it separately as a speculative position, not as insurance. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1285183546) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1289006503)

## Evidence

The Federal Reserve pursues price stability and maximum employment; the investor needs assets it can sell to meet liabilities during a drawdown. A Treasury strategic reserve is a government holding, not a Fed monetary-policy instrument or an institutional allocation benchmark. Powell’s description of Bitcoin as a competitor for gold identifies a rival for investor demand, not an endorsement of equivalent downside protection. The available evidence does not establish that government holdings would put a floor under Bitcoin’s price. [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1289006503) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250502112626/https://time.com/7275021/federal-reserve-chief-says-trump-tariffs-likely-to-raise-inflation/#:~:text=Federal%20Reserve%20Chief%20Says%20Trump%20Tariffs%20Likely%20to%20Raise,U.S.%20economy%2C%20Federal%20Reserve%20Chair%20Jerome%20Powell%20said%20Friday.)

The strongest case for a capped Bitcoin allocation is that a volatile asset can still diversify a portfolio if it holds up when other assets fall. A 2018 study found high volatility; a 2022 analysis found Bitcoin less volatile than some conventional assets during and after the 2020 crash. Those findings are compatible: one stress window can differ from a broader sample. Neither volatility ranking tells the committee how much cash a Bitcoin position would have preserved on the dates its own portfolio needed liquidity. [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1289006503)

## Outlook

The base case is near-term price pressure and weaker growth, not a permanent rise in the inflation rate. The 10% import tariff effective April 5, 2025 gives Powell’s warning a concrete basis. If firms pass through a higher import cost once, prices can remain higher even after inflation subsides. [4](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1289178317) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250502112626/https://time.com/7275021/federal-reserve-chief-says-trump-tariffs-likely-to-raise-inflation/#:~:text=Federal%20Reserve%20Chief%20Says%20Trump%20Tariffs%20Likely%20to%20Raise,U.S.%20economy%2C%20Federal%20Reserve%20Chair%20Jerome%20Powell%20said%20Friday.)

## What would change the view

Authorize a partial shift only if a portfolio with some Bitcoin in place of gold, tested at the same risk budget after custody and trading costs, repeatedly suffers smaller losses in both inflation surprises and equity selloffs while meeting the same cash calls. Until then, cap any separate, unlevered Bitcoin position at the amount the institution can lose in full without impairing those payments. A price rally alone would not pass the test. Without portfolio holdings, liability dates or joint return histories, a precise allocation cap would be false precision. question: How does the Energy Information Administration’s weekly Petroleum Status Report influence WTI crude oil price discovery, and to what extent do the report's inventory deviations from market expectations serve as a consistent lead indicator for short-term price volatility in energy markets?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-08-20

**Research question**
How does the Energy Information Administration’s weekly Petroleum Status Report influence WTI crude oil price discovery, and to what extent do the report's inventory deviations from market expectations serve as a consistent lead indicator for short-term price volatility in energy markets?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-08-20, treat the EIA’s weekly Petroleum Status Report as a WTI futures price-discovery event, not as a reliable forecast of volatility after the initial adjustment. For the week ending January 31, 2025, the American Petroleum Institute (API) had signaled a crude build of 5.025 million barrels. EIA reported a larger build of 8.7 million barrels, and WTI was reported to have extended its losses. That account gives the direction of the move, but neither a timestamped release-window return nor a measure of volatility over the following hour or session. The available evidence does not establish a consistent later effect for WTI across market conditions, let alone for Brent, refined products or natural gas. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250316151551/https://www.forexfactory.com/calendar/10-us-crude-oil-inventories#:~:text=this%20morning%20after%20surging%20yesterday%20on%20Trump%27s%20%22maximum%20pressure%22,build%20Distillates%20-5.47mm%20-%20biggest%20draw%20since%20March%202021) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250316151551/https://www.forexfactory.com/calendar/10-us-crude-oil-inventories#:~:text=U.S.%20crude%20oil%20refinery%20inputs%20averaged%2015.3%20million%20barrels,Build%20In%20A%20Year%20Oil%20prices%20are%20leaking%20lower)

The EIA report normally becomes public on Wednesday morning, after API’s Tuesday-evening estimate, with holiday exceptions. The crude surprise is the reported weekly change in commercial crude stocks, excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, minus the market consensus immediately before release. That consensus should reflect information available after API; the EIA–API gap is not itself a consensus miss. All else equal, a larger build than expected points to a looser balance and pressures WTI, while a larger draw than expected supports it. The sign matters for the initial return. The separate forecasting question is whether the absolute size of the miss predicts larger subsequent swings after accounting for the initial move and simultaneous gasoline and distillate news. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250407164604/https://seekingalpha.com/article/4768668-api-eia-data-reveal-crude-oil-markets#:~:text=The%20EIA%20report%20includes%20crucial%20refinery%20utilization%20data%2C%20providing,especially%20when%20the%20reported%20changes%20differ%20from%20market%20expectations.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250316151551/https://www.forexfactory.com/calendar/10-us-crude-oil-inventories#:~:text=U.S.%20crude%20oil%20refinery%20inputs%20averaged%2015.3%20million%20barrels,Build%20In%20A%20Year%20Oil%20prices%20are%20leaking%20lower) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250407164604/https://seekingalpha.com/article/4768668-api-eia-data-reveal-crude-oil-markets#:~:text=The%20timing%20of%20the%20reports%20also%20plays%20a%20role.,on%20October%2024.%20The%20Power%20of%20Refinery%20Utilization%20Data)

## Evidence

The January-end release contained mixed signals: gasoline stocks rose by 2.2 million barrels, distillate stocks fell by 5.5 million barrels, and total commercial petroleum stocks fell by 2.7 million barrels despite the crude build. API had already indicated a gasoline build and a distillate draw. Without pre-release consensus forecasts for crude and products, the stock changes cannot tell us how much news each contained or how much of WTI’s decline each explains. [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250316151551/https://www.forexfactory.com/calendar/10-us-crude-oil-inventories#:~:text=U.S.%20crude%20oil%20refinery%20inputs%20averaged%2015.3%20million%20barrels,Build%20In%20A%20Year%20Oil%20prices%20are%20leaking%20lower) [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250316151551/https://www.forexfactory.com/calendar/10-us-crude-oil-inventories#:~:text=this%20morning%20after%20surging%20yesterday%20on%20Trump%27s%20%22maximum%20pressure%22,build%20Distillates%20-5.47mm%20-%20biggest%20draw%20since%20March%202021)

For the earlier week ending January 24, EIA reported a 3.5 million barrels increase. Coverage called it a surprise but did not quantify the consensus miss. WTI was described as holding losses rather than extending them, in a rangebound market where traders were weighing planned tariffs on Canadian crude. Holding an existing loss is not evidence of a fresh decline at release. Neither this account nor the January-end account pairs a measured surprise with intraday returns, so the contrast cannot establish how often large misses precede elevated volatility. [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250316151551/https://www.forexfactory.com/calendar/10-us-crude-oil-inventories#:~:text=Commercial%20crude%20oil%20inventories%20in%20the%20United%20States%2C%20excluding,capacity.%20Gasoline%20production%20declined%2C%20averaging%209.2%20million%20bpd.%20...)

## Outlook

Base case: manage the risk of a WTI jump at release, but do not raise the subsequent volatility forecast solely because the crude surprise was large. The strongest alternative is that a large miss alongside conflicting product news takes time to interpret, leaving prices unusually volatile after the first move. Weekly WTI options offer a way to hedge the announcement under either interpretation: the jump alone is worth distinguishing from what follows. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250407164604/https://seekingalpha.com/article/4768668-api-eia-data-reveal-crude-oil-markets#:~:text=The%20timing%20of%20the%20reports%20also%20plays%20a%20role.,on%20October%2024.%20The%20Power%20of%20Refinery%20Utilization%20Data) [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250316151551/https://www.forexfactory.com/calendar/10-us-crude-oil-inventories#:~:text=this%20morning%20after%20surging%20yesterday%20on%20Trump%27s%20%22maximum%20pressure%22,build%20Distillates%20-5.47mm%20-%20biggest%20draw%20since%20March%202021)

## What would change the view

Across a series of releases, record the post-API consensus before EIA publishes and measure the WTI return in a fixed announcement window. Exclude that window from realized volatility measured over the following hour, through the close and over the next session. Compare a forecast using recent volatility, the initial return, API information and simultaneous product surprises with the same forecast augmented by the absolute crude surprise. Repeated out-of-sample improvement across quiet and stressed markets would support a WTI lead indicator; improvement only when the initial jump is counted would support repricing, not prediction. Extending the conclusion to another energy contract requires the same test on that contract’s returns. [6](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1294393092) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250407164604/https://seekingalpha.com/article/4768668-api-eia-data-reveal-crude-oil-markets#:~:text=The%20EIA%20report%20includes%20crucial%20refinery%20utilization%20data%2C%20providing,especially%20when%20the%20reported%20changes%20differ%20from%20market%20expectations.)

question: Given Citron Research’s bearish thesis and $40 price target for Palantir (PLTR) based on private-market comparisons, what is the projected volatility and liquidation risk for investors in the PLTU 2x leveraged ETF should Palantir’s valuation converge with Citron's fair value estimates?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-08-20

**Research question**
Given Citron Research’s bearish thesis and $40 price target for Palantir (PLTR) based on private-market comparisons, what is the projected volatility and liquidation risk for investors in the PLTU 2x leveraged ETF should Palantir’s valuation converge with Citron's fair value estimates?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-08-20, reduce PLTU for a multi-day Palantir investment; reserve it for a monitored tactical trade sized to withstand a total loss. From PLTR’s reported Monday price of $174.03, an abrupt fall to Citron’s $40 benchmark could wipe out a PLTU investment. A gradual fall to the same price could leave a small residual. The reason to reduce is the fund’s daily leverage, not a prediction that Citron will be right. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250504025417/https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/PLTU#:~:text=Bull%20or%20Bear%2C%20Seeking%20Alpha%20is%20there%20Markets%20change%2C,Overview%20PLTU%3A%20Too%20Bullish%20On%20Palantir%2C%20Even%20For%20Me) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250819112211/https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/25/08/47204445/short-seller-andrew-left-says-openai-at-500-billion-puts-palantir-at-40-and-thats-generous#:~:text=Last%20week%2C%20Citron%20slammed%20Cramer%20for%20what%20it%20called,a%20year-to-date%20basis%20and%20435.48%25%20over%20the%20past%20year.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250819112211/https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/25/08/47204445/short-seller-andrew-left-says-openai-at-500-billion-puts-palantir-at-40-and-thats-generous#:~:text=%E2%80%98OpenAI%20At%20%24500%20Billion%20Puts%20Palantir%20At%20%2440%E2%80%99%20Using,for%20Palantir%2C%20a%20figure%20the%20report%20labels%20as%20generous.)

## Evidence

Benzinga verifies the attribution to Citron, not the fair value itself. Citron took OpenAI’s proposed $500 billion valuation against projected 2026 revenue of $29.6 billion and applied the resulting sales multiple of nearly 17x to Palantir’s consensus revenue estimate of $5.6 billion for the same year. Citron called the implied $40 expensive even on those terms, citing differences in growth and revenue mix. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250819112211/https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/25/08/47204445/short-seller-andrew-left-says-openai-at-500-billion-puts-palantir-at-40-and-thats-generous#:~:text=The%20report%E2%80%99s%20central%20argument%20hinges%20on%20a%20direct%20valuation,be%20expensive%22.%20OpenAI%E2%80%99s%20%E2%80%98Unprecedented%E2%80%99%20Growth%20Versus%20PLTR%E2%80%99s%20%E2%80%98Steady%20Progress%E2%80%99) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250819112211/https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/25/08/47204445/short-seller-andrew-left-says-openai-at-500-billion-puts-palantir-at-40-and-thats-generous#:~:text=Citron%20argues%20Palantir%20does%20not%20deserve%20to%20trade%20at,reliance%20on%20%22lumpy%2C%20less%20scalable%20revenue%22%20from%20government%20contracts.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250819112211/https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/25/08/47204445/short-seller-andrew-left-says-openai-at-500-billion-puts-palantir-at-40-and-thats-generous#:~:text=Last%20week%2C%20Citron%20slammed%20Cramer%20for%20what%20it%20called,a%20year-to-date%20basis%20and%20435.48%25%20over%20the%20past%20year.)

A capital wipeout is not the same as forced liquidation. A fully paid PLTU holder can lose the purchase price without receiving a margin call. If the investor has borrowed against the account, falling collateral can breach the broker’s maintenance requirement and prompt sales while PLTU still has value; the trigger depends on account equity and broker terms, not a particular PLTR price. ETF closure is a separate fund-level event: shareholders receive any residual value. Nothing in the valuation comparison establishes a closure trigger. [6](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1305549097) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250819112211/https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/25/08/47204445/short-seller-andrew-left-says-openai-at-500-billion-puts-palantir-at-40-and-thats-generous#:~:text=%E2%80%98OpenAI%20At%20%24500%20Billion%20Puts%20Palantir%20At%20%2440%E2%80%99%20Using,for%20Palantir%2C%20a%20figure%20the%20report%20labels%20as%20generous.)

## Outlook

Compare paths from $174.03 to $40, assuming PLTU delivers its daily objective before costs. Abrupt: the stock loses more than half its value in a session, exhausting the modeled shareholder capital rather than producing a negative share price. Gradual: with many small daily declines, each doubled loss applies to a smaller balance. The fraction of capital left approaches the square of the ending-to-starting PLTR price ratio, small but positive. Volatile: insert a rally and an exact retracement before that same gradual slide. PLTR returns to its starting point, but PLTU takes the doubled retracement on an enlarged balance and starts the slide with less capital. It ends below the gradual case despite the identical PLTR endpoint. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250504025417/https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/PLTU#:~:text=Bull%20or%20Bear%2C%20Seeking%20Alpha%20is%20there%20Markets%20change%2C,Overview%20PLTU%3A%20Too%20Bullish%20On%20Palantir%2C%20Even%20For%20Me) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250819112211/https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/25/08/47204445/short-seller-andrew-left-says-openai-at-500-billion-puts-palantir-at-40-and-thats-generous#:~:text=Last%20week%2C%20Citron%20slammed%20Cramer%20for%20what%20it%20called,a%20year-to-date%20basis%20and%20435.48%25%20over%20the%20past%20year.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250819112211/https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/25/08/47204445/short-seller-andrew-left-says-openai-at-500-billion-puts-palantir-at-40-and-thats-generous#:~:text=%E2%80%98OpenAI%20At%20%24500%20Billion%20Puts%20Palantir%20At%20%2440%E2%80%99%20Using,for%20Palantir%2C%20a%20figure%20the%20report%20labels%20as%20generous.)

## What would change the view

The testable base case is about exposure, not direction: on ordinary trading days, PLTU’s returns should swing roughly twice as much as PLTR’s, which can be checked against daily fund net asset value returns. The endpoint alone cannot establish annualized volatility, tracking error or the likelihood of a wipeout. The strongest case for holding is a sustained PLTR advance with few reversals, when daily gains can compound in the holder’s favor. Upward revisions to Palantir’s revenue estimates would weaken Citron’s valuation case at the same multiple; a rising stock with repeated sharp reversals would be less supportive of holding the leveraged fund. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250504025417/https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/PLTU#:~:text=Bull%20or%20Bear%2C%20Seeking%20Alpha%20is%20there%20Markets%20change%2C,Overview%20PLTU%3A%20Too%20Bullish%20On%20Palantir%2C%20Even%20For%20Me) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250819112211/https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/25/08/47204445/short-seller-andrew-left-says-openai-at-500-billion-puts-palantir-at-40-and-thats-generous#:~:text=The%20report%E2%80%99s%20central%20argument%20hinges%20on%20a%20direct%20valuation,be%20expensive%22.%20OpenAI%E2%80%99s%20%E2%80%98Unprecedented%E2%80%99%20Growth%20Versus%20PLTR%E2%80%99s%20%E2%80%98Steady%20Progress%E2%80%99)

question: Given MSCI's sustained 52-week underperformance relative to the S&P 500 and XLF, how should investors interpret the divergence between heavy institutional selling by firms like BlackRock and Capital Research versus the aggressive insider buying and strategic expansion into private assets via the Intapp and Moody's partnerships?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-06-05

**Research question**
Given MSCI's sustained 52-week underperformance relative to the S&P 500 and XLF, how should investors interpret the divergence between heavy institutional selling by firms like BlackRock and Capital Research versus the aggressive insider buying and strategic expansion into private assets via the Intapp and Moody's partnerships?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Evidence

The relative-return check is inconclusive. XLF’s quoted gain is measured from a low on 7 Dec 2023, not over the trailing period ending 2025-06-05. The S&P 500 figure is a long-run compound return including dividends, and no comparable MSCI stock return is supplied. Compare dividend-reinvested returns for MSCI, the broad index and XLF over identical dates. Even a verified end-to-end shortfall would not show it was sustained without checking the intervening relative performance. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20241204095631/https://www.intelligentinvestor.com.au/shares/nyse-xlf/financial-select-sector-spdr-fund#:~:text=Financial%20Select%20Sector%20SPDR%20Fund%27s%20%28XLF%29%2052-week%20high%20is,average%20trading%20volume%20of%209%2C864%2C252%20XLF%20shares%20per%20day.) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1293815072)

A decline in reported holdings is not a discretionary sell call. BlackRock reports for operating subsidiaries and disclaims discretion at the parent. The filing excerpt identifies a holdings table but gives no MSCI share counts, and no comparable Capital Research positions are supplied. Compare shares, not market values, across quarter ends for the same reporting entities. Even a confirmed reduction could reflect client redemptions or index rebalancing; attributing it to a bearish view requires evidence from the manager. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20241208193934/https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1364742/000108636424008417/xslForm13F_X02/primary_doc.xml#:~:text=Signature%2C%20Place%2C%20and%20Date%20of%20Signing%3A%20BlackRock%2C%20Inc.%20is,of%20all%20such%20subsidiaries.%20Report%20Type%20%28Check%20only%20one.%29%3A) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250325183323/https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1067983/000095012324011775/0000950123-24-011775-index.htm#:~:text=Seq%20Description%20Document%20Type%20Size%20INFORMATION%20TABLE%20FOR%20FORM%2013F%20Complete%20submission%20text%20file) [5](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1223018657)

Insider buying would carry more weight than an institutional holdings change as evidence of personal conviction if insiders voluntarily put material new cash at risk. No insider transaction records here identify buyers, dates, prices or size relative to prior stakes. Check those records for open-market purchases rather than grants or option exercises before treating the two groups as taking opposite views. Even a verified purchase would not establish what the buyer expects from private assets. [5](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1223018657)

## What would change the view

The base case gives MSCI credit for owning Burgiss data but assumes no incremental partnership revenue in the buy decision. The strongest bullish alternative is that Intapp and Moody’s could bring that data to paying clients faster than MSCI could alone. The supplied record establishes the acquisition, not either partnership’s terms, paid adoption or economics. Reconsider an entry if MSCI discloses partner-sourced paid contracts converting into recurring private-assets revenue, distinguishes that growth from acquired Burgiss sales, and the contribution supports the share price. Announcements or a rebound against the benchmarks would not meet that test. [6](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1284092066)

question: How has the acquisition and integration of NuVasive transformed Globus Medical’s (GMED) operational leverage and capital structure, and to what extent does the 2025 non-GAAP EPS projection of 3.01 reflect the successful capture of synergies and the firm’s return to debt-free status?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-05-27

**Research question**
How has the acquisition and integration of NuVasive transformed Globus Medical’s (GMED) operational leverage and capital structure, and to what extent does the 2025 non-GAAP EPS projection of 3.01 reflect the successful capture of synergies and the firm’s return to debt-free status?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Evidence

The operating case begins with the merger’s completion, announced on September 1, 2023, rather than the earlier deal report in February 2023. Selling a broader portfolio through a shared commercial network could spread existing costs over more revenue; removing duplicate functions could lower costs even at flat sales. Those are distinct mechanisms. The closing statement describes capabilities and revenue potential, not expenses actually eliminated. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1275930656) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1283775401) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250518080909/https://www.surgicalroboticstechnology.com/news/globus-medical-completes-merger-with-nuvasive/#:~:text=%E2%80%9CWe%E2%80%99re%20thrilled%20to%20begin%20our%20journey%20together%20to%20create,surgeon%20customers%20and%20their%20patients%20as%20a%20combined%20company.%E2%80%9D)

The closest guidance reference is a third-party account of management’s revised net sales outlook for FY 2024, not a company forecast of adjusted EPS for 2025. The article’s author identifies its opinions as their own, but the excerpt does not give the EPS figure either. A dated company outlook or analyst estimate naming the metric, period and amount would settle authorship; a point estimate alone does not. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20241022062513/https://seekingalpha.com/article/4699419-globus-medical-nuvasive-merger-unlocks-incremental-nopat-growth#:~:text=Globus%20Medical%20faced%20market%20backlash%20post-merger%20with%20NuVasive%2C%20but,high%20growth%20and%20increased%20profits%20with%20lower%20operating%20costs.) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20241022062513/https://seekingalpha.com/article/4699419-globus-medical-nuvasive-merger-unlocks-incremental-nopat-growth#:~:text=Analyst%E2%80%99s%20Disclosure%3A%20I%2Fwe%20have%20a%20beneficial%20long%20position%20in,licensed%20or%20certified%20by%20any%20institute%20or%20regulatory%20body.)

The all-stock terms describe how Globus paid NuVasive shareholders, not whether the combined company had outstanding borrowings. Equity consideration makes diluted share count relevant to EPS; it does not demonstrate repayment of inherited debt or a decline in interest expense. The explicit “debt-free” wording concerns the purchase terms for BMG, a different target. Verification requires a dated consolidated balance sheet and debt note showing gross borrowings, not merely cash exceeding debt, plus any subsequent borrowing or repayment through the cutoff. [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1283775401) [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20190915184902/https://www.beckersspine.com/orthopedic-a-spine-device-a-implant-news/item/24505-globus-medical-acquires-device-manufacturer-5-key-notes.html#:~:text=1.%20Globus%20Medical%20will%20pay%20%2452.9%20million%20in%20cash,in%20March%202015%20after%20the%20companies%20satisfy%20closing%20conditions.)

## What would change the view

The base case is that integration offers cost savings, but sales growth is the strongest competing explanation for better operating earnings: the contemporary account describes growth while framing lower costs as an aim. The distinguishing signal would be a decline in comparable operating costs at similar sales volume and mix, tied to documented integration actions. To translate that into adjusted EPS, start with prior-period adjusted earnings, separate incremental realized savings from sales and mix effects, then isolate interest and tax changes and apply each period’s diluted share count. Compare the GAAP-to-adjusted reconciliations for changes in exclusions. Without that bridge, neither a higher EPS figure nor a debt payoff would measure synergy capture. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20241022062513/https://seekingalpha.com/article/4699419-globus-medical-nuvasive-merger-unlocks-incremental-nopat-growth#:~:text=Globus%20Medical%20faced%20market%20backlash%20post-merger%20with%20NuVasive%2C%20but,high%20growth%20and%20increased%20profits%20with%20lower%20operating%20costs.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250518080909/https://www.surgicalroboticstechnology.com/news/globus-medical-completes-merger-with-nuvasive/#:~:text=%E2%80%9CWe%E2%80%99re%20thrilled%20to%20begin%20our%20journey%20together%20to%20create,surgeon%20customers%20and%20their%20patients%20as%20a%20combined%20company.%E2%80%9D)

question: Given Apellis Pharmaceuticals' reported EPS of -$0.74 for Q1 2025 and its sNDA submission for EMPAVELI in rare kidney diseases, how will the company’s capital requirements and path to profitability evolve as it transitions from PNH commercialization to Phase 3 trials in FSGS and DGF?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-05-11

**Research question**
Given Apellis Pharmaceuticals' reported EPS of -$0.74 for Q1 2025 and its sNDA submission for EMPAVELI in rare kidney diseases, how will the company’s capital requirements and path to profitability evolve as it transitions from PNH commercialization to Phase 3 trials in FSGS and DGF?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-05-11, Apellis has not demonstrated that available cash and commercial receipts will fund its kidney program through operating break-even. I would retain external financing as a contingency, not call it likely: the evidence identifies existing pegcetacoplan indications and a late-stage kidney study, but establishes neither Apellis’s liquidity nor its share of future trial costs. The size and timing of any funding gap are therefore unknown. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1279327704) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250417033533/https://www.tga.gov.au/resources/prescription-medicines-registrations/syfovre-apellis-australia-pty-ltd#:~:text=SYFOVRE%20is%20indicated%20for%20the%20treatment%20of%20adult%20patients,cultures%2C%20and%20to%20all%20Elders%20both%20past%20and%20present.)

## Evidence

The renal indications supported by VALIANT are C3 glomerulopathy and primary immune complex–mediated membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis. That identifies the diseases studied, not the exact indications, patient population or status of the EMPAVELI sNDA described in the question. Verifying the submission requires a dated company or FDA filing notice; VALIANT is not evidence of a filing for FSGS or DGF. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1279327704)

Neither focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) nor delayed graft function (DGF) can be treated as a confirmed new Apellis trial expense. VALIANT is the documented Phase 3 study; NOBLE studied recurrent disease in transplant recipients, not DGF. The passages do not verify whether the proposed FSGS or DGF trials have begun, who sponsors them or who ultimately pays. Assigning Apellis either the full cost or no cost would be speculative. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1279327704) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250203224513/https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39810766/#:~:text=Create%20a%20file%20for%20external%20citation%20management%20software%20Introduction%3A,by%20subcutaneous%20infusion%20plus%20standard-of-care%20%28SOC%29%20or%20SOC%20only.)

## What would change the view

The financing test is whether unrestricted cash covers the largest cumulative cash shortfall before sustained operating break-even, while leaving enough liquidity to operate. Start with collections from existing products, give no base-case credit for renal sales before approval, and vary the unreimbursed trial spend rather than assuming it. Self-funding becomes credible if quarterly filings show the cash deficit narrowing fast enough and collaboration terms limit Apellis’s outlay. The strongest contrary case is that Apellis must pay substantial trial costs before commercial margins cover them. Dated trial records and cost-sharing terms, together with quarterly cash flow, debt payments and product margins, would distinguish those outcomes; clinical efficacy alone cannot. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1279327704) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250417033533/https://www.tga.gov.au/resources/prescription-medicines-registrations/syfovre-apellis-australia-pty-ltd#:~:text=SYFOVRE%20is%20indicated%20for%20the%20treatment%20of%20adult%20patients,cultures%2C%20and%20to%20all%20Elders%20both%20past%20and%20present.)

## Sources

1. [Pegcetacoplan](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1279327704), available by 2025-03-07.
2. [SYFOVRE (Apellis Australia Pty Ltd) | Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA)](https://web.archive.org/web/20250417033533/https://www.tga.gov.au/resources/prescription-medicines-registrations/syfovre-apellis-australia-pty-ltd#:~:text=SYFOVRE%20is%20indicated%20for%20the%20treatment%20of%20adult%20patients,cultures%2C%20and%20to%20all%20Elders%20both%20past%20and%20present.), available by 2025-04-17.
3. question: Given CEO Lisa Su's projection of tens of billions in AI revenue, how will the reported resumption of AMD's MI308 exports to China—facilitated by shifting U.S. trade policies—impact the company's data center margins and growth trajectory through the second half of 2025?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-08-05

**Research question**
Given CEO Lisa Su's projection of tens of billions in AI revenue, how will the reported resumption of AMD's MI308 exports to China—facilitated by shifting U.S. trade policies—impact the company's data center margins and growth trajectory through the second half of 2025?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-08-05, assume no China sales of AMD’s MI308 accelerators in the second-half 2025 base case. Treat a restart as contingent upside to Data Center revenue, not as a reason to raise the segment’s operating-margin forecast. The U.S. Commerce Department signaled that license reviews would proceed; AMD said shipments would follow approval. Neither statement establishes a shipment or recognized revenue. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250722060924/https://www.notebookcheck.net/Washington-clears-AMD-to-resume-shipments-of-advanced-AI-chips-to-China.1059400.0.html#:~:text=The%20U.S.%20Commerce%20Department%20has%20told%20AMD%20that%20its,hit%20of%20about%20%245.5%20billion%20tied%20to%20H20%20restrictions.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250722125344/https://www.cnbc.com/2025/07/15/amd-mi308-ai-chip-china.html#:~:text=Advanced%20Micro%20Devices%20said%20Tuesday%20that%20it%20will%20soon,an%20AMD%20spokesperson%20said%20in%20a%20statement%20to%20CNBC.)

## Evidence

The reported $800 million is not a second-half sales estimate. One July account calls it estimated lost revenue; another describes a potential hit to results. Those are different measures. An inventory charge reduces profit when recorded; it is neither a lost customer order nor revenue AMD can recover by obtaining a license. The accounts do not reconcile the figures or quantify orders still available to fill. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250716215652/https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/amd-resume-ai-chip-shipments-china-us-eases-export-review#:~:text=CEO%20Lisa%20Su%20is%20also%20expected%20to%20attend%20an,chips%20to%20China%20after%20receiving%20similar%20assurances%20from%20Washington.) [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250722060924/https://www.notebookcheck.net/Washington-clears-AMD-to-resume-shipments-of-advanced-AI-chips-to-China.1059400.0.html#:~:text=The%20U.S.%20Commerce%20Department%20has%20told%20AMD%20that%20its,hit%20of%20about%20%245.5%20billion%20tied%20to%20H20%20restrictions.)

A rebound in companywide gross margin as an inventory charge falls out of the comparison would not demonstrate better underlying Data Center operating margin. For the segment margin to rise on resumed sales, operating profit on the additional business, relative to its revenue, would have to exceed the segment’s existing margin. The export reports provide neither a segment operating-margin baseline nor the selling prices, costs or inventory-charge allocation needed to test that condition. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250722060924/https://www.notebookcheck.net/Washington-clears-AMD-to-resume-shipments-of-advanced-AI-chips-to-China.1059400.0.html#:~:text=The%20U.S.%20Commerce%20Department%20has%20told%20AMD%20that%20its,hit%20of%20about%20%245.5%20billion%20tied%20to%20H20%20restrictions.) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250716215652/https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/amd-resume-ai-chip-shipments-china-us-eases-export-review#:~:text=Written%20by%20RTTNews.com%20for%20RTTNews-%3E%20%28RTTNews%29%20-%20Advanced%20Micro,to%20U.S.%20AI%20leadership%2C%22%20AMD%20said%20in%20a%20statement.)

## Outlook

The base case therefore gets no second-half growth contribution from a China restart; it does not imply that the rest of Data Center stops growing. [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250722125344/https://www.cnbc.com/2025/07/15/amd-mi308-ai-chip-china.html#:~:text=Advanced%20Micro%20Devices%20said%20Tuesday%20that%20it%20will%20soon,an%20AMD%20spokesperson%20said%20in%20a%20statement%20to%20CNBC.) [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250722060924/https://www.notebookcheck.net/Washington-clears-AMD-to-resume-shipments-of-advanced-AI-chips-to-China.1059400.0.html#:~:text=The%20U.S.%20Commerce%20Department%20has%20told%20AMD%20that%20its,hit%20of%20about%20%245.5%20billion%20tied%20to%20H20%20restrictions.)

## What would change the view

The strongest upside case is prompt approval while customers still want delivery before year-end. Move sales into the forecast when AMD confirms issued licenses and orders with a second-half delivery schedule; use subsequent shipment disclosures and reported revenue to test how much actually landed in the period. Raise the underlying margin forecast only with evidence of profitable mix improvement, rather than a comparison flattered by the earlier charge. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250716215652/https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/amd-resume-ai-chip-shipments-china-us-eases-export-review#:~:text=Written%20by%20RTTNews.com%20for%20RTTNews-%3E%20%28RTTNews%29%20-%20Advanced%20Micro,to%20U.S.%20AI%20leadership%2C%22%20AMD%20said%20in%20a%20statement.) question: How does MicroStrategy’s rapid expansion of its STRK preferred stock program, offering high effective yields of 9.9%, impact its overall cost of capital and solvency risk, especially considering the persistent bearish sentiment in MSTR options markets observed throughout early 2025?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-06-29

**Research question**
How does MicroStrategy’s rapid expansion of its STRK preferred stock program, offering high effective yields of 9.9%, impact its overall cost of capital and solvency risk, especially considering the persistent bearish sentiment in MSTR options markets observed throughout early 2025?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

By 2025-06-29, Strategy had priced 7,300,000 shares of STRK for estimated net proceeds of $563.4 million. Selling STRK rather than common stock adds a cumulative dividend claim for each dollar raised. Relative to low-coupon convertible debt, STRK can cost more in annual payouts but poses less refinancing risk because it has no maturity. The evidence establishes neither a rise in Strategy’s overall weighted cost of capital nor a solvency warning from MSTR options. It documents the launch pricing, not the pace or net proceeds of subsequent sales through the cutoff. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250627045016/https://www.strategy.com/press/microstrategy-announces-pricing-of-strike-preferred-stock-offering-strk_01-31-2025#:~:text=Press%20Release%20%E2%80%A2%20January%2031%2C%202025%20TYSONS%20CORNER%2C%20Va.%E2%80%94%28BUSINESS,including%20the%20acquisition%20of%20bitcoin%20and%20for%20working%20capital.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250217134821/https://www.benzinga.com/content/43755797/microstrategys-8-preferred-stock-what-investors-should-know#:~:text=Dividend%20Dynamics%3A%20Understanding%20STKR%E2%80%99s%208%25%20Dividend%20On%20Jan.%2031%2C,dividends%20through%20shares%20of%20common%20stock%20rather%20than%20cash.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250326185400/https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2025/01/02/bitcoin-leveraged-play-micro-strategys-bullish-call-skew-disappears-in-cautious-market-sentiment#:~:text=Traders%20are%20no%20longer%20chasing%20upside%20in%20Nasdaq-listed%20MicroStrategy,than%20the%20unusually%20high%20premium%20observed%20three%20weeks%20ago.)

## Evidence

Dividend cost is not the same as total economic cost. Common issuance avoids a fixed payout but gives new holders a share of future upside; a convertible can obtain a lower coupon by giving investors conversion rights. Preferred dividends generally lack the corporate tax deduction available for interest. Those differences favor common on immediate cash needs and can favor a convertible on annual after-tax financing expense. They do not rank the alternatives on total cost without comparable issue terms, the value of potential dilution, required equity returns and the weights of each funding source. [4](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1255556769) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20230518071742/https://www.microstrategy.com/content/dam/website-assets/collateral/financial-documents/financial-document-archive/form-8-k-12-28-2022.pdf#:~:text=Item%208.01.%20Other%20Events.%20On%20December%2028%2C%202022%2C%20MicroStrategy,between%20October%201%2C%202022%20and%20December%2027%2C%202022%2C%20MicroStrategy)

The options observations do not establish persistent pricing of insolvency. In March, 250-day put-call volatility skew moved from -20% to parity: calls lost their premium, but puts did not acquire one. The June report’s 3.86 put/call open-interest ratio measures outstanding positions for a particular expiration, not the price of downside protection or whether put holders were hedging existing stock. It also reports new call activity. Together these observations fit reduced upside enthusiasm and demand for Bitcoin-sensitive downside hedges; neither isolates default risk. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250326185400/https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2025/01/02/bitcoin-leveraged-play-micro-strategys-bullish-call-skew-disappears-in-cautious-market-sentiment#:~:text=Traders%20are%20no%20longer%20chasing%20upside%20in%20Nasdaq-listed%20MicroStrategy,than%20the%20unusually%20high%20premium%20observed%20three%20weeks%20ago.) [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20250621174833/https://www.ainvest.com/news/bitcoin-bull-run-fuels-microstrategy-momentum-navigating-options-risks-2506/#:~:text=Option%20Markets%20Signal%20Volatility%2C%20Not%20Just%20Bullishness%20While%20the,volatility%2C%20but%20only%20if%20Bitcoin%20sustains%20its%20upward%20momentum.)

## Outlook

The base case is pressure on cash or common shareholders before pressure on solvency. If Strategy uses proceeds to buy Bitcoin, it must find cash elsewhere to maintain cash dividends without selling assets. It can instead defer dividends, leaving arrears, or pay in common shares, diluting holders. Neither choice is equivalent to missing a required debt payment. Test the base case by comparing cash dividends with operating cash generation and liquid reserves, and by tracking stock-settled dividends and arrears. The launch announcement gives intended uses, not dividend coverage at the cutoff. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250627045016/https://www.strategy.com/press/microstrategy-announces-pricing-of-strike-preferred-stock-offering-strk_01-31-2025#:~:text=Press%20Release%20%E2%80%A2%20January%2031%2C%202025%20TYSONS%20CORNER%2C%20Va.%E2%80%94%28BUSINESS,including%20the%20acquisition%20of%20bitcoin%20and%20for%20working%20capital.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250217134821/https://www.benzinga.com/content/43755797/microstrategys-8-preferred-stock-what-investors-should-know#:~:text=Dividend%20Dynamics%3A%20Understanding%20STKR%E2%80%99s%208%25%20Dividend%20On%20Jan.%2031%2C,dividends%20through%20shares%20of%20common%20stock%20rather%20than%20cash.) [4](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1255556769)

## What would change the view

The strongest alternative is that put demand anticipated a Bitcoin drawdown severe enough to shut Strategy out of funding markets while debt payments came due. A sustained premium for MSTR puts beyond that explained by Bitcoin volatility, alongside widening debt spreads and a documented cash shortfall against maturities, would favor that interpretation over ordinary hedging. The historical margin-call discussion concerned a specific earlier loan; it is not a current liquidation threshold or a substitute for that liquidity test. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250326185400/https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2025/01/02/bitcoin-leveraged-play-micro-strategys-bullish-call-skew-disappears-in-cautious-market-sentiment#:~:text=Traders%20are%20no%20longer%20chasing%20upside%20in%20Nasdaq-listed%20MicroStrategy,than%20the%20unusually%20high%20premium%20observed%20three%20weeks%20ago.) question: How is Aker Solutions' dual-track strategy—expanding high-margin 'Life Cycle' services with Vår Energi while securing large-scale 'New Build' renewable infrastructure like BalWin—affecting its overall margin stability and competitive positioning in the offshore energy transition through the second half of 2025?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-07-09

**Research question**
How is Aker Solutions' dual-track strategy—expanding high-margin 'Life Cycle' services with Vår Energi while securing large-scale 'New Build' renewable infrastructure like BalWin—affecting its overall margin stability and competitive positioning in the offshore energy transition through the second half of 2025?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-07-09, Aker Solutions’ NOK 0.5 billion to NOK 1.5 billion Vår Energi renewal helps keep crews employed through the second half of 2025, but I would not count on a material cushion for the group EBITDA margin. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250702105006/https://www.akersolutions.com/news/news-archive/2025/aker-solutions-asa-aker-solutions-signs-long-term-strategic-partnership-with-var-energi/#:~:text=V%C3%A5r%20Energi%27s%20operations%20span%20the%20entire%20Norwegian%20continental%20shelf,being%20between%20NOK%200.5%20billion%20and%20NOK%201.5%20billion) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250702111632/https://www.akersolutions.com/news/news-archive/2024/aker-solutions-asaaker-solutions-secures-new-frame-agreement-with-var-energi/#:~:text=Aker%20Solutions%20secures%20new%20frame%20agreement%20with%20V%C3%A5r%20Energi,the%20contract%20by%20up%20to%20three%20additional%20two-year%20periods.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250702111632/https://www.akersolutions.com/news/news-archive/2024/aker-solutions-asaaker-solutions-secures-new-frame-agreement-with-var-energi/#:~:text=%22This%20contract%20renewal%20reflects%20our%20long-term%20relationship%20and%20status,with%20V%C3%A5r%20Energi%20to%20achieve%20this%20goal%2C%22%20said%20Eikeseth.) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250501015343/https://news.cision.com/aker-solutions-asa/r/aker-solutions-asa--first-quarter-results,c4143132#:~:text=Order%20intake%20for%20the%20quarter%20ended%20at%20NOK%2025.6,3.4%20billion%20at%20the%20end%20of%20the%20first%20quarter.)

## Evidence

The Vår agreement protects an existing workload rather than creating an entirely new one. Aker already serviced Jotun, Balder and Ringhorne; the renewed work started in January 2025 and is included in the broader partnership, so the announcements should not be counted as separate awards for the same work. Continuity can reduce idle time in Stavanger and Egersund even without a premium service margin. Neither the timing of individual orders nor their profitability is disclosed, and the extension options are not firm orders. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250702111632/https://www.akersolutions.com/news/news-archive/2024/aker-solutions-asaaker-solutions-secures-new-frame-agreement-with-var-energi/#:~:text=%22This%20contract%20renewal%20reflects%20our%20long-term%20relationship%20and%20status,with%20V%C3%A5r%20Energi%20to%20achieve%20this%20goal%2C%22%20said%20Eikeseth.) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250702111632/https://www.akersolutions.com/news/news-archive/2024/aker-solutions-asaaker-solutions-secures-new-frame-agreement-with-var-energi/#:~:text=The%20work%20will%20be%20managed%20from%20Aker%20Solutions%27%20office,The%20work%20under%20the%20frame%20agreement%20starts%20January%202025.) [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250702105006/https://www.akersolutions.com/news/news-archive/2025/aker-solutions-asa-aker-solutions-signs-long-term-strategic-partnership-with-var-energi/#:~:text=V%C3%A5r%20Energi%27s%20operations%20span%20the%20entire%20Norwegian%20continental%20shelf,being%20between%20NOK%200.5%20billion%20and%20NOK%201.5%20billion) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250702111632/https://www.akersolutions.com/news/news-archive/2024/aker-solutions-asaaker-solutions-secures-new-frame-agreement-with-var-energi/#:~:text=Aker%20Solutions%20secures%20new%20frame%20agreement%20with%20V%C3%A5r%20Energi,the%20contract%20by%20up%20to%20three%20additional%20two-year%20periods.)

The stronger New Build argument concerns future bids, not current profit. Aker reported NOK 25.6 billion of quarterly intake and NOK 72.1 billion of secured backlog across the group. Management says most new orders emphasize standardization and more balanced risk sharing. Reusing a proven grid-platform design could lower the cost and execution risk of the next bid. But the disclosure does not allocate intake or backlog to BalWin or demonstrate successful delivery. Nor is the roughly NOK 85 billion tender pipeline a measure of offshore-grid demand: European oil and gas opportunities dominate it. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250501015343/https://news.cision.com/aker-solutions-asa/r/aker-solutions-asa--first-quarter-results,c4143132#:~:text=Order%20intake%20for%20the%20quarter%20ended%20at%20NOK%2025.6,3.4%20billion%20at%20the%20end%20of%20the%20first%20quarter.) [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20250702104518/https://www.akersolutions.com/news/news-archive/2025/aker-solutions-asa-first-quarter-results/#:~:text=Outlook%20and%20financial%20guiding%20The%20company%20continues%20to%20have,which%20will%20be%20paid%20on%20May%208%2C%202025.%20ENDS)

## Outlook

My base case is that second-half execution of legacy renewables matters more to the margin than the Vår renewal does. The comparable first-quarter margin was 7.2 percent excluding OneSubsea net income, not the headline 8.4 percent. That is consistent with management’s 7.0-7.5 percent underlying full-year range on revenue expected to exceed NOK 55 billion; the range is not second-half guidance. With legacy projects due for delivery this year, the costs Aker ultimately bears after client and subcontractor negotiations remain a nearer-term risk than the size of its new order book suggests. [7](https://web.archive.org/web/20250702104518/https://www.akersolutions.com/news/news-archive/2025/aker-solutions-asa-first-quarter-results/#:~:text=Key%20developments%20Revenue%20in%20the%20first%20quarter%20increased%20to,both%20clients%20and%20subcontractors%20to%20solve%20these%20commercial%20challenges.) [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20250702104518/https://www.akersolutions.com/news/news-archive/2025/aker-solutions-asa-first-quarter-results/#:~:text=Outlook%20and%20financial%20guiding%20The%20company%20continues%20to%20have,which%20will%20be%20paid%20on%20May%208%2C%202025.%20ENDS)

## What would change the view

The strongest upside alternative is that Vår orders arrive early enough to fill otherwise idle capacity and materially offset legacy costs. I would look for disclosed second-half Vår volumes and a Life Cycle earnings improvement tied to utilization, not just a better group margin that could reflect a favorable legacy settlement. For BalWin, a documented delivery milestone followed by a grid award reusing the same design would turn a plausible bidding advantage into evidence of repeat business. [8](https://web.archive.org/web/20250702105006/https://www.akersolutions.com/news/news-archive/2025/aker-solutions-asa-aker-solutions-signs-long-term-strategic-partnership-with-var-energi/#:~:text=The%20contract%20has%20a%20duration%20of%205%20years%20with,one%20of%20the%20world%27s%20fastest-growing%20oil%20and%20gas%20companies.%E2%80%9D) [7](https://web.archive.org/web/20250702104518/https://www.akersolutions.com/news/news-archive/2025/aker-solutions-asa-first-quarter-results/#:~:text=Key%20developments%20Revenue%20in%20the%20first%20quarter%20increased%20to,both%20clients%20and%20subcontractors%20to%20solve%20these%20commercial%20challenges.)
