question: How do Oxford Economics' macroeconomic projections regarding tariff-driven price inflation and labor market resilience, as analyzed by Michael Pearce, reconcile with Tourism Economics' sector-specific growth forecasts for the U.S. leisure and travel industry through the end of 2025?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-08-12

**Research question**
How do Oxford Economics' macroeconomic projections regarding tariff-driven price inflation and labor market resilience, as analyzed by Michael Pearce, reconcile with Tourism Economics' sector-specific growth forecasts for the U.S. leisure and travel industry through the end of 2025?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-08-12, the available evidence does not establish that Tourism Economics forecast growth in aggregate U.S. leisure travel through year-end 2025. Its documented full-year forecast was an 8.2% decline in international overnight arrivals, reaffirmed using data through June. That rules out a forecast gain in inbound visitor volume as the explanation for industry growth. It leaves open whether domestic trips or higher prices could support revenue. Neither is established by the arrivals forecast. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250802193734/https://www.oxfordeconomics.com/resource/us-inbound-travel-arrivals-decline-2025/#:~:text=The%20forecasted%208.2%25%20decline%20in%20annual%20international%20arrivals%20solidifies,air%20arrivals%20contracted%2028.0%25%20and%2013.3%25%20year-to-date%20%28YTD%29%2C%20respectively.)

## Evidence

Michael Pearce’s July briefing for Oxford Economics argued that tariff revenue would be hard to replace, making tariffs likely to persist. June’s 0.3% increase in consumer prices is an observation, not Pearce’s inflation forecast or a measure of travel prices. [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250724212321/https://www.supplychainbrain.com/articles/42097-us-tariffs-are-here-to-stay-says-oxford-economics#:~:text=As%20the%20much-anticipated%20deadline%20for%20the%20implementation%20of%20a,exporters%20face%20higher%20trade%20barriers%20today%20because%20of%20retaliation.%E2%80%9D) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250721232852/https://www.reuters.com/business/us-inflation-expected-rise-june-with-tariff-driven-price-hikes-2025-07-15/#:~:text=Consumer%20Price%20Index%20increases%200.3%25%20in%20June%20Core%20CPI%20rises%200.2%25%3B%20advances%202.9%25%20on%20year-over-year%20basis)

Marriott’s August report does not fill the forecast gap. Leisure helped lift worldwide second-quarter revenue per available room by 1.5 percent, but U.S. and Canada revenue per available room was flat year over year. Growth at Marriott’s hotels abroad is not growth in visits to the U.S.; the combined U.S. and Canada figure, in turn, mixes leisure and business demand and does not separate room rates from occupancy. These are quarterly operating results, not a year-end forecast of U.S. leisure trips. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250809181447/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/marriott-international-reports-second-quarter-2025-results-302521754.html#:~:text=BETHESDA%2C%20Md.%2C%20Aug.%205%2C%202025%20%2FPRNewswire%2F%20--%20Marriott%20International%2C,net%20rooms%20growth%20to%20approach%205%20percent%20this%20year.)

## Outlook

The investment base case is uneven demand: expect destinations reliant on Canadian visitors to face a greater volume headwind than domestic-oriented markets, without assuming a nationwide leisure boom. Tourism Economics identified Seattle, Portland and Detroit as most exposed. The strongest alternative to a price-led revenue gain is a genuine domestic travel expansion despite inbound weakness. Rising domestic leisure trip counts and inflation-adjusted spending through year-end would favor that interpretation; rising nominal spending with flat trip counts and flat real spending would favor prices. A dated Tourism Economics forecast separating those measures would be needed to attribute either view to the firm. [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250802193734/https://www.oxfordeconomics.com/resource/us-inbound-travel-arrivals-decline-2025/#:~:text=Overseas%20arrivals%20fell%203.4%25%20in%20June%20compared%20to%20a,material%20changes%20to%20our%20Eurozone%20baseline%20forecast%20of%201.1%25...)

## Sources

1. [International Arrivals to the US Decline in 2025 | Tourism Economics](https://web.archive.org/web/20250802193734/https://www.oxfordeconomics.com/resource/us-inbound-travel-arrivals-decline-2025/#:~:text=The%20forecasted%208.2%25%20decline%20in%20annual%20international%20arrivals%20solidifies,air%20arrivals%20contracted%2028.0%25%20and%2013.3%25%20year-to-date%20%28YTD%29%2C%20respectively.), available by 2025-08-02.
2. [U.S. Tariffs are Here to Stay, Says Oxford Economics | SupplyChainBrain](https://web.archive.org/web/20250724212321/https://www.supplychainbrain.com/articles/42097-us-tariffs-are-here-to-stay-says-oxford-economics#:~:text=As%20the%20much-anticipated%20deadline%20for%20the%20implementation%20of%20a,exporters%20face%20higher%20trade%20barriers%20today%20because%20of%20retaliation.%E2%80%9D), available by 2025-07-24.
3. [US consumer prices rise in June as tariff pass-through begins | Reuters](https://web.archive.org/web/20250721232852/https://www.reuters.com/business/us-inflation-expected-rise-june-with-tariff-driven-price-hikes-2025-07-15/#:~:text=Consumer%20Price%20Index%20increases%200.3%25%20in%20June%20Core%20CPI%20rises%200.2%25%3B%20advances%202.9%25%20on%20year-over-year%20basis), available by 2025-07-21.

question: How does MicroStrategy’s utilization of the 10% Series A Perpetual Preferred Stock (STRF) as a funding vehicle for Bitcoin accumulation impact its weighted average cost of capital and institutional risk profile, particularly for major holders like American Balanced Fund and the iShares Preferred ETF?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-11-04

**Research question**
How does MicroStrategy’s utilization of the 10% Series A Perpetual Preferred Stock (STRF) as a funding vehicle for Bitcoin accumulation impact its weighted average cost of capital and institutional risk profile, particularly for major holders like American Balanced Fund and the iShares Preferred ETF?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-11-04, the evidence does not establish that Strategy raised or lowered its market-value-weighted cost of capital by issuing STRF rather than common stock or convertible debt to buy Bitcoin. It changed who bears the risk: STRF preserves common shareholders’ upside but adds a dividend claim ahead of them. The scale matters: Strategy’s Bitcoin was already reported to be worth $42.43 billion in December 2024; that is historical asset value, not STRF proceeds. Neither American Balanced Fund nor the iShares Preferred and Income Securities ETF is verified here as a STRF holder. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1320001949) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20251006133615/https://seekingalpha.com/article/4827775-strategy-common-stock-dilution-continues#:~:text=STRF%20stands%20out%20among%20Strategy%27s%20preferreds%20due%20to%20its,returns%20amid%20growing%20competition%20in%20the%20Bitcoin%20treasury%20space.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20251006133615/https://seekingalpha.com/article/4827775-strategy-common-stock-dilution-continues#:~:text=Analyst%E2%80%99s%20Disclosure%3AI%2Fwe%20have%20a%20beneficial%20long%20position%20in%20the,licensed%20or%20certified%20by%20any%20institute%20or%20regulatory%20body.)

## Evidence

Against common equity, the relevant comparison is required return, not dividend versus no dividend. [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20251006133615/https://seekingalpha.com/article/4827775-strategy-common-stock-dilution-continues#:~:text=STRF%20stands%20out%20among%20Strategy%27s%20preferreds%20due%20to%20its,returns%20amid%20growing%20competition%20in%20the%20Bitcoin%20treasury%20space.) [4](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1255556769)

Against convertible debt, STRF removes a maturity to refinance and does not give the investor a conversion option. A convertible’s low coupon therefore understates what shareholders give up: the investor also receives contingent equity upside. Compare the required return on its debt and option components, allowing for any usable interest tax shield; preferred dividends generally offer no such shield. Management’s stated aim of reducing convertible debt is consistent with reducing refinancing risk, not proof that preferred capital is cheaper. [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20251006133615/https://seekingalpha.com/article/4827775-strategy-common-stock-dilution-continues#:~:text=STRF%20stands%20out%20among%20Strategy%27s%20preferreds%20due%20to%20its,returns%20amid%20growing%20competition%20in%20the%20Bitcoin%20treasury%20space.) [4](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1255556769) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20251031115025/https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2025/10/20/michael-saylor-highlights-yield-gap-between-strf-strd-preferred-stock-offerings#:~:text=The%20company%20reported%20%2412%20billion%20in%20operating%20income%20and,has%20qualified%20for%20potential%20inclusion%20in%20the%20S%26P%20500.)

For American Balanced Fund, STRF ownership and portfolio weight are unknown; the same is true separately for the iShares Preferred and Income Securities ETF. The disclosed long position belongs to an analyst and may include derivatives. Neither that disclosure nor the ETF’s mandate establishes a holding. Check each fund’s latest dated holdings schedule available by the cutoff for the exact STRF series, not merely the issuer, and report the holdings date. Only if confirmed should STRF’s market value be measured against that fund’s net assets and combined with any separately verified Strategy exposure. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20251006133615/https://seekingalpha.com/article/4827775-strategy-common-stock-dilution-continues#:~:text=Analyst%E2%80%99s%20Disclosure%3AI%2Fwe%20have%20a%20beneficial%20long%20position%20in%20the,licensed%20or%20certified%20by%20any%20institute%20or%20regulatory%20body.)

## Outlook

The base case for a STRF investor is income with limited Bitcoin upside, not direct Bitcoin ownership. If Bitcoin falls persistently, the asset cushion beneath Strategy’s debt and preferred claims shrinks. STRF ranks ahead of common but behind debt, and a rise in required yields can depress a perpetual preferred’s price without any missed dividend. Reported STRF gains since mid-July do not contradict the later ‘B-’ rating: the former measure past shareholder returns; the latter assesses the issuer, not STRF specifically. [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20251006133615/https://seekingalpha.com/article/4827775-strategy-common-stock-dilution-continues#:~:text=Strategy%20Inc.%20has%20underperformed%20Bitcoin%20since%20mid-July%2C%20while%20STRF,have%20delivered%20strong%20returns%20through%20price%20appreciation%20and%20dividends.) [7](https://web.archive.org/web/20251028115422/https://www.strategy.com/press/s-p-global-ratings-assigns-a-b--issuer-credit-rating-to-strategy_10-27-2025#:~:text=S%26P%20Global%20Ratings%20Assigns%20a%20%E2%80%98B-%E2%80%99%20Issuer%20Credit%20Rating%20to%20Strategy%20Press%20Release%20%E2%80%A2%20October%2027%2C%202025) [4](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1255556769)

## What would change the view

For equal Bitcoin purchases, the testable base case is that STRF buys refinancing flexibility at a higher cash servicing cost than a low-coupon convertible. The strongest alternative is that surrendering conversion upside or issuing common is expensive enough to make STRF cheaper overall. The deciding signal is a lower pro forma WACC for STRF after pricing all three financing choices on the same issue date: use equal net proceeds, post-deal market-value weights and required returns that reflect the changed risk of the outstanding claims. The supplied evidence lacks those inputs; neither the preferred’s realized return nor management’s financing preference settles the comparison. [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20251006133615/https://seekingalpha.com/article/4827775-strategy-common-stock-dilution-continues#:~:text=STRF%20stands%20out%20among%20Strategy%27s%20preferreds%20due%20to%20its,returns%20amid%20growing%20competition%20in%20the%20Bitcoin%20treasury%20space.) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20251031115025/https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2025/10/20/michael-saylor-highlights-yield-gap-between-strf-strd-preferred-stock-offerings#:~:text=The%20company%20reported%20%2412%20billion%20in%20operating%20income%20and,has%20qualified%20for%20potential%20inclusion%20in%20the%20S%26P%20500.) [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20251006133615/https://seekingalpha.com/article/4827775-strategy-common-stock-dilution-continues#:~:text=Strategy%20Inc.%20has%20underperformed%20Bitcoin%20since%20mid-July%2C%20while%20STRF,have%20delivered%20strong%20returns%20through%20price%20appreciation%20and%20dividends.)

## Sources

1. [MicroStrategy](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1320001949), available by 2025-11-02.
2. [Strategy: Common Stock Dilution Continues (NASDAQ:MSTR) | Seeking Alpha](https://web.archive.org/web/20251006133615/https://seekingalpha.com/article/4827775-strategy-common-stock-dilution-continues#:~:text=STRF%20stands%20out%20among%20Strategy%27s%20preferreds%20due%20to%20its,returns%20amid%20growing%20competition%20in%20the%20Bitcoin%20treasury%20space.), available by 2025-10-06.
3. [Strategy: Common Stock Dilution Continues (NASDAQ:MSTR) | Seeking Alpha](https://web.archive.org/web/20251006133615/https://seekingalpha.com/article/4827775-strategy-common-stock-dilution-continues#:~:text=Analyst%E2%80%99s%20Disclosure%3AI%2Fwe%20have%20a%20beneficial%20long%20position%20in%20the,licensed%20or%20certified%20by%20any%20institute%20or%20regulatory%20body.), available by 2025-10-06.
4. [Preferred stock](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1255556769), available by 2024-11-05.
5. [Strategy (MSTR) Executive Chairman Michael Saylor Highlights Yield Gap Between Preferred Stock Offerings](https://web.archive.org/web/20251031115025/https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2025/10/20/michael-saylor-highlights-yield-gap-between-strf-strd-preferred-stock-offerings#:~:text=The%20company%20reported%20%2412%20billion%20in%20operating%20income%20and,has%20qualified%20for%20potential%20inclusion%20in%20the%20S%26P%20500.), available by 2025-10-31.
6. [Strategy: Common Stock Dilution Continues (NASDAQ:MSTR) | Seeking Alpha](https://web.archive.org/web/20251006133615/https://seekingalpha.com/article/4827775-strategy-common-stock-dilution-continues#:~:text=Strategy%20Inc.%20has%20underperformed%20Bitcoin%20since%20mid-July%2C%20while%20STRF,have%20delivered%20strong%20returns%20through%20price%20appreciation%20and%20dividends.), available by 2025-10-06.
7. [S&P Global Ratings Assigns a ‘B-’ Issuer Credit Rating to Strategy](https://web.archive.org/web/20251028115422/https://www.strategy.com/press/s-p-global-ratings-assigns-a-b--issuer-credit-rating-to-strategy_10-27-2025#:~:text=S%26P%20Global%20Ratings%20Assigns%20a%20%E2%80%98B-%E2%80%99%20Issuer%20Credit%20Rating%20to%20Strategy%20Press%20Release%20%E2%80%A2%20October%2027%2C%202025), available by 2025-10-28.

question: How does Michele Bullock’s 'timing vs. direction' framework, coupled with the RBA's warnings of a shallower easing cycle, align with market expectations for the August 12 policy meeting and the subsequent trajectory of Australian interest rates through late 2025?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-08-05

**Research question**
How does Michele Bullock’s 'timing vs. direction' framework, coupled with the RBA's warnings of a shallower easing cycle, align with market expectations for the August 12 policy meeting and the subsequent trajectory of Australian interest rates through late 2025?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-08-05, markets expected a cut at the RBA’s August 12 meeting: market reporting described a cut as near certain, and Westpac forecast a move from 3.85 per cent to 3.6%. That expectation fit Governor Michele Bullock’s view that the July hold was about when to ease, not whether to ease. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250731163746/https://www.afr.com/policy/economy/lower-inflation-sets-up-rba-rate-cut-20250728-p5mig2#:~:text=Lower%20fuel%20prices%20and%20easing%20home%20building%20costs%20have,the%20topics%2C%20people%20and%20companies%20that%20matter%20to%20you.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250803221114/https://www.rba.gov.au/speeches/2025/mc-gov-2025-07-08.html#:~:text=Media%20Conference%20Monetary%20Policy%20Decision%20Thank%20you%20for%20coming.,still%20on%20track%20to%20sustainably%20reach%202.5%20per%20cent.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250803015232/https://www.westpaciq.com.au/economics/2025/07/lucis-note-30-july-20252#:~:text=Accordingly%2C%20we%20expect%20the%20RBA%20to%20cut%20the%20cash,a%20little%20lower%20than%20what%20it%20forecast%20in%20May.) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250803221114/https://www.rba.gov.au/speeches/2025/mc-gov-2025-07-08.html#:~:text=In%20summary%2C%20we%20must%20keep%20inflation%20down%20while%20trying,that%20we%20are%20on%20a%20path%20towards%20easing%20further.)

## Evidence

The July hold and the subsequent August cut expectation reflected different information, not a reversal of policy. In July, Bullock wanted confirmation that inflation was moving sustainably toward 2.5 per cent. June-quarter underlying inflation then came in at 2.7 per cent, down from 2.9 per cent in March. That was stronger evidence for resuming cuts than the lower headline reading, which temporary energy subsidies helped depress. [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250803221114/https://www.rba.gov.au/speeches/2025/mc-gov-2025-07-08.html#:~:text=Media%20Conference%20Monetary%20Policy%20Decision%20Thank%20you%20for%20coming.,still%20on%20track%20to%20sustainably%20reach%202.5%20per%20cent.) [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250731163746/https://www.afr.com/policy/economy/lower-inflation-sets-up-rba-rate-cut-20250728-p5mig2#:~:text=Lower%20fuel%20prices%20and%20easing%20home%20building%20costs%20have,the%20topics%2C%20people%20and%20companies%20that%20matter%20to%20you.)

## Outlook

The base case is an August cut, a pause and a further cut in November, rather than cuts at successive meetings. That matches Westpac’s forecast, not an observed market-implied path. Bullock noted that 50 basis points of earlier easing had yet to work through the economy. That supports patience on timing, not a specific floor for rates. The available remarks do not specify a year-end target, and the market report gives no December futures or swap rate against which to test whether pricing was too aggressive. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250803015232/https://www.westpaciq.com.au/economics/2025/07/lucis-note-30-july-20252#:~:text=Accordingly%2C%20we%20expect%20the%20RBA%20to%20cut%20the%20cash,a%20little%20lower%20than%20what%20it%20forecast%20in%20May.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250803221114/https://www.rba.gov.au/speeches/2025/mc-gov-2025-07-08.html#:~:text=Media%20Conference%20Monetary%20Policy%20Decision%20Thank%20you%20for%20coming.,still%20on%20track%20to%20sustainably%20reach%202.5%20per%20cent.) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250803221114/https://www.rba.gov.au/speeches/2025/mc-gov-2025-07-08.html#:~:text=In%20summary%2C%20we%20must%20keep%20inflation%20down%20while%20trying,that%20we%20are%20on%20a%20path%20towards%20easing%20further.) [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250731163746/https://www.afr.com/policy/economy/lower-inflation-sets-up-rba-rate-cut-20250728-p5mig2#:~:text=Lower%20fuel%20prices%20and%20easing%20home%20building%20costs%20have,the%20topics%2C%20people%20and%20companies%20that%20matter%20to%20you.)

## What would change the view

The strongest alternative is an earlier follow-up cut if labour-market weakness persists while underlying inflation continues to ease. The July employment release, due after the August decision, would be an early test of the November timing, not evidence the Board could use in August. A sustained rise in unemployment would carry more weight than a single monthly increase; without it, the case for accelerating cuts remains weaker than the case for resuming them. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250803015232/https://www.westpaciq.com.au/economics/2025/07/lucis-note-30-july-20252#:~:text=Accordingly%2C%20we%20expect%20the%20RBA%20to%20cut%20the%20cash,a%20little%20lower%20than%20what%20it%20forecast%20in%20May.) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250803221114/https://www.rba.gov.au/speeches/2025/mc-gov-2025-07-08.html#:~:text=In%20summary%2C%20we%20must%20keep%20inflation%20down%20while%20trying,that%20we%20are%20on%20a%20path%20towards%20easing%20further.)

question: How will the impending Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) regulatory framework for Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) providers impact Klarna’s valuation and path to profitability, considering its 13% revenue growth to USD 701 million and its strategic transition toward becoming a fully regulated retail bank?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-05-27

**Research question**
How will the impending Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) regulatory framework for Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) providers impact Klarna’s valuation and path to profitability, considering its 13% revenue growth to USD 701 million and its strategic transition toward becoming a fully regulated retail bank?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-05-27, I would apply a modest near-term discount to Klarna relative to its value without the proposed UK BNPL rules, not a bank-licence premium. I would allow for a delay in sustained group net profit rather than move the forecast to a specific later quarter. Compliance spending and lost UK checkout volume could precede any reduction in credit losses. That matters when global adjusted operating profit is only $3 million. The paused US IPO’s prospective valuation of over $15 billion is not a traded price from which to measure an FCA discount; the reported reason for the pause was tariff-related investor uncertainty. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250520152709/https://www.ft.com/content/fb473d88-112b-432e-8e13-f7b974d7bf5d#:~:text=UK%20to%20regulate%20%E2%80%98buy%20now%2C%20pay%20later%E2%80%99%20lenders%20in,journalism%20on%20any%20device.%20Cancel%20anytime%20during%20your%20trial.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250519194221/https://financialit.net/news/payments/klarna-accelerates-global-momentum-q1-2025-and-unlocks-large-gains-ai-innovation#:~:text=Klarna%2C%20the%20AI-powered%20global%20payments%20and%20commerce%20network%2C%20today,grow.%20Sebastian%20Siemiatkowski%2C%20Co-founder%20and%20CEO%20of%20Klarna%2C%20said%3A) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250526121802/https://www.cnbc.com/2025/05/19/klarna-doubles-losses-in-first-quarter-as-ipo-remains-on-hold.html#:~:text=It%20comes%20as%20Klarna%20remains%20in%20pause%20mode%20regarding,one-off%20costs%20related%20to%20depreciation%2C%20share-based%20payments%20and%20restructuring.) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250520175619/https://tech.eu/2025/05/19/klarna-q1-revenues-climb-to-700m-but-losses-widen/#:~:text=Klarna%20paused%20plans%20to%20IPO%20in%20April%20amid%20investor,it%20had%20hit%20100m%20active%20consumers%20in%20the%20period.)

## Evidence

The growth is real, but it is not evidence of a UK regulatory benefit. For Q1 2025, reported revenue rose 13 per cent year on year to $701 million; Klarna’s 15% is the like-for-like revenue comparison for the same period and total. Separately, 13% was like-for-like growth in gross merchandise volume. These are global measures: US revenue alone rose 33%, and neither source isolates UK BNPL revenue. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250520175619/https://tech.eu/2025/05/19/klarna-q1-revenues-climb-to-700m-but-losses-widen/#:~:text=Klarna%20paused%20plans%20to%20IPO%20in%20April%20amid%20investor,it%20had%20hit%20100m%20active%20consumers%20in%20the%20period.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250519194221/https://financialit.net/news/payments/klarna-accelerates-global-momentum-q1-2025-and-unlocks-large-gains-ai-innovation#:~:text=Klarna%2C%20the%20AI-powered%20global%20payments%20and%20commerce%20network%2C%20today,grow.%20Sebastian%20Siemiatkowski%2C%20Co-founder%20and%20CEO%20of%20Klarna%2C%20said%3A) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250519194221/https://financialit.net/news/payments/klarna-accelerates-global-momentum-q1-2025-and-unlocks-large-gains-ai-innovation#:~:text=Reaping%20the%20benefits%20of%20spearheading%20AI%20Klarna%20is%20setting,4%20volumes%20four%20times%20higher%20than%20its%20nearest%20competitor.)

Adjusted profitability is not sustained net profitability. Klarna reported its fourth consecutive profitable quarter on an adjusted operating basis, yet its quarterly net loss widened to $99 million from $47 million a year earlier. Management attributed the deterioration to costs it described as one-off. Their non-recurrence could improve net earnings independently of UK policy; the evidence neither establishes that all will disappear nor attributes the loss to FCA oversight. [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250519194221/https://financialit.net/news/payments/klarna-accelerates-global-momentum-q1-2025-and-unlocks-large-gains-ai-innovation#:~:text=Klarna%2C%20the%20AI-powered%20global%20payments%20and%20commerce%20network%2C%20today,grow.%20Sebastian%20Siemiatkowski%2C%20Co-founder%20and%20CEO%20of%20Klarna%2C%20said%3A) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250526121802/https://www.cnbc.com/2025/05/19/klarna-doubles-losses-in-first-quarter-as-ipo-remains-on-hold.html#:~:text=It%20comes%20as%20Klarna%20remains%20in%20pause%20mode%20regarding,one-off%20costs%20related%20to%20depreciation%2C%20share-based%20payments%20and%20restructuring.)

## What would change the view

The strongest case for a premium is that better screening cuts defaults while merchants favour a large provider able to spread compliance costs. The base case instead assumes that extra checks reduce completed purchases in a product built on decisions within seconds. Once the rules and their scope are known, compare affected UK merchants’ approval and checkout completion rates with comparable unaffected merchants, then track credit losses as those loans mature. I would reverse the discount if loss savings and incremental merchant earnings consistently exceeded compliance costs and margin lost on declined sales. Without UK exposure, implementation costs or a recurring group net-income baseline, neither a percentage discount nor a break-even date is defensible. [6](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1289206705) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250519194221/https://financialit.net/news/payments/klarna-accelerates-global-momentum-q1-2025-and-unlocks-large-gains-ai-innovation#:~:text=Klarna%2C%20the%20AI-powered%20global%20payments%20and%20commerce%20network%2C%20today,grow.%20Sebastian%20Siemiatkowski%2C%20Co-founder%20and%20CEO%20of%20Klarna%2C%20said%3A) [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250520152709/https://www.ft.com/content/fb473d88-112b-432e-8e13-f7b974d7bf5d#:~:text=UK%20to%20regulate%20%E2%80%98buy%20now%2C%20pay%20later%E2%80%99%20lenders%20in,journalism%20on%20any%20device.%20Cancel%20anytime%20during%20your%20trial.)

question: How does the recent volatility in heavyweight investor sentiment for ServiceNow reflect institutional skepticism toward Bill McDermott’s 'AI control tower' strategy, and what specific risks are implied by the bearish positioning and mixed options sweeps observed as of July 8, 2025, preceding the Q2 earnings release?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-07-21

**Research question**
How does the recent volatility in heavyweight investor sentiment for ServiceNow reflect institutional skepticism toward Bill McDermott’s 'AI control tower' strategy, and what specific risks are implied by the bearish positioning and mixed options sweeps observed as of July 8, 2025, preceding the Q2 earnings release?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Evidence

The base case is earnings risk, not a forecast of an earnings miss. A shareholder buying a put for protection and a trader buying the same put to bet on a decline can produce the same print. A sweep describes how an order was executed, not the trader’s net exposure; mixed orders could also be legs of a spread. A test of the event-risk reading would be whether downside protection was especially expensive in expirations spanning the release and became cheaper afterward. The available company announcements describe products, not the options prices needed for that test. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250319091502/https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20231218270685/en/ServiceNow-to-Acquire-Task-Mining-Company-UltimateSuite-to-Enhance-Process-Mining-and-Intelligent-Automation-on-the-Now-Platform#:~:text=ServiceNow%E2%80%99s%20Latest%20Platform%20Release%20Adds%20to%20Thousands%20of%20AI,More%20for%20Faster%2C%20Smarter%20Workflows%20and%20Maximum%20Business%20Impact)

## Outlook

The AI-specific risk is that customers use governance and automation features without paying enough extra to lift subscription revenue. ServiceNow describes operational benefits, not paid Control Tower adoption. Broader subscription risk is different: weaker renewals or smaller expansions across the platform could slow growth even if AI sells well. Valuation is a separate risk again: subscription revenue could rise and the shares still fall if guidance disappoints relative to the growth investors had priced in. None of those outcomes is established by the reported flow. [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250319091502/https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20231218270685/en/ServiceNow-to-Acquire-Task-Mining-Company-UltimateSuite-to-Enhance-Process-Mining-and-Intelligent-Automation-on-the-Now-Platform#:~:text=SANTA%20CLARA%2C%20Calif.--%28BUSINESS%20WIRE%29--ServiceNow%20%28NYSE%3A%20NOW%29%2C%20the%20leading%20digital,to%20accelerate%20digital%20business%20transformation%20and%20enhance%20employee%20experiences.) [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250319091502/https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20231218270685/en/ServiceNow-to-Acquire-Task-Mining-Company-UltimateSuite-to-Enhance-Process-Mining-and-Intelligent-Automation-on-the-Now-Platform#:~:text=Investor%20Relations%20Darren%20Yip%20925.388.7205%20ir%40servicenow.com%20ServiceNow%20and%20NVIDIA,With%20Enhanced%20Automation%2C%20Stronger%20Governance%2C%20and%20Seamless%20Workflow%20Intelligence)

## What would change the view

The strongest alternative is a deliberate bearish bet that AI rollouts will not convert into paid upgrades. Weak incremental AI bookings alongside resilient core renewals would favor that business diagnosis; weakness across renewals and expansions would favor a broader subscription slowdown. The distinction matters because a partnership to deliver AI services is not evidence of customer spending. Even a later AI shortfall would not reveal the July traders’ motive: attributing the trades to institutional skepticism would require a verified institutional position and evidence linking it to that thesis. [4](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1301527221)

[ServiceNow to Acquire Task Mining Company UltimateSuite to Enhance Process Mining and Intelligent Automation on the Now Platform](https://web.archive.org/web/20250319091502/https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20231218270685/en/ServiceNow-to-Acquire-Task-Mining-Company-UltimateSuite-to-Enhance-Process-Mining-and-Intelligent-Automation-on-the-Now-Platform#:~:text=ServiceNow%E2%80%99s%20Latest%20Platform%20Release%20Adds%20to%20Thousands%20of%20AI,More%20for%20Faster%2C%20Smarter%20Workflows%20and%20Maximum%20Business%20Impact), available by 2025-03-19.

question: How do Vivek Ramaswamy's consistent share divestments throughout Q2 2025 impact the market valuation and investor sentiment for Roivant Sciences (ROIV) as the company approaches critical late-stage clinical catalysts for its lead asset, the TYK2/JAK1 inhibitor brepocitinib?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-08-05

**Research question**
How do Vivek Ramaswamy's consistent share divestments throughout Q2 2025 impact the market valuation and investor sentiment for Roivant Sciences (ROIV) as the company approaches critical late-stage clinical catalysts for its lead asset, the TYK2/JAK1 inhibitor brepocitinib?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-08-05, do not discount Roivant Sciences (ROIV) or lower brepocitinib’s probability of success on account of sales by Vivek Ramaswamy. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250723072607/https://newrepublic.com/article/170733/vivek-ramaswamy-business-china-roivant#:~:text=SEC%20filings%20from%20last%20March%20show%20Roivant%20has%20subsidiaries,reference%20the%20Chinese-domiciled%20Cytovant%20companies%20listed%20in%20earlier%20filings.) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1302334088)

## Evidence

Even a confirmed founder sale would establish a change in his exposure, not a change in investors’ estimate of clinical success. Ramaswamy had already left both the CEO and chair roles. Moreover, ROIV represents a portfolio, not just Priovant’s rights to brepocitinib. The available evidence includes neither a contemporaneous price-and-volume series nor investor estimates of the dermatomyositis trial’s odds, so it establishes neither selling pressure nor a deterioration in sentiment. [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1302334088) [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1280731494)

## What would change the view

Keep clinical assumptions unchanged pending the dermatomyositis readout or new trial-specific evidence. First verify any quarter sales against dated transaction disclosures and compare their size with normal ROIV trading volume. Weakness concentrated on sale dates that reverses as volume normalizes would favor temporary supply pressure. The strongest alternative is that investors marked down the trial’s odds: persistent underperformance versus biotech peers after selling ends, accompanied by explicit cuts to brepocitinib success estimates rather than news about other Roivant assets, would support that interpretation. A price decline alone would not. [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1280731494)

## Sources

1. [GOP Presidential Candidate Vivek Ramaswamy, Who Used to Do Business With China, Wants to Ban Business With China | The New Republic](https://web.archive.org/web/20250723072607/https://newrepublic.com/article/170733/vivek-ramaswamy-business-china-roivant#:~:text=SEC%20filings%20from%20last%20March%20show%20Roivant%20has%20subsidiaries,reference%20the%20Chinese-domiciled%20Cytovant%20companies%20listed%20in%20earlier%20filings.), available by 2025-07-23.

question: How does Netflix’s reported interest in Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio assets, coupled with the high-cost rollout of Stranger Things Season 5, signal a shift in capital allocation strategy from organic content growth toward consolidation-led scaling in the face of streaming market maturity?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-11-10

**Research question**
How does Netflix’s reported interest in Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio assets, coupled with the high-cost rollout of Stranger Things Season 5, signal a shift in capital allocation strategy from organic content growth toward consolidation-led scaling in the face of streaming market maturity?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-11-10, Netflix was exploring a studio-scale acquisition while rolling out the final season of Stranger Things. That signals a willingness to buy an existing library and production business rather than build every franchise title by title. It does not establish that Netflix submitted a bid for Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD), committed a purchase price, or diverted money from originals. The change was in what Netflix was prepared to consider, not a demonstrated change in what it funded. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20251031135212/https://variety.com/2025/digital/news/netflix-actively-exploring-warner-bros-discovery-acquisition-hires-bank-1236566752/#:~:text=Could%20Netflix%20become%20the%20future%20home%20of%20the%20DC,Liam%20Hemsworth%20Takes%20Over%20From%20Henry%20Cavill%3A%20TV%20Review) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1320914868) [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1321498762)

## Evidence

The reported diligence was more than casual interest but less than an offer. Reuters reporting described Netflix hiring Moelis and gaining access to WBD’s financials. Reports pointed to the studios and possibly streaming; whether HBO Max would be included remained unclear. WBD itself confirmed unsolicited interest from multiple parties, not a Netflix bid. The reported bids for the whole company came from Paramount Skydance, not Netflix. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20251031135212/https://variety.com/2025/digital/news/netflix-actively-exploring-warner-bros-discovery-acquisition-hires-bank-1236566752/#:~:text=Could%20Netflix%20become%20the%20future%20home%20of%20the%20DC,Liam%20Hemsworth%20Takes%20Over%20From%20Henry%20Cavill%3A%20TV%20Review) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20251031135212/https://variety.com/2025/digital/news/netflix-actively-exploring-warner-bros-discovery-acquisition-hires-bank-1236566752/#:~:text=Warner%20Bros.%20Discovery%E2%80%99s%20board%20last%20week%20announced%20that%20it,did%20not%20immediately%20respond%20to%20requests%20for%20comment%20Friday.) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20251027195610/https://www.wbd.com/news/warner-bros-discovery-initiates-review-potential-alternatives-maximize-shareholder-value#:~:text=While%20Warner%20Bros.%20Discovery%20%28the%20%22Company%22%29%20%28NASDAQ%3A%20WBD%29%20continues,Bros.%20and%20spin-off%20of%20Discovery%20Global%20to%20our%20shareholders.) [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20251031135212/https://variety.com/2025/digital/news/netflix-actively-exploring-warner-bros-discovery-acquisition-hires-bank-1236566752/#:~:text=Netflix%E2%80%99s%20reported%20active%20interest%20in%20buying%20perhaps%20some%20of,maybe%20some%20of%20the%20public%20commentary%20that%E2%80%99s%20out%20there.%E2%80%9D)

Stranger Things shows Netflix following through on an original, not how its next production dollar would be spent. The season was planned well before the WBD review, premiered on November 6, 2025, and was scheduled for a staggered streaming release. That schedule gives viewers reasons to return across release dates. [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1321498762)

## Outlook

The base case is continued investment in originals with acquisitions considered selectively. If subscriber growth becomes harder, owning established franchises such as Harry Potter and a studio that already makes shows for Netflix could help retain viewers without waiting for the next original hit. That is a rationale for exploring a purchase, not proof that streaming maturity prompted it or that buying would outperform commissioning. The base case predicts continued original commissions without a corresponding cut to finance a studio deal. [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1320914868) [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20251031135212/https://variety.com/2025/digital/news/netflix-actively-exploring-warner-bros-discovery-acquisition-hires-bank-1236566752/#:~:text=Could%20Netflix%20become%20the%20future%20home%20of%20the%20DC,Liam%20Hemsworth%20Takes%20Over%20From%20Henry%20Cavill%3A%20TV%20Review) [7](https://web.archive.org/web/20251031135212/https://variety.com/2025/digital/news/netflix-actively-exploring-warner-bros-discovery-acquisition-hires-bank-1236566752/#:~:text=Box-office%20hits%20in%202025%20for%20Warner%20Bros.%E2%80%99s%20film%20studios%2C,WB%20Television%20include%20%E2%80%9CAbbott%20Elementary%2C%E2%80%9D%20%E2%80%9CShrinking%E2%80%9D%20and%20%E2%80%9CThe%20Voice.%E2%80%9D)

## What would change the view

The strongest alternative is that Netflix was finishing an expensive-to-abandon existing slate while preparing to prioritize acquisitions over new commissions. A submitted offer would distinguish bidding from diligence; a signed purchase agreement would establish a commitment. Neither alone would show that originals paid for the deal. The decisive signal would be Netflix explicitly linking a reduction in planned original-production spending to acquisition funding. [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1321498762) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20251031135212/https://variety.com/2025/digital/news/netflix-actively-exploring-warner-bros-discovery-acquisition-hires-bank-1236566752/#:~:text=Warner%20Bros.%20Discovery%E2%80%99s%20board%20last%20week%20announced%20that%20it,did%20not%20immediately%20respond%20to%20requests%20for%20comment%20Friday.) [8](https://web.archive.org/web/20251027195610/https://www.wbd.com/news/warner-bros-discovery-initiates-review-potential-alternatives-maximize-shareholder-value#:~:text=%22Our%20decision%20to%20initiate%20this%20review%20underscores%20the%20Board%27s,or%20otherwise%20determines%20further%20disclosure%20is%20appropriate%20or%20necessary.)

question: Given Chardan Capital's successive price target reductions for CRISPR Therapeutics and their 2026 loss projections, how is the 60/40 profit-sharing agreement with Vertex Pharmaceuticals for Casgevy influencing CRISPR's valuation and its ability to achieve self-sustained profitability following the therapy's initial commercial rollout?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-05-11

**Research question**
Given Chardan Capital's successive price target reductions for CRISPR Therapeutics and their 2026 loss projections, how is the 60/40 profit-sharing agreement with Vertex Pharmaceuticals for Casgevy influencing CRISPR's valuation and its ability to achieve self-sustained profitability following the therapy's initial commercial rollout?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-05-11, Chardan’s documented move was a cut in CRISPR Therapeutics’ price target from $84 to $82, with its Buy rating intact. Vertex’s 60/40 split limits what Casgevy can contribute to CRISPR, but it predates the cut: it explains why Casgevy sales are worth less to CRISPR than sales of a wholly owned drug, not why Chardan changed its target. Neither a slower rollout nor a change in pipeline valuation is established as the cause. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250508203114/https://www.benzinga.com/general/biotech/25/05/45263363/crispr-therapeutics-data-provides-promising-balance-rfk-jr-appointee#:~:text=The%20company%20plans%20to%20present%20the%20CTX310%20Phase%201,more%20detailed%20data%20in%202H25%20will%20help%20understand%20competitiveness.%E2%80%9D) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250118013844/https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20231115290500/en/%C2%A0Vertex-and-CRISPR-Therapeutics-Announce-Authorization-of-the-First-CRISPRCas9-Gene-Edited-Therapy-CASGEVY%E2%84%A2-exagamglogene-autotemcel-by-the-United-Kingdom-MHRA-for-the-Treatment-of-Sickle-Cell-Disease-and-Transfusion-Dependent-Beta-Thalassemia#:~:text=About%20the%20Vertex%20and%20CRISPR%20Collaboration%20Vertex%20and%20CRISPR,neuropathic%20pain%2C%20type%201%20diabetes%20and%20alpha-1%20antitrypsin%20deficiency.)

## Evidence

CRISPR receives the smaller share of worldwide program profit, not a royalty on sales. Its share can cover its own expenses only when the profit left after shared program costs is large enough that CRISPR’s portion covers its remaining research and corporate expenses, without counting the shared costs twice. While the program is loss-making, CRISPR bears its share of costs rather than collecting a positive contribution. Neither the program margin nor CRISPR’s remaining expense base is quantified here, so there is no supported sales threshold or break-even date. [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250118013844/https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20231115290500/en/%C2%A0Vertex-and-CRISPR-Therapeutics-Announce-Authorization-of-the-First-CRISPRCas9-Gene-Edited-Therapy-CASGEVY%E2%84%A2-exagamglogene-autotemcel-by-the-United-Kingdom-MHRA-for-the-Treatment-of-Sickle-Cell-Disease-and-Transfusion-Dependent-Beta-Thalassemia#:~:text=About%20the%20Vertex%20and%20CRISPR%20Collaboration%20Vertex%20and%20CRISPR,neuropathic%20pain%2C%20type%201%20diabetes%20and%20alpha-1%20antitrypsin%20deficiency.) [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1275310986)

## Outlook

The base case is that access is expanding ahead of demonstrated earnings, not that demand has missed forecast. Through May 1st, Vertex reported more than 65 active treatment centers and approximately 90 patients with a first collection since launch. Collections are not paid infusions, and a cumulative count cannot show a slowdown relative to Chardan’s prior forecast. Vertex’s revenue guidance assumes continued Casgevy uptake but covers several products; it is not a Casgevy sales forecast. Growth in paid infusions followed by a sustained positive collaboration contribution would strengthen the case for eventual expense coverage. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250507105206/https://investors.vrtx.com/news-releases/news-release-details/vertex-reports-first-quarter-2025-financial-results#:~:text=CASGEVY%20for%20the%20treatment%20of%20sickle%20cell%20disease%20%28SCD%29,approximately%2090%20patients%20have%20had%20their%20first%20cell%20collection.) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250507105206/https://investors.vrtx.com/news-releases/news-release-details/vertex-reports-first-quarter-2025-financial-results#:~:text=Full%20Year%202025%20Financial%20Guidance%20Vertex%20today%20raised%20the,rates%20and%20regulations.%20Vertex%E2%80%99s%20financial%20guidance%20is%20summarized%20below%3A)

## What would change the view

The strongest alternative to a rollout-driven cut is a more cautious valuation of CRISPR’s cardiovascular pipeline. Chardan highlighted early activity but reserved judgment on competitiveness until fuller data, and the accompanying report raised a possible regulatory concern. Those comments identify risks, not changes to a valuation model. A comparison of Chardan’s forecasts before and after the cut would distinguish the explanations: later expected paid infusions or lower program margins would implicate Casgevy; unchanged Casgevy forecasts alongside a lower probability of pipeline success would point elsewhere. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250508203114/https://www.benzinga.com/general/biotech/25/05/45263363/crispr-therapeutics-data-provides-promising-balance-rfk-jr-appointee#:~:text=The%20company%20plans%20to%20present%20the%20CTX310%20Phase%201,more%20detailed%20data%20in%202H25%20will%20help%20understand%20competitiveness.%E2%80%9D) [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20250508203114/https://www.benzinga.com/general/biotech/25/05/45263363/crispr-therapeutics-data-provides-promising-balance-rfk-jr-appointee#:~:text=Prasad%27s%20social%20media%20reveals%20criticism%20of%20Verve%27s%201st-gen%20PCSK9,trial%20now.%20Stock%20Score%20Locked%3A%20Want%20to%20See%20it%3F)

question: Given the 2.5% decline in utility output reported by the Federal Reserve in early 2025, how is the subsequent surge in AI-related energy demand impacting the growth projections and valuation premiums for utility operators like NRG Energy and Entergy compared to the benchmark VPU ETF?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-04-23

**Research question**
Given the 2.5% decline in utility output reported by the Federal Reserve in early 2025, how is the subsequent surge in AI-related energy demand impacting the growth projections and valuation premiums for utility operators like NRG Energy and Entergy compared to the benchmark VPU ETF?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Answer

As of 2025-04-23, the evidence does not warrant paying a higher forward P/E for either NRG Energy or Entergy than for VPU on the strength of expected AI data-center load alone. NRG has a stated demand thesis; Entergy has a route to earnings through investment in power plants. Neither has a quantified AI-driven increase in expected earnings in the supplied record, and the record does not establish whether either stock actually traded at a premium to VPU that day. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250311100749/https://seekingalpha.com/article/4766373-nrg-energy-attractively-priced-as-demand-ratchets-up#:~:text=NRG%20Energy%20has%20pulled%20back%20~15%25%20since%20my%20last,performance%2C%20and%20aggressive%20capital%20returns%20bolster%20the%20investment%20thesis.) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1279009081)

## Evidence

For NRG, the March commentary reported a 12.1% historical EPS compound annual growth rate, not a forecast. It also reported reaffirmed 2025 guidance, not an AI-related increase. Reaffirmation does not rule out demand already embedded in guidance, but it does not quantify that contribution. The cited discount was to peers such as Vistra in March, not to VPU on 2025-04-23; neither NRG’s prospective growth advantage nor its relative forward P/E is established. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250311100749/https://seekingalpha.com/article/4766373-nrg-energy-attractively-priced-as-demand-ratchets-up#:~:text=NRG%20trades%20at%20a%20discount%20to%20peers%20like%20Vistra%2C,respectively%20while%20offering%20an%20This%20article%20was%20written%20by) [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250311100749/https://seekingalpha.com/article/4766373-nrg-energy-attractively-priced-as-demand-ratchets-up#:~:text=NRG%20Energy%20has%20pulled%20back%20~15%25%20since%20my%20last,performance%2C%20and%20aggressive%20capital%20returns%20bolster%20the%20investment%20thesis.)

For Entergy, serving new load could support earnings if regulators allow the company to recover its investment and earn a return. That is different from treating every additional unit of power sold as profit. The available commission excerpt identifies no project approval or cost-recovery terms. There is also no comparable forecast of Entergy and VPU earnings growth or same-date forward P/E for either, so the size and even the sign of Entergy’s valuation spread remain unknown. [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1279009081) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250423072448/https://lpscpubvalence.lpsc.louisiana.gov/portal/PSC/DocketDetails?docketId=32146#:~:text=Date%20FiledTypeDescription)

## What would change the view

The base case assigns no separate AI premium. The strongest alternative is that durable data-center commitments produce faster per-share earnings growth than VPU’s holdings can deliver. For NRG, look for signed supply contracts with disclosed margins that raise EPS forecasts beyond the effects of Vivint and capital returns. For Entergy, look for a regulatory order specifying recoverable costs, allowed returns and timing. Then compare each operator’s expected EPS growth with VPU’s over the same horizon and its forward P/E with VPU’s on the same date: a growth advantage matters only if the price leaves room for it. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250311100749/https://seekingalpha.com/article/4766373-nrg-energy-attractively-priced-as-demand-ratchets-up#:~:text=NRG%20Energy%20has%20pulled%20back%20~15%25%20since%20my%20last,performance%2C%20and%20aggressive%20capital%20returns%20bolster%20the%20investment%20thesis.) [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1279009081)

## Sources

1. [NRG Energy: Attractively Priced As Demand Ratchets Up (NYSE:NRG) | Seeking Alpha](https://web.archive.org/web/20250311100749/https://seekingalpha.com/article/4766373-nrg-energy-attractively-priced-as-demand-ratchets-up#:~:text=NRG%20Energy%20has%20pulled%20back%20~15%25%20since%20my%20last,performance%2C%20and%20aggressive%20capital%20returns%20bolster%20the%20investment%20thesis.), available by 2025-03-11.
2. [Entergy](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1279009081), available by 2025-03-05.
3. [NRG Energy: Attractively Priced As Demand Ratchets Up (NYSE:NRG) | Seeking Alpha](https://web.archive.org/web/20250311100749/https://seekingalpha.com/article/4766373-nrg-energy-attractively-priced-as-demand-ratchets-up#:~:text=NRG%20trades%20at%20a%20discount%20to%20peers%20like%20Vistra%2C,respectively%20while%20offering%20an%20This%20article%20was%20written%20by), available by 2025-03-11.

question: Given the Q2 2025 upward revision of Skyrizi's sales guidance to $17.1 billion and the successful Phase 3 topline results for upadacitinib in alopecia areata, how effectively is AbbVie’s newer immunology portfolio positioning the company to offset Humira's revenue erosion through 2026?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-08-05

**Research question**
Given the Q2 2025 upward revision of Skyrizi's sales guidance to $17.1 billion and the successful Phase 3 topline results for upadacitinib in alopecia areata, how effectively is AbbVie’s newer immunology portfolio positioning the company to offset Humira's revenue erosion through 2026?

Some parts of the question could not be established from eligible evidence.

## Outlook

Use the last full fiscal year before U.S. biosimilar entry in January 2023 as the common baseline. For each of 2025 and 2026, the offset holds if the increase in combined annual global Skyrizi and Rinvoq net revenue equals or exceeds the decline in annual global Humira net revenue from that same baseline. The quarterly figures support the direction of the base case, but the evidence supplies neither the annual baseline sales nor a complete set of annual product forecasts to measure the surplus or shortfall. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250614084558/https://www.truveta.com/blog/research/research-insights/humira-and-biosimilars-2024/#:~:text=Market%20exclusively%20for%20Humira%20ended%20in%20January%202023%2C%20when,approved%20biosimilars%20before%20and%20after%20the%20CVS%20formulary%20change.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250731142530/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/abbvie-reports-second-quarter-2025-financial-results-302518052.html#:~:text=Delivers%20Second-Quarter%20Net%20Revenues%20of%20%2415.423%20Billion%2C%20an%20Increase,Global%20Ubrelvy%20and%20Qulipta%20Net%20Revenues%20Were%20%24605%20Million)

Assume no Rinvoq alopecia areata sales in 2026. The positive pivotal readout supports a possible future indication, not an approval or launch. There is a commercial basis for growth without it: Rinvoq already has approved uses across rheumatology, gastroenterology and dermatology, and Skyrizi is approved for ulcerative colitis. Full replacement is therefore plausible without alopecia sales, but no forecast for Rinvoq excluding that indication establishes that the combined gain clears the threshold. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250804145945/https://news.abbvie.com/2025-07-31-AbbVie-Reports-Second-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results#:~:text=Note%3A%20%22Operational%22%20comparisons%20are%20presented%20at%20constant%20currency%20rates,no%20new%20safety%20signals%20were%20identified%20in%20this%20study.) question: Given Disney's 2025 launch of ESPN’s $29.99/month direct-to-consumer platform and recent carriage disputes, how will this high-ARPU pricing strategy and the search for strategic partners impact the sports segment’s operating margins and Disney’s ability to offset terminal linear cable subscriber declines?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-08-05

**Research question**
Given Disney's 2025 launch of ESPN’s $29.99/month direct-to-consumer platform and recent carriage disputes, how will this high-ARPU pricing strategy and the search for strategic partners impact the sports segment’s operating margins and Disney’s ability to offset terminal linear cable subscriber declines?

## Answer

Forecast ESPN’s $29.99 monthly flagship tier to slow the decline in Disney’s Sports operating margin, not stabilize it, during the launch period. As of 2025-08-05, ESPN had announced a fall launch, not reported a paying flagship subscriber base. The relevant scale is the number of sustained, incremental paid households per lost ESPN cable household: the premium price helps only to the extent Disney retains it, and a distributor can offer access without collecting another retail subscription. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1304268280) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250430141147/https://www.mediapost.com/publications/article/399322/directv-disney-ends-blackout-new-carriage-deal-in.html#:~:text=For%20DirecTV%2C%20it%20also%20includes%20the%20ability%20to%20package,Totaled%3A%204%25%20Rise%20In%20Prime-Time%2C%20CBS%20Set%20To%20Lead)

## Evidence

The flagship is a closer substitute for cable ESPN than the existing ESPN+ service: it combines ESPN’s main channels with ESPN+ content. That gives a cord-cutter a reason to pay a premium, but also gives a cable household a reason to leave. Existing ESPN+ subscribers were slated to move automatically to Select, not to become new full-price flagship customers. For an upgrade, count only the contribution above what Disney already earned. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1304268280) [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1304201846)

The verified partners are distributors. The DirecTV settlement ended a two-week impasse and granted flagship distribution rights; Spectrum’s earlier agreement also covered the future flagship. These deals can protect affiliate income by making the TV package worth keeping. But more flexible packages can also reduce ESPN’s paid reach, and an included activation is not a retail sale. No additional charge to the viewer does not establish what the distributor pays Disney. [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250430141147/https://www.mediapost.com/publications/article/399322/directv-disney-ends-blackout-new-carriage-deal-in.html#:~:text=by%20Wayne%20Friedman%20%2C%20September%2015%2C%202024%20DirecTV-Walt%20Disney,new-season%20NFL%20and%20college%20football%20games%20were%20blacked%20out.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250430141147/https://www.mediapost.com/publications/article/399322/directv-disney-ends-blackout-new-carriage-deal-in.html#:~:text=For%20DirecTV%2C%20it%20also%20includes%20the%20ability%20to%20package,Totaled%3A%204%25%20Rise%20In%20Prime-Time%2C%20CBS%20Set%20To%20Lead) [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1304201846) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250430141147/https://www.mediapost.com/publications/article/399322/directv-disney-ends-blackout-new-carriage-deal-in.html#:~:text=If%20those%20levels%20are%20not%20reached%2C%20pay-TV%20services%20need,kids%20and%20family%2C%20and%20more%20in%20the%20new%20year.%E2%80%9D)

Do not give the forecast an equity-partner benefit on the strength of a carriage deal. The separate Venu venture with Fox and TNT was cancelled. The available evidence does not verify a completed flagship equity investment or a contractual partner take rate by the cutoff. A strategic partner would help Sports margins if its distribution lowered acquisition costs or brought enough additional paying homes to outweigh any revenue share and incremental rights expense. An ownership stake alone would not establish that trade-off. [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1304268280) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250430141147/https://www.mediapost.com/publications/article/399322/directv-disney-ends-blackout-new-carriage-deal-in.html#:~:text=For%20DirecTV%2C%20it%20also%20includes%20the%20ability%20to%20package,Totaled%3A%204%25%20Rise%20In%20Prime-Time%2C%20CBS%20Set%20To%20Lead)

## Outlook

Estimate the replacement hurdle in average monthly paying households: multiply lost cable households by monthly contribution lost per household (affiliate fees plus lost ad contribution, less avoidable costs), then divide by monthly contribution per incremental paying flagship home. For that denominator, start with the amount allocated to Sports after bundle discounts, deduct any distribution share, add incremental ad contribution and subtract streaming, servicing and acquisition costs spread over paid months. Holding ads and other inputs fixed, each deduction raises the hurdle relative to using sticker price. Disney needs fewer paying homes than it loses on cable only if the net contribution per paying home is higher. The sources identify per-subscriber cable fees but disclose neither current lost contribution nor realized streaming economics; a numerical household count is not supportable. [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20110828123342/http://corporate.disney.go.com/investors/annual_reports/2004/pdfs/annual.pdf#:~:text=Family%20due%20to%20higher%20ratings.%20Revenues%20from%20cable%20and,of%20%24147%20million%20at%20the%20ABC%20Television%20Production%20and) [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1304268280) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250430141147/https://www.mediapost.com/publications/article/399322/directv-disney-ends-blackout-new-carriage-deal-in.html#:~:text=For%20DirecTV%2C%20it%20also%20includes%20the%20ability%20to%20package,Totaled%3A%204%25%20Rise%20In%20Prime-Time%2C%20CBS%20Set%20To%20Lead)

## What would change the view

The strongest alternative is that distributors retain cable homes while ESPN sells directly to sports fans who would otherwise pay Disney nothing. Test that case with retained paid household-months, Sports revenue per home after bundle allocation, and contribution after partner and streaming costs—not app activations. Replacing lost cable contribution preserves operating income before new fixed costs; it does not necessarily preserve the margin on a different revenue base. Upgrade to stabilization when the change in Sports operating income after rights and launch costs meets or exceeds the prior Sports margin times the change in Sports revenue. Disney’s historical cable results show why the distinction matters: higher revenue did not prevent programming costs from eroding profit. [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250430141147/https://www.mediapost.com/publications/article/399322/directv-disney-ends-blackout-new-carriage-deal-in.html#:~:text=For%20DirecTV%2C%20it%20also%20includes%20the%20ability%20to%20package,Totaled%3A%204%25%20Rise%20In%20Prime-Time%2C%20CBS%20Set%20To%20Lead) [7](https://web.archive.org/web/20100107083229/http://corporate.disney.go.com:80/investors/annual_reports/2002/pdfs/ar_2002.pdf#:~:text=54%20Media%20Ne%20two%20r%20k%20s%20The%20following,ABC%20Family%20operations%20in%20the%20current%20period%20and%20losses)

question: How will the decelerating Chinese macroeconomic indicators reported by the NBS throughout Q3 2025, coupled with the sharp decline in U.S. soybean procurement following diplomatic friction, influence China's agricultural import strategy and the risk profile for global soybean futures through year-end?
report:
# Investment research memo

As of 2025-09-29

**Research question**
How will the decelerating Chinese macroeconomic indicators reported by the NBS throughout Q3 2025, coupled with the sharp decline in U.S. soybean procurement following diplomatic friction, influence China's agricultural import strategy and the risk profile for global soybean futures through year-end?

## Answer

As of 2025-09-29, keep expected Chinese soybean imports broadly intact through December, but shift expected autumn purchases from U.S. exporters chiefly to Brazil. By mid-August, Chinese importers had booked around 8 million metric tons for September shipment, all from South America, and had already secured about 4 million tons there for October. That is evidence of a lost U.S. sales window, not an equivalent loss of world demand. The higher-conviction call is on relative export prices, not an outright decline in Chicago futures. [1](https://web.archive.org/web/20250813120024/https://www.agriculture.com/partners-u-s-losing-out-on-china-soybean-sales-as-brazil-fills-key-supply-period-11789980#:~:text=By%20Naveen%20Thukral%20and%20Ella%20Cao%20SINGAPORE%2FBEIJING%2C%20Aug.%2013,tons%2C%20all%20from%20South%20America%2C%20three%20traders%20told%20Reuters.) [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250813120024/https://www.agriculture.com/partners-u-s-losing-out-on-china-soybean-sales-as-brazil-fills-key-supply-period-11789980#:~:text=For%20October%2C%20Chinese%20buyers%20have%20secured%20about%204%20million,said%20Wang%20Wenshen%2C%20an%20analyst%20at%20Sublime%20China%20Information.)

## Evidence

The NBS evidence does not establish a quarter-long deceleration in soybean demand. July industrial producer prices fell 3.6 percent year on year, but factory-gate prices were flat month on month in August; cumulative retail sales rose 4.6 percent through August. Annual price weakness and monthly stabilization can coexist. Neither industrial prices nor nominal retail spending measures feed use or crusher throughput, and the available releases do not cover September activity. [3](https://web.archive.org/web/20250906105741/https://www.stats.gov.cn/english/PressRelease/202508/t20250815_1960785.html#:~:text=In%20July%2C%20the%20producer%20prices%20for%20industrial%20products%20went,nominal%20growth%20by%20using%20current%20prices%20unless%20otherwise%20specified.) [4](https://web.archive.org/web/20250917175238/https://english.www.gov.cn/archive/statistics/202509/15/content_WS68c804bec6d00fa19f7a2781.html#:~:text=%22The%20slight%20increase%20was%20due%20to%20the%20graduation%20season%2C%22,processing%20prices%20rising%202.8%20percent%20and%201.9%20percent%2C%20respectively.) [5](https://web.archive.org/web/20250917175238/https://english.www.gov.cn/archive/statistics/202509/15/content_WS68c804bec6d00fa19f7a2781.html#:~:text=BEIJING%2C%20Sept.%2015%20--%20China%27s%20economy%20maintained%20its%20steady,by%205.1%20percent%20--%20faster%20than%20that%20of%20goods.)

## Outlook

Export basis—the cash export price relative to comparable futures—is where the origin switch should show most clearly. Chinese buying supports Brazilian premiums while U.S. sellers may need to cut theirs to attract other buyers. Traders put October U.S. cargoes around $40 per ton below Brazilian cargoes before tariffs, yet China was buying Brazilian beans. That comparison illustrates the importance of trade policy; it is neither a tariff-inclusive landed-price comparison nor a measured basis spread. [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20250813120024/https://www.agriculture.com/partners-u-s-losing-out-on-china-soybean-sales-as-brazil-fills-key-supply-period-11789980#:~:text=%22One%20possible%20scenario%20is%20that%20if%20both%20sides%20reach,imports%20with%20purchases%20hitting%20record%20highs%20in%20recent%20months.) [7](https://web.archive.org/web/20250912184439/https://www.reuters.com/world/china/us-losing-out-china-soybean-sales-brazil-fills-key-supply-period-2025-08-13/#:~:text=Chinese%20crushers%20buy%20Brazilian%20beans%20amid%20US-China%20trade%20war,soybeans%20around%20%2440%2Fton%20cheaper%20than%20Brazilian%20for%20October%20shipment)

CBOT November faces the more immediate downside: U.S. harvest supplies reach the market just as South American bookings displace customary U.S. export demand. But cargoes already booked are not a fresh bearish surprise, and cheaper U.S. beans can find other buyers. With Chicago already reported near multiyear lows, further downside depends more on continued weak U.S. sales than on the September origin mix alone. [8](https://web.archive.org/web/20250813120024/https://www.agriculture.com/partners-u-s-losing-out-on-china-soybean-sales-as-brazil-fills-key-supply-period-11789980#:~:text=Last%20year%2C%20Chinese%20oilseed%20importers%20bought%20around%207%20million,before%20Brazilian%20supplies%20take%20over%20after%20South%20America%27s%20harvest.) [7](https://web.archive.org/web/20250912184439/https://www.reuters.com/world/china/us-losing-out-china-soybean-sales-brazil-fills-key-supply-period-2025-08-13/#:~:text=Chinese%20crushers%20buy%20Brazilian%20beans%20amid%20US-China%20trade%20war,soybeans%20around%20%2440%2Fton%20cheaper%20than%20Brazilian%20for%20October%20shipment) [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20250813120024/https://www.agriculture.com/partners-u-s-losing-out-on-china-soybean-sales-as-brazil-fills-key-supply-period-11789980#:~:text=%22One%20possible%20scenario%20is%20that%20if%20both%20sides%20reach,imports%20with%20purchases%20hitting%20record%20highs%20in%20recent%20months.)

CBOT January has a more two-sided risk through year-end. If China stays away until Brazil's next harvest approaches, unsold U.S. supplies can weigh on January even after November expires. Conversely, tariff relief followed by confirmed Chinese bookings for winter U.S. shipment could lift January futures and U.S. basis while eroding Brazil's premium. That rally would not require higher Chinese consumption: buyers switching back would suffice. A November deal was a trader's scenario, not a commitment. [8](https://web.archive.org/web/20250813120024/https://www.agriculture.com/partners-u-s-losing-out-on-china-soybean-sales-as-brazil-fills-key-supply-period-11789980#:~:text=Last%20year%2C%20Chinese%20oilseed%20importers%20bought%20around%207%20million,before%20Brazilian%20supplies%20take%20over%20after%20South%20America%27s%20harvest.) [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20250813120024/https://www.agriculture.com/partners-u-s-losing-out-on-china-soybean-sales-as-brazil-fills-key-supply-period-11789980#:~:text=%22One%20possible%20scenario%20is%20that%20if%20both%20sides%20reach,imports%20with%20purchases%20hitting%20record%20highs%20in%20recent%20months.)

## What would change the view

The strongest case for cutting total imports is that China bought early and can draw down stocks rather than replace every missing U.S. cargo. October was only partly covered in the August report; shipment bookings are not customs arrivals and do not establish December volumes. Trim the forecast if all-origin bookings and subsequent arrivals fall short of seasonal needs while crushers consume inventories or slow throughput. If total arrivals hold up and South America gains share, retain the volume forecast even if U.S. sales remain weak. [2](https://web.archive.org/web/20250813120024/https://www.agriculture.com/partners-u-s-losing-out-on-china-soybean-sales-as-brazil-fills-key-supply-period-11789980#:~:text=For%20October%2C%20Chinese%20buyers%20have%20secured%20about%204%20million,said%20Wang%20Wenshen%2C%20an%20analyst%20at%20Sublime%20China%20Information.) [6](https://web.archive.org/web/20250813120024/https://www.agriculture.com/partners-u-s-losing-out-on-china-soybean-sales-as-brazil-fills-key-supply-period-11789980#:~:text=%22One%20possible%20scenario%20is%20that%20if%20both%20sides%20reach,imports%20with%20purchases%20hitting%20record%20highs%20in%20recent%20months.)

## Sources
